fact_uses.text: [L1] The deformation to the normal cone gives the open flat deformation family $D_i\to\mathbb P^1$ with special fibre the normal cone and ordinary fibres the ambient scheme and a well-defined specialization operation on Chow groups, natural in the base ([[def-deformation-to-the-normal-cone-and-specialization]]).

proof_steps.claim: The cone embedding. Under a base change $T'\to T$ the ideal of $Z'$ is $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$ and its powers are generated by the images of the powers of $\mathcal I$, so the Rees algebra of $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$ is a quotient of the base change of the Rees algebra of $\mathcal I$; taking the symmetric algebra of the pulled-back conormal surjection and composing with the canonical map to the associated graded gives $\operatorname{Sym}(N'^\vee)\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}}\mathcal O_{T'}$, and hence a closed immersion $a:C_{Z'}T'\hookrightarrow N'$ of the normal cone over $Z'$ into the vector bundle. This holds for arbitrary, including nonflat, base change, since only surjectivity of the graded maps is used.

Bivariant axioms. For each base $T'$ the operation is $c(Z,T,N)_{T'}=s_{N'}^!\,a_*\sigma_{Z'/T'}$, a composite of the well-defined specialization $\sigma_{Z'/T'}:A_m(T')\to A_m(C_{Z'}T')$ of [L1], the proper pushforward $a_*$, and the bijection $s_{N'}^!=(p'^*)^{-1}$ of [L2]. Proper compatibility: push a lift of the pulled-back class forward along the given proper morphism and use that Cartier Gysin commutes with proper pushforward [L3]. Flat compatibility: pull the lift back and use flat/Cartier compatibility. Divisor compatibility: apply the Cartier Gysin to the lift and use that two Cartier Gysins commute [L3], noting that the ordinary restriction of the result is the lift of the desired input. Base restriction is simply the reindexing of the family. These verifications are exactly the three bivariant axioms of [L2].

Base change. Under a base change the blowup of $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$ admits a closed immersion into the base change of the original blowup, induced by the surjection of Rees algebras of step 1.1, and this immersion is an isomorphism over the ordinary part $\mathbb A^1_{T'}$; the induced proper morphism between the two deformation families is therefore an isomorphism over the ordinary fibres, and pushing a lift along it exhibits the two infinity operations as equal after pushforward. Consequently the cone portions of the two operations define the same class after pushforward to $N'$, and since proper pushforward, open restriction and $(p'^*)^{-1}$ are bivariant, the operation is compatible with arbitrary base change.

fact_uses.text: [L3] The deformation blowup $M$ is smooth and quasi-projective with strict transform $F$ isomorphic to $X\times\mathbb P^1$; it is flat over $\mathbb P^1$ with ordinary fibres $Y$; the open $M\setminus B$ has special fibre $C_XY$, while the complete fibre at infinity is the union $B+\mathbb P(N\oplus1)$ with intersection $\mathbb P(N)$ ([[def-deformation-to-the-normal-cone-and-specialization]], [[lem-smooth-immersion-normal-sequence-and-deformation-charts]]).

proof_steps.claim: The deformation blowup. By [L3], $M$ is smooth and quasi-projective over the field, so every coherent sheaf on $M$ has a finite locally free resolution by [L2]; the strict transform $F$ is isomorphic to $X\times\mathbb P^1$ and meets the fibre at infinity in the section $[0:1]$ of $P=\mathbb P(N\oplus1)$, while it is disjoint from $B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, since $B$ meets $P$ in $\mathbb P(N)$ and the strict transform of $X\times\mathbb P^1$ lies over $X\times\{\infty\}$ inside the exceptional component. On the chart where the infinity fibre is Cartier with equation $t$, the ordinary fibre $Y$ has equation $t-1$, and both act injectively on the coherent sheaf $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$, since on its support $F\cong X\times\mathbb P^1$ they are parameter equations on the second factor and $\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ is locally free there. This sheaf need not be locally free on $M$. Near its intersection with $P$ the component $B$ is absent, so the Cartier equation of $P$ agrees with that of the infinity fibre; step 1.2 therefore restricts a finite locally free resolution of $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ exactly to the ordinary fibre and to $P$, where the restricted complex resolves the restrictions of the sheaf. Near $B$ the sheaf is zero, and a bounded exact complex of vector bundles resolving the zero sheaf is split exact by induction on its length, starting from the last cokernel; hence the restriction of the resolution to $B$ is an exact complex, as asserted.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-adhm-fixed-point-instanton-count]]: the fixed points for $N=1,k=1$ are indexed by the one one-box partition, and their tangent character is computed from the ADHM deformation complex.

proof_steps.claim: There is exactly one partition of $k=1$ for $N=1$, namely $Y_1=\{(0,0)\}$, so [F2] gives the unique fixed point. Here $\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=e_1$ and $\mathbf W=e_1^{-1}$, whence $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf V=1$, $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf W^\vee=1$, and $t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V=t_1t_2$. Substitution in the tangent character gives $t_1+t_2$; the two additive weights are $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$, so the Euler class is $\epsilon_1\epsilon_2$.

The degree-one coefficient is the sum over the single fixed point, so it equals $(\epsilon_1\epsilon_2)^{-1}$. This is a formal equivariant fixed-point contribution, not an asserted continuum path-integral value.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-adhm-fixed-point-instanton-count]]: fixed points are indexed by two-tuples of partitions of total size one, and the tangent character is $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf V(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V$.

proof_steps.claim: A two-tuple of partitions with total size one places its single box in exactly one of the two colors, so the only possibilities are $(\{(0,0)\},\varnothing)$ and $(\varnothing,\{(0,0)\})$. Their quotient representatives have $V$-characters $e_1$ and $e_2$, respectively.

For the first point, the ADHM convention [F1] gives $\mathbf W=e_1^{-1}+e_2^{-1}$ and $\mathbf W^\vee=e_1+e_2$, while $\mathbf V=e_1$. Substitution in [F2] gives $$t_1+t_2+\frac{e_2}{e_1}+t_1t_2\frac{e_1}{e_2}.$$ The corresponding additive weights are $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_2-a_1,\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2+a_1-a_2$, so their product is $E_1$. Interchanging the two colors gives the second displayed character and $E_2$.

Each fixed-point contribution is the reciprocal of its Euler product, so the degree-one coefficient is $E_1^{-1}+E_2^{-1}$. The TikZ drawing only records the two one-box colorings and is not used in this calculation.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] Stable data yield the stated framed monad, and its sheaf is locally free exactly for costable data. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: At zero real level, $J=0$ still follows from $I\ne0$ and $IJ=0$, while the real equation becomes $|I|^2=0$. This contradicts $I\ne0$, so the stable zero-level locus is empty. In the positive chamber, $J=0$ makes all of $V$ a nonzero invariant subspace in $\ker J$; the data are not costable. By [F3], their framed sheaves are not locally free.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] The ADHM-to-monad construction uses source $V\mathcal O(-1)$, middle $(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O$, target $V\mathcal O(1)$, and the displayed Hilbert polynomial. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Substituting $V=0$ into the monad leaves $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its kernel at the right is $W\mathcal O$ and the image at the left is zero, so the middle cohomology is canonically $W\mathcal O$. Restriction to $L_\infty$ is the identity framing on the prescribed basis of $W$. Since $\chi(\mathcal O(m))=\binom{m+2}{2}$, its Hilbert polynomial is $N\binom{m+2}{2}$, the case $k=0$ of [F2]. No Euler-block or empty-matrix convention changes these calculations.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] For a stable complex datum the framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad has maps $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0B_2+z_2,z_0B_1-z_1,z_0I)$, and its middle cohomology is a framed torsion-free sheaf; local freeness is equivalent to costability. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Substituting that representative in [F3] gives $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ and $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,z_0)$. Their product is $-z_2z_1+z_1z_2=0$. The row $\beta$ is surjective at every projective point because its three entries have no common zero, and $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map because it is nonzero away from $p$. Let $K=\ker\beta$. Projection to the third coordinate restricts to a morphism $\gamma:K\to\mathcal O$. On the affine chart $z_0=1$, put $x=z_1$ and $y=z_2$; a vector in $K$ has the form $(u,v,-yu+xv)$, so $\gamma(K)=(x,y)$ and its kernel is generated by $(-x,-y,0)$, the image of $\alpha$. On any chart away from $p$ where $z_1$ or $z_2$ is a unit, the same equations show that $\gamma$ is onto and its kernel is generated by $\alpha$. Hence $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha\cong I_p$ globally, where $I_p$ is the ideal sheaf of $p$.

At $p$, the local ideal $(x,y)$ is not principal: if it were generated by one element in the regular local ring $\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x,y)}$, its quotient by the maximal ideal would have dimension at most one, whereas $(x,y)/(x,y)^2$ has dimension two. Therefore $I_p$ is not locally free at $p$. Its framing on $L_\infty$ is the canonical trivialization because $p\notin L_\infty$. This exhibits a positive-FI stable point outside the costable, locally-free zero-FI locus; the correspondence with ordinary ASD moduli is restricted to that zero-FI locus and does not absorb this boundary point.

final_edge_fact_uses.text:
[F3] The finite monad resolution gives
$c_2(F)=kH^2$; the charge on $S^4$ is conditional on the stated pullback.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-charge-normalization]]

proof_steps.claim:
The residual $U(1)$ action sends
$I\mapsto gI$ and $J\mapsto Jg^{-1}$; it preserves the raw representative's
orbit, and its stabilizer is trivial because $gI=I$ with $I\ne0$ forces
$g=1$. The framed $W$ coordinates at infinity are fixed, so they introduce
no extra unitary factor. The finite monad resolution and [F3] give
$c_2(F)=H^2$, the unit charge under the positive incidence pullback
condition. The example verifies an exact one-instanton block with no
singularity because $f_z$ never vanishes.

final_edge_fact_uses.text:
[F2] The finite monad resolution has
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N-kH^2$, $c_2(F)=kH^2$, and
$\chi(F)=N-2k$; the topological charge statement is conditional on a

[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-charge-normalization]]

proof_steps.claim:
Setting $k=0$ in [F2] gives
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N$, $c_2(F)=0$, and $\chi(F)=N$. Directly,
$F=W\otimes\mathcal O$ has these same classes; if it is written as

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] The preceding vanishing lemma reconstructs a three-term monad with dimensions $k,2k+N,k$ from the Ward bundle. [[lem-qftx-asd-twistor-vanishing-and-monad-reconstruction]]

proof_steps.claim: The reconstructed monad in [F1] is linear with locally free middle bundle, trivial on every real line, and has the positive Hermitian Ward pairing and unitary framing fixed in the definition. Its dimensions are those required by [A1]. Thus, assuming the exact supplier [A1], extract the raw tuple from its intrinsic normal form. Its monad composition vanishes, so [F5]'s polynomial identity makes both raw moment coefficients zero. Full fiber rank on each real line and [F5]'s Gram/rank equivalence identify the locus exactly with stable-and-costable regularity. The intrinsic unitary normalization and inverse-extraction clause in [A1] identify the remaining framed monad changes precisely with $(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ for $g\in U(k)$. The compact-rotation and framing chain maps are exactly those in [F5] and [A1]; first-order naturality is used only in [A1]’s locally-free/base-change range. No arbitrary analytic-family algebraization is inferred. No source-coordinate conjugation or nonexistent universal equivalence is invoked.

Conversely, the regular raw monad in [F5] is a global holomorphic bundle, trivial on every real line, with canonical positive reality: its pairing is induced by the standard Hermitian form on K and β(v)=α(σv)*. It is well-defined on cohomology since kerβ(v) is orthogonal to imα(σv), and on a real line its canonical representatives are kerD with the positive restricted metric; at infinity it is W. Apply the proved local Ward construction to obtain a global framed unitary ASD connection. On the finite chart it equals P d: for a kernel representative v along a D=ker(de) direction, β is constant, so its derivative lies in kerβ; the component of dv orthogonal to kerD lies in im a⊕im b, and β=f(−λ₂,λ₁) forces that component to lie in im(aλ₁+bλ₂)=imα. It therefore vanishes in monad cohomology, leaving exactly P dv. Thus evaluation identifies the projection and Ward connections; the Ward construction supplies the smooth extension and framing at infinity. The normalization of [F3] with determinant reduction [F4] gives k=c₂(E)[S⁴]=−q_N. Under [A1], extraction and construction are inverse on U(k) orbits and framed Ward connections, proving the full claim under the exact normal-form, GAGA and coupled-vanishing hypotheses stated above.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] The standard projective diagonal has the Koszul resolution $0\to\mathcal O(-3)\boxtimes\Omega^3(3)\to\mathcal O(-2)\boxtimes\Omega^2(2)\to\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes\Omega^1(1)\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\Delta\to0,$ because the diagonal is a regular embedding of codimension three and its three local coordinate differences form a regular sequence. [[lem-koszul-resolution-and-flat-fibre-restriction]]

proof_steps.claim: Apply [F4] to the diagonal Koszul resolution [F3], tensoring the second factor by $\mathcal E(-2)$, pushing to the first factor, and twisting that output factor by $\mathcal O(2)$. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Z,\mathcal E(-2)\otimes\Omega_Z^{-p}(-p))\otimes\mathcal O_Z(p+2)$ for $p=-3,-2,-1,0$. Steps 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 and Serre duality make every term in rows $q=0,1,3$ vanish except possibly $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)$ at $(-2,1)$. No differential can enter this term; its only possible outgoing $d_2$ lands in $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. It therefore survives to $E_\infty$, but the diagonal construction resolves $\mathcal E(-2)$ before the output twist and $\mathcal E$ after that twist; it is concentrated in degree zero and has no degree $-1$ hypercohomology. Since $(-2)+1=-1$, the term is zero. Thus the remaining spectral-sequence row is $q=2$.

The row $q=2$ gives the complex $H^2(\mathcal E(-3))\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)\otimes\mathcal O\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))\otimes\mathcal O(1)$. All higher differentials vanish because all other rows are zero. Its only cohomology is the degree-zero hypercohomology of the diagonal resolution, namely $\mathcal E$; the first and last terms are exact because the other total degrees vanish. The maps are linear in the homogeneous output coordinates, since each Koszul differential is contraction with the universal linear section. Thus this is the stated monad; its cohomology vector spaces are canonical, and changing bases acts by $GL(U)\times GL(K)\times GL(U')$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] The total Chern character is additive on exact complexes of vector bundles, $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal O(1))=e^H$, $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal O(-1))=e^{-H}$, and on $\mathbb CP^3$ all classes of degree greater than six vanish. [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]]

proof_steps.claim: In the Grothendieck group, exactness of the monad gives $[\mathcal E]=(2k+N)[\mathcal O]-k[\mathcal O(-1)]-k[\mathcal O(1)]$. By [F1], its Chern character is $(2k+N)-ke^{-H}-ke^H=N-kH^2$, because the constant terms cancel to $N$, the linear terms cancel, the quadratic contribution is $-kH^2$, and terms of degree at least four vanish on $Z$. Therefore $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$ and $c_2(\mathcal E)=-\operatorname{ch}_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F4] Chern classes are natural under pullback, the second Chern class of a bundle with $c_1=0$ is represented by $-\operatorname{ch}_2$, and Chern–Weil forms represent the corresponding real characteristic classes. [[thm-chern-weil-forms-represent-the-at-characteristic-classes-over-the-reals]], [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]]

proof_steps.claim: In the Grothendieck group, exactness of the monad gives $[\mathcal E]=(2k+N)[\mathcal O]-k[\mathcal O(-1)]-k[\mathcal O(1)]$. By [F1], its Chern character is $(2k+N)-ke^{-H}-ke^H=N-kH^2$, because the constant terms cancel to $N$, the linear terms cancel, the quadratic contribution is $-kH^2$, and terms of degree at least four vanish on $Z$. Therefore $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$ and $c_2(\mathcal E)=-\operatorname{ch}_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] The Koszul complex of a section whose zero scheme is a regular codimension-two subscheme resolves its structure sheaf, and exactness persists under the stated flat fiber restriction. [[lem-koszul-resolution-and-flat-fibre-restriction]]

proof_steps.claim: Let $Q$ be the universal rank-two quotient bundle on the first factor. The section of $\mathcal O(1)$ on the second factor tensored with $Q$ on the first, induced by the second tautological line modulo the first, vanishes exactly on the diagonal. In affine coordinates transverse to the diagonal its two components are a regular parameter pair; hence its Koszul complex is exact and resolves $\mathcal O_\Delta$. Since $\det Q=\mathcal O(1)$ and $Q^*=\Omega^1(1)$, the resolution is $0\to\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes\mathcal O(-2)\to\Omega^1(1)\boxtimes\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O\boxtimes\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\Delta\to0$. The regularity check is local along the diagonal, and outside it one component is a unit; this verifies exactness at every point. Its alternating $K$-class is the diagonal generator from [F5], but here the actual Koszul complex, rather than only its $K$-class, supplies the resolution.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] The Chern character is additive on exact complexes, $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal L)=e^{c_1(\mathcal L)}$ for a line bundle, and $\operatorname{ch}_2=\tfrac12(c_1^2-2c_2)$. [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]]

proof_steps.claim:
In the algebraic Chow ring, [F1] and $H=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ give
$$
\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)=(2k+N)-ke^{-H}-ke^H=N-kH^2,
$$
because $H^4=0$ on the complex threefold and the odd powers cancel. Thus $c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal F)=0$ and $c_2^{\rm alg}(\mathcal F)=kH^2$. In the underlying topological category the same exact sequences are exact sequences of complex vector bundles, so [F5] and the line-class identity $c_1(\mathcal O(1))=H$ give
$$
c(\mathcal F)=\frac{1}{(1-H)^k(1+H)^k}=(1-H^2)^{-k}=1+kH^2
$$
through degree six, since $H^4=0$. Hence the topological classes are $c_1(\mathcal F)=0$, $c_2(\mathcal F)=kH^2$, and $c_3(\mathcal F)=0$. The universal formulas $\operatorname{ch}_1=c_1$, $\operatorname{ch}_2=\tfrac12(c_1^2-2c_2)$, and $\operatorname{ch}_3=\tfrac16(c_1^3-3c_1c_2+3c_3)$ then give the topological $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)=N-kH^2$. This compares only the identical finite line-bundle resolution and its line class, not arbitrary analytic and algebraic cohomology.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F6] The algebraic first Chern class of $\mathcal O(1)$ is the hyperplane divisor class; its cycle class is the Poincaré dual of the complex hyperplane, which is the Euler class of its complex normal line. Thus its cycle class is $H_{\rm top}$. [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]], [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]]

proof_steps.claim: A fiber $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)$ is a complex linear $\mathbb P^1\subset\mathbb P^3$. Its real codimension in $\mathbb P^3$ is $4$ and its real dimension is $2$, so the sign in [F3] is $(-1)^{4\cdot2}=+1$. Therefore $\pi^*u$ is Poincaré dual to $[L_x]$. The restriction of $\mathcal O(1)$ to this linear $\mathbb P^1$ has first Chern number $1$; [F2] then identifies its Poincaré dual as $H_{\rm top}^2$. Thus $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] The exact rank-two theorem supplies the ordinary framed ASD connection of a regular rank-two datum by its raw forward monad/projection construction, extends it smoothly over infinity, and proves $q_2=-k$. Its exact GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form hypotheses are retained in the rank-one raw emptiness deduction. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition.

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] The exact framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad theorem gives the stable-data/framed torsion-free-sheaf correspondence, with rank $N\ge1$, Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, framing character $\sum e_\alpha^{-1}$, inverse extraction, and tangent correspondence in its stated locally-free/base-change family range. Combined with the finite real/complex quotient theorem, its positive-FI clause has the quotient used here. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: The quotient in [A1] has exactly the raw equation, stability, dual framing representation, rank and Hilbert polynomial of the Statement. Its normalized construction is equivariant for those framing and rotation characters, and the first-order family clause identifies tangent representations in its stated base-change range. Thus [A1] transfers the fixed-point bijection and tangent characters of step 1.1 to the Gieseker space.

For $k>0$, use the tuple $Y_1=\{(i,0):0\leq i<k\}$ and $Y_\alpha=\varnothing$ for $\alpha>1$; step 1.1 constructs a stable datum. Replacing $B_1$ by $B_1+c\,\mathrm{id}_V$ preserves the complex equation and stability while changing $\operatorname{tr}(B_1)$ by $kc$ for every $c\in\mathbb C$. Trace is invariant under conjugation, so the descended trace function on the geometric quotient has image $\mathbb C$, which is not compact. Thus the quotient is noncompact. The completed Borel carrier matches the compact real-Borel interface in [L1]. The ADHM/monad comparisons in [A1]–[A2] retain their exact analytic and family hypotheses, while step 2.3 has supplied the precise intrinsic localized Borel–Moore pushforward covered by [F6].

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] The preceding lemma supplies the exact P² diagonal monad and its framed vanishings under the stated cohomology/base-change assumptions; its algebraic/analytic family comparison uses the exact projective GAGA interface and the stated base-change hypotheses. [[lem-qftx-p2-beilinson-diagonal-and-framed-vanishing]]

proof_steps.claim: Conversely, let $\mathcal E$ be a framed torsion-free sheaf with the stated Hilbert polynomial. The preceding Beilinson lemma constructs its monad, with terms $V_1\mathcal O(-1)$, $M\mathcal O$, and $V_2\mathcal O(1)$ of ranks $k,2k+N,k$. Its restriction to $L_\infty$ remains exact at the ends because $\mathcal E$ is locally free there. Put $K=\ker\beta|_{L_\infty}$. The sequence $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to W\mathcal O\to0$ splits since $\operatorname{Ext}^1(W\mathcal O,V_1\mathcal O(-1))=V_1\otimes W^*\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$.

The remaining line extension $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\oplus W\mathcal O\to M\mathcal O\to V_2\mathcal O(1)\to0$ has class in $\operatorname{Hom}(V_2,V_1)\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$, since $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$. Twist by $\mathcal O(-1)$ and take cohomology. The connecting map $V_2\to V_1\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$ is an isomorphism: the adjacent groups $H^0(\mathcal O(-1))$ and $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))$ vanish, while $H^1(\mathcal O(-2))\cong\mathbb C$. Thus $V_2$ is identified with $V_1$ by this canonical extension class. Choosing a basis of $V_1$ and using the fixed framed basis of $W$ identifies $M=V\oplus V\oplus W$ and the line maps with the two Euler blocks in the Statement. Any other such choice differs by one simultaneous element of $GL(V)$.

The remaining coefficients of the two linear maps are their $z_0$ coefficients, so write $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0C_1+z_2,z_0C_2-z_1,z_0I)$. The coefficients of $z_0z_1$ and $z_0z_2$ in $\beta\alpha=0$ force $C_1=B_2$ and $C_2=B_1$; the $z_0^2$ coefficient is then $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. This recovers the stated ADHM form. The surjectivity of $\beta$ implies stability: if $U=\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(W)\}$ were proper, it is invariant and the induced $B_1,B_2$ on $V/U$ commute because $[B_1,B_2]=-IJ$ has image in $U$. Their dual actions on the nonzero annihilator $U^\perp\subset V^*$ commute, so [F6] gives a common eigen-covector $\lambda\ne0$ with $\lambda I=0$. At the corresponding affine point, $\lambda\beta=0$, contradicting surjectivity.

The Beilinson construction is natural under framed sheaf isomorphisms, so an isomorphism of framed sheaves induces maps on the cohomology vector spaces used in steps 1.2–6.2 and hence a single change of basis $g\in GL(V)$; the normalized Euler blocks force the recovered tuples to differ by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)$. Conversely such a $g$ is an isomorphism of monads acting trivially on $W$, and therefore induces a framed sheaf isomorphism. This proves the pointwise inverse equivalence modulo $GL(V)$. For a finite-type data family, step 2.1 makes $\beta$ surjective on the total space, so $K=\ker\beta$ is locally free. The sequence $0\to V\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to\mathcal E\to0$ is exact and its terms before $\mathcal E$ are flat over the base. After tensoring with any residue field of the base, the first map remains sheaf-injective by step 1.1; hence $\operatorname{Tor}_1(k(s),\mathcal E)=0$. Since $\mathcal E$ is finite over each local ring of $\mathbb P^2\times S$ and its residue fiber is a vector space over the residue field, [F8] gives flatness over $S$. Under the stated relative cohomology and base-change hypotheses, the same constructions use vector bundles and are inverse for families.

Apply the family equivalence to $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. A first-order deformation of the ADHM data is $(\dot B_1,\dot B_2,\dot I,\dot J)$ satisfying $d\mu_{\mathbb C}=0$; infinitesimal changes of basis are $d_0(\xi)=([\xi,B_1],[\xi,B_2],\xi I,-J\xi)$. Differentiating the monad gives the chain perturbation $(\dot\alpha,\dot\beta)$ with $\beta\dot\alpha+\dot\beta\alpha=0$, and a change by $d_0(\xi)$ is the corresponding chain homotopy. Since the family construction and its inverse commute with this dual-number base change, they induce inverse linear maps on first-order framed deformations and on the quotient tangent spaces $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$.

If $k=0$, $V=0$, all four maps and both equations are the unique zero-dimensional maps, stability and costability are vacuous, and the monad is $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its middle cohomology is the framed bundle $W\mathcal O$ with Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}$. Conversely, [F3] constructs this same zero-term monad from every framed sheaf with that polynomial, so the framing identifies each such sheaf with $W\mathcal O$. Thus both moduli spaces are points, and all empty-matrix and Euler-block conventions are satisfied.

final_edge_fact_uses.text:
[F7] The finite algebraic resolution gives
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N-kH^2$, $c_1(F)=0$, $c_2(F)=kH^2$,

[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-charge-normalization]]

proof_steps.claim: The finite monad resolution and its locally free cohomology give the algebraic Chern character and Chern classes in [F7]. Its same finite line resolution yields the topological classes after the hyperplane cycle class is identified with the Euler class of the complex normal line. The positive incidence-fiber Thom calculation in [F7] gives $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$. If the topological bundle is $\pi^*E$, naturality gives $\pi^*c_2(E)=kH_{\rm top}^2=k\pi^*u$; since $\pi^*u$ is a generator, $c_2(E)=ku$. fact_uses.text: [F2] $Q\subseteq\{x:|x_i-c_{Q,i}|\le\ell/2\ \text{for every }i\}$ and $Q^*=\{x:|x_i-c_{Q,i}|\le\sqrt n\,\ell\ \text{for every }i\}$ in the notation of [[def-dyadic-cube-in-rn-all-generations]]; the Euclidean and supremum norms on $\mathbb R^n$ satisfy $\|v\|_\infty\le\|v\|_2\le\sqrt n\,\|v\|_\infty$.

proof_steps.claim:
If $y\in Q$ and $x
otin Q^*$, then $\|x-c_Q\|_\infty>\sqrt n\,\ell$ and $\|y-c_Q\|_\infty\le\ell/2$, so by [F2] $\|x-c_Q\|_2\ge\|x-c_Q\|_\infty>\sqrt n\,\ell\ge2\|y-c_Q\|_2$; hence $|x-c_Q|\ge2|y-c_Q|$, and in particular $x

fact_uses.text: [L1] $Q_{k,m}=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:m_i2^{-k}<x_i\le(m_i+1)2^{-k}\text{ for every }i<n\}$ with $k\in\mathbb Z$, the side length is $2^{-k}$, and every dyadic cube is nonempty ([[def-dyadic-cube-in-rn-all-generations]]).

proof_steps.claim: Given $x\in\mathbb R^n$, step 1.1 applied in each coordinate to the real $2^kx_i$ produces exactly one integer $m_i$ with $m_i<2^kx_i\le m_i+1$; by step 1.2 the function $m$ is the unique index of a generation-$k$ dyadic cube containing $x$. Hence the generation-$k$ cubes cover $\mathbb R^n$ and no two distinct ones share a point, and by step 1.4 each has volume $2^{-kn}$.

Put $d:=k'-k\ge0$ and $M_i:=m_i2^{d}\in\mathbb Z$; by [F2], $m_i2^{-k}=M_i2^{-k'}$ and $(m_i+1)2^{-k}=(M_i+2^{d})2^{-k'}$, so in coordinate $i$ the cube $Q$ is cut out by $M_i2^{-k'}<x_i\le(M_i+2^{d})2^{-k'}$ while $Q'$ is cut out by $m_i'2^{-k'}<x_i\le(m_i'+1)2^{-k'}$. If $x\in Q\cap Q'$, step 1.3 with $A:=M_i$, $B:=M_i+2^{d}$, $C:=m_i'$ and $t:=2^{k'}x_i$ gives $M_i\le m_i'$ and $m_i'+1\le M_i+2^{d}$ in every coordinate, so $Q'\subseteq Q$.

Fix $j<k$ and take the upper corner $x_i=(m_i+1)2^{-k}$ of $Q$; the half-open convention places $x$ in $Q$. By step 2.1 there is exactly one generation-$j$ cube $P$ containing $x$. Since $P$ and $Q$ intersect and $j<k$, step 2.2 gives $Q\subseteq P$. If $P'$ is another generation-$j$ cube containing $Q$, it contains $x$, hence $P'=P$ by step 2.1. This proves unique ancestry without any erroneous scaling of the integer index. For the parent $j=k-1$, step 1.4 gives $|P|=2^{-(k-1)n}=2^n2^{-kn}=2^n|Q|$.

fact_uses.text: [F2] $\int_Q|f|\,d\lambda\le\|f\|_1<\infty$ for every measurable $Q$, and every dyadic cube has finite volume ([[def-l-one-of-a-measure]], [[def-dyadic-cube-in-rn-all-generations]]).

proof_steps.claim: Call a dyadic cube **bad** when $|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|f|>\lambda$. Every bad cube satisfies $0\le\lambda|Q|<\int_Q|f|\le\|f\|_1$, so $|Q|<\lambda^{-1}\|f\|_1$; in particular there is a scale above which no bad cube lives.

Let $Q$ be a maximal bad cube and $P$ its parent; by step 1.2 the cube $P$ is good, that is, $|P|^{-1}\int_P|f|\le\lambda$. Since $Q\subseteq P$ and $|P|=2^n|Q|$ by [F1], $\int_Q|f|\le\int_P|f|\le\lambda|P|=2^n\lambda|Q|$, so the average of every maximal bad cube is at most $2^n\lambda$. For the sum, the maximal bad cubes are pairwise disjoint by step 1.2, so with disjoint additivity and monotonicity of the integral, $$\sum_Q\lambda|Q|\le\sum_Q\int_Q|f|=\int_{\bigcup Q}|f|\le\|f\|_1,$$ because each maximal bad cube has average $>\lambda$; hence $\sum_Q|Q|\le\lambda^{-1}\|f\|_1$, the sums being understood as suprema of finite partial sums over the countable family.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-qftx-taubes-arbitrary-divisor-plane-vortex]]: for each effective divisor there is a unique scalar $h$ with the stated logarithmic subtractions and decay; the reconstruction is smooth, solves the positive first-order equations, has finite energy, and has flux $2\pi$ times the degree. Negative winding follows by conjugation.

proof_steps.claim: Its multiplicities give degree $N=2+1=3$ and distributional source $4\pi(2\delta_{z_0}+\delta_{z_1})=8\pi\delta_{z_0}+4\pi\delta_{z_1}$. The center subtraction coefficients are $2m_0=4$ and $2m_1=2$. Applying [F2] gives the unique scalar $h$, its smooth subtractions, $h\to0$, and strict negativity away from the divisor.
Apply [F2] to the explicit effective divisor $|n|[0]$ of degree $|n|$ (the empty divisor if $n=0$) and conjugate when $n<0$. Its signed flux is $2\pi n$, and [F3] gives $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|$.

Here $P=(z-z_0)^2(z-z_1)$ and $s=2\log|P|$. The reconstruction in [F2] extends smoothly over both centers, solves the positive critical equations, and has flux $2\pi N=6\pi$. Since it is a fixed-divisor reconstructed solution, [F3] gives its attained absolute transverse energy $2\pi\xi N=6\pi\xi$. The argument determines the profile by the unique scalar boundary-value problem and supplies no elementary closed form.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F8] [[thm-interior-w-two-p-estimate-for-uniformly-elliptic-equations]]: for $p>2$ and $\Delta w=f\in L^p$ on a ball in $\mathbb R^2$, the $W^{2,p}$ norm on the concentric half-ball is bounded by the local $L^p$ norms of $f$ and $w$.

proof_steps.claim: On any smaller compact disk $K\Subset U$, [F8] applied on finitely many nested balls and the uniform $L^\infty$ bound of step 7.1 yields uniform $W^{2,p}$ bounds for $w_R$ for every finite $p>2$, since its Laplacian is bounded. For a prescribed $0<\alpha<1$, choose $p>2/(1-\alpha)$ and then $\beta$ with $\alpha<\beta<1-2/p$; [F6] gives a uniform $C^{1,\beta}$ bound on a slightly larger compact disk. As $e^s$ is smooth and $\Delta w_R=\kappa(e^s e^{w_R}-1)$, the right-hand side has a uniform $C^{0,\alpha}$ bound there; [F9] then yields a uniform $C^{2,\alpha}$ bound on $K$. These bounds are independent of $R$ and are the local compactness estimates used for disk exhaustion.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] For every effective divisor, the scalar Taubes problem has its unique smooth desingularized solution and reconstructs a smooth finite-energy critical connection/Higgs field with the prescribed zeros, flux, and exponential gauge-invariant decay; negative winding uses conjugation. [[thm-qftx-taubes-arbitrary-divisor-plane-vortex]]

proof_steps.claim: For each chosen effective divisor of degree $|n|$, apply [F3] with $e=g$ and $\xi=2v^2$, using its conjugate for negative n. [F4] fixes its finite energy and flux normalization. The polynomial phase correction relative to $n\theta$ is degree zero and tends to zero; the cutoff cleanup used in [F5] removes only this correction globally, preserving the divisor. The resulting embedded fields have a=p=0 and satisfy the appropriate critical equations, so all residuals in step 2.1 vanish and the full-model energy is exactly $T_n$. The same identity bounds every competing full-model profile below by $T_n$, proving absolute minimality. Compactly supported smooth variations preserve the flux/vacuum class, so differentiability of their energy at the minimum gives vanishing first variation. This proves actual existence and stationarity for every divisor, without a radial or unit-winding restriction.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F5] [[pthm-qftx-n2-linear-monopole-bps-vortex-bound]]: in the frozen-metric linear truncation, actual mathematical arbitrary-divisor vortices embed as stationary absolute full-model minima with $T_n=4\pi v^2|n|$; actual canonical full-model collars give $T_nL+O(1)$ for fixed-flux cylinder infima. Its nonlinear stationarity obstruction and screened dual-electric response keep this exact critical result separate from generic nonlinear confinement.

proof_steps.claim:
Under the additional vortex/minimization hypothesis in the Statement,
[F4] gives nonzero quantized original electric flux and a tension
$\sigma>0$. The interior of a translation-invariant tube of length $L$
contains the same transverse profile at each longitudinal coordinate, so
its bulk energy is $\sigma L$. The uniformly bounded endcap contribution
therefore gives $V(L)=\sigma L+O(1)$, which is linear confinement in this
effective model. This last conclusion is conditional: no preceding step establishes existence or minimization of the required profile. Original electric probes correspond to dual magnetic flux; the condensed original magnetic charges are dual electric charges and are screened in the linear response about the dual Higgs vacuum described by [F5]. This conclusion concerns classical effective energy, not a quantum Wilson-loop area law.

In the explicitly linear truncation, assume [A3] and apply [F5] with $\xi=2v^2$ to each chosen effective divisor of degree $|n|$. It supplies an actual smooth stationary full-model minimum of tension $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|=4\pi v^2|n|$, and actual finite collars from every fixed canonical full-model end trace in the stated valid neutral disk. Thus $T_nL\le I_L\le T_n(L-2\ell)+C_0+C_1$, proving $I_L=T_nL+O(1)$; matching minimizing traces attain $T_nL$ exactly. No solution or endcap existence is assumed for this critical boundary problem. The nonlinear obstruction in [F5] prevents extending its exact BPS assertion to generic u.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-qftx-taubes-arbitrary-divisor-plane-vortex]]: for every effective finite divisor of degree $|n|$ there is a smooth finite-energy planar critical pair with flux $2\pi n$ (using conjugation for $n<0$); for the empty divisor it is the vacuum. The local unwound exterior gauge has $q=\sqrt\xi e^{h/2}$ and $A=-\tfrac12*dh$; that degree-changing exterior gauge is not asserted to extend globally. Separately, removing only the smooth degree-zero polynomial phase correction relative to $n\theta$ by a global cutoff gauge yields the canonical winding representative $q=\sqrt\xi e^{h/2}e^{in\theta}$, $A=n\,d\theta-\tfrac12*dh$.

proof_steps.claim: For an end trace with exterior phase $n\theta+\phi$, choose a smooth radial cutoff $\eta$ which is zero on a disk containing the noncanonical region and one outside a larger disk. The real function $\chi=-\eta\phi$ extends smoothly by zero to the whole plane; the allowed gauge transformation $(q,A)\mapsto(e^{i\chi}q,A+d\chi)$ therefore makes the exterior phase exactly $n\theta$. This constructs the asserted degree-zero exterior phase cleanup without attempting to extend a degree-$n$ angular map across the disk. For the planar minimizer in [F2], write $P=|P|e^{i\vartheta}$ on the exterior; $\vartheta-n\theta$ is single-valued, smooth and tends to zero because $P(z)=z^n(1+O(|z|^{-1}))$ for $n\ge0$ (use the conjugate construction for $n<0$). Applying the same cutoff extension to $-(\vartheta-n\theta)$ changes its exterior fields to $q^*=\rho_*e^{in\theta}$ and $A^*=n\,d\theta-\tfrac12*dh$; hence $A^*-n\,d\theta$ decays exponentially.

In canonical exterior gauge write $q=\rho e^{in\theta}$ and $\alpha=A-n\,d\theta$. Directly, $D_Aq=e^{in\theta}(d\rho-i\rho\alpha)$, so the real and imaginary terms are orthogonal and $|D_Aq|^2=|d\rho|^2+\rho^2|\alpha|^2$. Uniform convergence gives $\rho\ge\sqrt\xi/2$ outside a disk; thus finite kinetic energy implies $\alpha\in L^2$ there. Also $|\rho-\sqrt\xi|\le |\rho^2-\xi|/\sqrt\xi$, so finite potential energy gives $\rho-\sqrt\xi\in L^2$ there. On compact disks all fields are smooth and bounded. Consequently, for any two cleaned end traces and the cleaned minimizer, differences of connections and Higgs fields are globally in $L^2$; each Higgs field is bounded.

Apply step 3.1 first to $p_0$ and $p_*$, defining its finite energy to be $C_0$, and then to $p_*$ and $p_1$, defining its finite energy to be $C_1$. For $L\ge2\ell$, place the first collar on $[0,\ell]$, the constant planar minimizer on $[\ell,L-\ell]$, and the second collar on $[L-\ell,L]$. The profiles match smoothly because the collar cutoff is constant near its ends. The middle has no longitudinal energy and contributes exactly $T_n(L-2\ell)$ by [F2]–[F3]. At $L=2\ell$ this middle interval has zero length; the two collars meet at the constant value $p_*$, so the same upper bound holds. This admissible concatenation proves $\inf\mathcal E_L\le C_0+T_n(L-2\ell)+C_1$.

Combining steps 1.1 and 4.1 gives $0\le\inf\mathcal E_L-T_nL\le C_0+C_1-2\ell T_n$ for every $L\ge2\ell$; the right side is a finite constant independent of $L$, proving the bounded-remainder conclusion. If $p_0=p_1=p_*$, the constant extension $(A_1,A_2,q)=(A^*,q^*)$, $A_3=0$, has energy $T_nL$ and satisfies the angular and no-leakage conditions. The lower bound from step 1.1 then proves it is an exact translation-invariant minimum.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-qftx-taubes-arbitrary-divisor-plane-vortex]]: for each effective finite divisor of degree $|n|$, the reconstructed smooth critical fields satisfy the corresponding first-order equations, have finite energy, and have flux $2\pi n$ with sign set by the orientation.

proof_steps.claim: For each fixed divisor, [F2] supplies a smooth pair satisfying the relevant first-order equations. Its square terms in step 1.1 vanish identically; the sequence estimates of steps 1.2–2.1 apply because [F2] gives finite energy and the same boundary sector. Hence its energy is exactly $2\pi\xi|n|$. The lower bound of step 3.1 applies to every admissible same-winding configuration, so this pair is an absolute transverse energy minimum, without radial or unit-winding assumptions.

Let $(a,\eta)$ be a smooth compactly supported variation of a minimizing pair, and set $A_t=A+ta$, $q_t=q+t\eta$; for any field expression $F$, define $\delta F:=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}F(A_t,q_t)$. For sufficiently small $t$, the fields remain in the same boundary sector; outside the compact support they equal the original fields. Thus the boundary-current limit in the disk identity is unchanged and the flux is unchanged by Stokes applied to $d a$. The energy along this variation is the constant $2\pi\xi|n|$ plus the squared $L^2$ norms of the two first-order residuals in step 1.1. Both residuals vanish at $t=0$; differentiating the squared norms gives $E'(0)=0$ and
$$E''(0)=2\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(|\delta(D_{A,1}\pm iD_{A,2})q|^2+\frac{|\delta(B\mp e^2(\xi-|q|^2))|^2}{2e^2}\right)dx_1dx_2\ge0,$$
with the upper signs for $n\ge0$ and lower signs for $n\le0$ (either choice when $n=0$). Therefore the first variation vanishes and no smooth compactly supported same-sector perturbation lowers the energy. Distinct divisors give distinct possible minimizing fields, so no cross-divisor uniqueness follows.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] [[thm-interior-w-two-p-estimate-for-uniformly-elliptic-equations]]: for $p>2$ on a two-dimensional ball, the interior $W^{2,p}$ norm is bounded by the local $L^p$ norms of the solution and its Laplacian.

proof_steps.claim: To obtain derivative decay, fix $\alpha<\alpha'<\sqrt\kappa$ and use step 3.3 at rate $\alpha'$. On each unit ball centered at large $z$, both $w$ and $\Delta w=\kappa(1-e^{-w})$ are $O(e^{-\alpha'|z|})$. By [F3] and [F5], $w$ has a $C^{1,\beta}$ norm of that order on the concentric half-ball for some $\beta>0$. Thus the right-hand side has a $C^{0,\beta}$ norm of the same order, and [F4] gives $C^{2,\beta}$ decay on a smaller ball. Inductively, for each multi-index $\gamma$, differentiating $\Delta w=\kappa(1-e^{-w})$ gives $\Delta D^\gamma w=\kappa e^{-w}D^\gamma w+G_\gamma$, where $G_\gamma$ is a finite sum of products of lower derivatives of $w$ and is exponentially small by the induction hypothesis. Applying [F3] and [F4] on nested unit balls gives the same $e^{-\alpha'|z|}$ bound for two more derivatives. Since $e^{-\alpha'|z|}\le e^{-\alpha|z|}$ outside a fixed disk, every finite derivative has the stated rate.

fact_uses.text: [F1] For a product $G$ of complex general linear groups, equivariant Borel–Moore homology is $\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j])$; its normalized dualizing object restricts to the ordinary one, and the groups agree in the stable range with dimension-shifted Borel approximations. The case $G=T=(\mathrm{GL}_1)^r$ applies. [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]

proof_steps.claim: Since $T=(\mathrm{GL}_1)^r$, [F1] supplies the normalized equivariant Borel–Moore groups and the stable scalar-frame construction. For $U_m=(\mathbb C^{m+1}\setminus\{0\})^r$, the quotient is $B_m=(\mathbb{CP}^m)^r$ and $\dim_{\mathbb C}U_m-\dim_{\mathbb C}T=rm$, giving the stated degree shift. AC is inherited from [F1] and is the only choice assumption added here.

The polar decomposition $T\cong K\times(\mathbb R_{>0})^r$ makes $K\hookrightarrow T$ a homotopy equivalence. Choose one contractible free $T$-space $E$; it is also free for $K$, and $E/K\to E/T$ has contractible fiber $T/K$. The Borel fibrations $(E\times X)/K\to E/K$ and $(E\times X)/T\to E/T$ have common fiber $X$, with identity map on that fiber. Their homotopy exact sequences therefore make $(E\times X)/K\to(E\times X)/T$ a weak equivalence. Model independence of the universal free contractible space identifies this with the product right Milnor model and the algebraic-torus approximation in [F1].

The operations in the Definition are the proper pushforward, open restriction, and support maps of [F2]; the cap action is the action of Borel cohomology through $E_K\times_KX\to B_K$. For smooth pure complex dimension $d$, the normalized dualizing object restricts to $\mathbb Q_X[2d]$, so the complex orientation gives $[X]_T$ degree $2d$. These constructions respect the stable comparison of [F1].

fact_uses.text: [F3] Assume AC. The definition [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]] fixes $H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j])$, its stable Borel value $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{j+2b}(X\times_GU;k)$ for a free smooth approximation with $b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, and the corner degrees $d_i+d_j-p$; the ambient category is that of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]].

proof_steps.claim: Orientation and the degree. The smooth orientation of [F1] on the smooth pure $d_j$-dimensional source $X_j$ says $k_{X_j}=\omega_{X_j}[-2d_j]$, and dualizing transitivity for $q$ gives $q^!k_{X_j}=q^!\omega_{X_j}[-2d_j]=\omega_{Z_{ij}}[-2d_j]$. Substituting $t=r+d_j-d_i$, the group of step 1.1 is $\operatorname{Hom}(k_Z,\omega_Z[r-d_i-d_j])$, which is exactly $H_{d_i+d_j-r}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij};k)$ in the normalization of [F3]. At a finite free smooth approximation of dimension offset $b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, the space $X_j\times_GU$ is smooth of complex dimension $d_j+b$ while the descended complex retains the shift $d_j$, so the identical calculation gives ordinary Borel–Moore degree $d_i+d_j+2b-r$; removing $2b$ gives the stated equivariant degree, and no stack-dimension shift is inserted into $\omega_X^G$.

Naturality, linearity and finiteness. Every map in the chain of steps 1.1 and 2.1 is an adjunction, base-change or orientation map supplied naturally by [F1], so the composite is natural in constructible coefficient morphisms before the smooth orientation is applied and is compatible with composition of the $f_i$. By [F2] these maps commute with the approximation transition pullbacks on the bounded ranges, so the composite induces an isomorphism in each stable degree; coherent scalar pullback from the base point together with the projection formula of [F1] gives equivariant-cohomology linearity. Degreewise finiteness is exactly the conclusion of [F4] for bounded algebraically constructible objects, and it is asserted nowhere that the direct sum over all degrees is finite-dimensional. Smoothness of the sources is used only for the orientation in step 2.1, and properness only in the base change and in the identification $f_{i!}=f_{i*}$; no semismallness, decomposition theorem, purity or smoothness of $E$ or of the fiber products $Z_{ij}$ is used.

fact_uses.text: [F2] [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]] fixes the source-first convention, the geometric product $a*b=h_*\Delta_{X_j}^!(a\boxtimes b)$ with its degree drop $2d_j$, the ordered coordinates, the zero rule for nonmatching indices and the corner degrees.

proof_steps.claim: Geometric interpretation of the mate. Put $S=A\times B$, $F=(q,u):S\to X_j\times X_j$, and $\theta:T\hookrightarrow S$. By [F1] the pulled-back positive purity counit is $g_F:\theta_*k_T[-2d_j]\to k_S$. The external dualizing class corresponding to $\kappa\boxtimes\lambda$ has degree $n+n'$, where $n=d_i+d_j-r$ and $n'=d_j+d_k-s$ by [F3]; composing it with $g_F$ and taking the adjoint under $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$ gives a class of degree $n+n'-2d_j$ on $T$. The graph-factorization and composition-of-counits comparison proved in [F1] identifies this supported cap map with the mate in step 2.1, followed by $b^!\lambda[t]$. Thus its representative is exactly the adjoint of $W$. The purity counit, its pullback, and the mate are fixed global morphisms; the positive normal-ball generator fixes their orientation, while their equality on arbitrary supports follows from that supported adjunction comparison.

Pushing the correspondence to the third corner. Its adjoint representative is $U_C:m_!k_C\xrightarrow{m_!\eta_h}m_!h_*k_T=(vb)_!k_T\xrightarrow{W}k_k[t+w]$, where $\eta_h:k_C\to h_*h^*k_C=h_*k_T$ is the ordinary adjunction unit and $h_*=h_!$ by [F4]. Apply [F6] to the band-limited source $J=P_EJ$ and the positive operator verified in step 1.1; its vector and action inequalities are the two displayed remainder bounds. When the additional condition $E<M$ holds, the factor $E^2/M^2$ is less than one and the bound decreases geometrically with $N$. final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] For every continuous map from a finite polyhedron into $\mathcal A_\infty$, with irreducible values on a subpolyhedron, the relative avoidance lemma supplies a homotopy fixed on that subpolyhedron and an open neighborhood of it whose endpoint is entirely irreducible. proof_steps.claim: The affine space $\mathcal A_\infty$ contains $A_0$. Apply [F2] to the constant map from a one-point polyhedron with empty subpolyhedron and value $A_0$. Its endpoint is an element of $\mathcal A_\infty^*$, proving nonemptiness.

Let $A,B\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$. The affine path $\gamma(t)=(1-t)A+tB$ is continuous in the Fréchet topology and has irreducible endpoints. Apply [F2] with $K=I$ and $L=\{0,1\}$. The resulting endpoint path remains in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and fixes both endpoints, so the locus is path-connected.

Apply [F2] to $F$ with $K=D^{j+1}$ and $L=\partial D^{j+1}=S^j$. Its boundary is already irreducible, so the endpoint is a map $G:D^{j+1}\to\mathcal A_\infty^*$ agreeing with $u$ on the boundary. Choose the based point $x_0\in S^j$ with $u(x_0)=A$. Since the disk is convex, $C_t(x)=(1-t)x+tx_0$ remains in the disk and fixes $x_0$. Then $G(C_t(x))$ is a homotopy from $G$ to the constant map at $A$ that fixes $x_0$ and remains in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$. Restricting it to $S^j$ gives a based nullhomotopy of $u$; by [F3], its class in $\pi_j(\mathcal A_\infty^*,A)$ is zero. Since $j$ and $u$ were arbitrary, every stated homotopy group vanishes.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[def-qftx-unitary-super-poincare-representation]]: the Hilbert inner product is positive, $\bar Q=(Q)^*$ is the actual adjoint with its actual domain, and every product in these anticommutators is defined on the common invariant domain.

proof_steps.claim: At rest $P_0=-M I$ and $P_j=0$, so [F1] gives $\{Q^I_1,(Q^J_1)^*\}=2M\delta_{IJ}I$ and $\{Q^I_2,(Q^J_2)^*\}=2M\delta_{IJ}I$. Put $q_I=Q^I_1$ and $r_I=(Q^I_2)^*$; then $\{q_I,r_J^*\}=2z^{IJ}I$ and $\{r_J,q_I^*\}=2\bar z_{IJ}I$, with all these products defined on $\mathcal D$.

For $u,v\in\mathbb C^N$, define on $\mathcal D$ the charge combination $B_{u,v}=\sum_I\bar u_Iq_I+\sum_I\bar v_Ir_I$ and the combination of its summand adjoints $B^\sharp_{u,v}=\sum_Iu_Iq_I^*+\sum_Iv_Ir_I^*$. Expanding the algebraic anticommutator on $\mathcal D$ gives $B_{u,v}B^\sharp_{u,v}+B^\sharp_{u,v}B_{u,v}=\left(2M(\|u\|_2^2+\|v\|_2^2)+4\operatorname{Re}(u^*Zv)\right)I$. The diagonal blocks use the two mixed rest anticommutators in step 1.1, and the off-diagonal terms are $2u^*Zv$ and its complex conjugate. For every $\psi\in\mathcal D$, expanding the quadratic form term by term and using the adjoint identity for each individual charge gives $\langle(B_{u,v}B^\sharp_{u,v}+B^\sharp_{u,v}B_{u,v})\psi,\psi\rangle=\|B_{u,v}\psi\|^2+\|B^\sharp_{u,v}\psi\|^2\ge0$.

If $M=|z|$, step 4.1 gives $AA^\sharp+A^\sharp A=0$ on $\mathcal D$. For every $\psi\in\mathcal D$, the actual-adjoint identity for the individual charge summands in [F2] gives $0=\langle(AA^\sharp+A^\sharp A)\psi,\psi\rangle=\|A\psi\|^2+\|A^\sharp\psi\|^2$. Each squared norm is nonnegative, so both vanish. If $\mathcal K$ is finite-dimensional, $A^\sharp=A^*$ and this is the ordinary operator-adjoint conclusion; in general it is the stated dense-domain conclusion. The result is confined to the fixed rest fiber and asserts no state existence or stability.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] For the stated Sobolev index, the smooth irreducible projection $\mathcal A_\infty^*\to\mathcal A_\infty^*/\overline{\mathcal G}_\infty$ is a locally trivial topological principal $\overline{\mathcal G}_\infty$-bundle with its actual $C^\infty$ quotient topology; the Sobolev irreducible locus $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open. [[thm-qftx-sobolev-smooth-irreducible-gauge-bundle]]

proof_steps.claim: Choose the fixed integer $k>r/2+1$. The smooth clause of [F3], applied with the configuration data [F2], makes $q_*$ a locally trivial principal $\overline{\mathcal G}^\infty(P)$-bundle. By [F4], its total space is nonempty, path connected, and has $\pi_j=0$ for every $j\ge1$, so it is weakly contractible in the sense used in [F6]. For a constant central gauge section $u=\zeta I_N$, the local action formula gives $A^u=A$ because $u^{-1}Au=A$ and $du=0$; hence reduced and full gauge groups have the same orbits on $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)$.

The locus $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)$ is gauge invariant: in the chosen frame, the based holonomy subgroup of $A^u$ is $u(p_m)^{-1}\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)u(p_m)$, so it has the same invariant subspaces up to conjugation. It is open: by [F2], the inclusion $\mathcal A^\infty(P)\hookrightarrow\mathcal A_k(P)$ is continuous, as each fixed $H^k$ norm is bounded by finitely many smooth derivative seminorms on the finite compact atlas. The smooth irreducible locus is the inverse image of the Sobolev irreducible locus, which is open by [F3]. The full orbit projection $q$ is open because, for any open $U\subseteq\mathcal A^\infty(P)$, its saturation $q^{-1}(q(U))=\bigcup_{u\in\mathcal G^\infty(P)}U\cdot u$ is open. For fixed smooth $u$, the map $A\mapsto u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$ is continuous in every finite-atlas derivative seminorm by the Leibniz rule; its inverse is the same formula for $u^{-1}$, so each gauge translate is a homeomorphism. Therefore $q(\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P))$ is open and $q|_{\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)}$ is an open quotient map onto this subset. The reduced and full actions have the same orbits there, so their quotient topologies identify the reduced orbit space homeomorphically with $q(\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P))$; this proves the claim about $\iota$ in the Statement. If $q$ had a continuous section, its restriction to this open subset would take each irreducible orbit to a point in that same orbit, hence into $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)$. Via the stated homeomorphism, this would give a continuous section of $q_*$, contradicting step 3.1. Thus $q$ has no continuous section.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] The reduced action is free and proper, and the irreducible locus is open. [[lem-qftx-gauge-stabilizer-and-properness]]

proof_steps.claim: Apply the inverse-function theorem [F4] to $\Phi_A(s,u):=s^u$ on the local Banach product $S_{A,\varepsilon}\times\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ near $(A,e)$; its derivative is $L_A$ from step 1.2. Shrink $\varepsilon$ so the slice remains in the open irreducible locus. At $(s,e)$, for $s=A+a$, the derivative is $L_s(b,\xi)=b+d_s\xi$ on $b\in\ker d_A^*$; this differs from $L_A$ only by $(b,\xi)\mapsto[a,\xi]$. Its operator norm is at most $C\|a\|_{H^k}$ by [F7]. Choose $\varepsilon$ so $C\varepsilon\|L_A^{-1}\|<1$; then [F5] makes $L_s$ an isomorphism for every $s$ in the slice. At an arbitrary $(s,u_0)$, write $u=u_0v$ near $u_0$ and use $s^{u_0v}=(s^{u_0})^v$. Applying the inverse action by $u_0$ to the target tangent and changing the gauge tangent by the invertible adjoint action identifies this derivative with $L_s$. Hence the derivative is an isomorphism at every point of the slice product, and the inverse-function theorem makes $\Phi_A$ a local diffeomorphism throughout.

The map $\Phi_A$ is injective after possibly shrinking the slice further. Otherwise there would be sequences $s_j,t_j\in S_{A,1/j}$ and distinct pairs $(s_j,u_j)\ne(t_j,v_j)$ with $s_j^{u_j}=t_j^{v_j}$. Put $w_j=u_jv_j^{-1}$; then $s_j^{w_j}=t_j$ and $s_j,t_j\to A$. Properness [F2] gives a subsequence of $w_j$ converging to $w$ with $A^w=A$. Freeness [F2] gives $w=e$. Hence for all sufficiently large indices, both $(s_j,w_j)$ and $(t_j,e)$ lie in the local injectivity neighborhood from step 2.1. Their equal images force $s_j=t_j$ and $w_j=e$, and freeness then gives $u_j=v_j$, contradicting distinctness.

The orbit relation on $\mathcal A_k^*$ is closed: if $x_j^{u_j}=y_j$ and $(x_j,y_j)\to(x,y)$, properness [F2] gives a convergent subsequence $u_{j_\ell}\to u$, and continuity of the action gives $x^u=y$. For distinct orbits, the complement of this closed relation contains their pair, so there are product neighborhoods $O_x\times O_y$ disjoint from the relation. Their saturations are open and disjoint: if the saturations intersected, some translate of a point in $O_x$ would equal a translate of a point in $O_y$, making that pair related. Their quotient images therefore separate the two orbits. This proves the quotient is Hausdorff.

For the smooth-space clause, fix now a smooth irreducible center $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and use the Banach slice and trivialization established in step 4.1. Put $U_A=\Phi_A(S_{A,\varepsilon}\times\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1})$ and $V_A=\pi_k(S_{A,\varepsilon})$. Since $U_A$ is open in $\mathcal A_k^*$, $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open in the stated $C^\infty$ topology; set $S_A^\infty=S_{A,\varepsilon}\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and $V_A^\infty=\pi_\infty(S_A^\infty)$. For a smooth $B\in U_A$, its unique reduced gauge class from step 4.1 has a representative $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$. It satisfies $d_A^*(B^{u^{-1}}-A)=0$. Locally in a bundle frame, write $C_j=uB_j u^{-1}-(\partial_j u)u^{-1}-A_j$. Substitution in $d_A^*C=0$, use of $\partial_i(u^{-1})=-u^{-1}(\partial_i u)u^{-1}$, and multiplication on the right by $u$ isolate the equation $g^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j u=R(A,B,g;u,u^{-1},du)$ on each chart. Every term in $R$ is a finite product of smooth coefficients (including first derivatives of $A,B$) and factors among $u,u^{-1},du$; hence the principal operator is the scalar smooth Laplacian on each matrix entry. If $u\in H^{r+1}$ for $r\ge k$, then this right-hand side lies in $H^r$ by [F7] and the smooth coefficient bounds. Elliptic regularity [F6] gives $u\in H^{r+2}$. Iteration proves $u$ smooth; changing its representative by an element of the finite center preserves smoothness. Thus every smooth point of the Banach saturation has a smooth trivialization representative, and $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*=\pi_\infty^{-1}(V_A^\infty)$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-qftx-unitary-super-poincare-representation]]: $E$ is a joint PVM with future-cone support, it is covariant under the even Lorentz group, it commutes with translations, and every charge and adjoint has the stated reducing-projection/domain property for each $E(B)$.

proof_steps.claim: The function $s(p)=-\eta^{\mu\nu}p_\mu p_\nu=(p^0)^2-|\vec p|^2$ is continuous and nonnegative on the closed future cone in [F1]. For each Borel $A\subseteq[0,\infty)$, $\{p\in\mathcal C_+^*:s(p)\in A\}$ is Borel in the full covector space because $\mathcal C_+^*$ is closed and $s$ is continuous there. Inverse images preserve disjoint unions, and the preimage of $[0,\infty)$ is $\mathcal C_+^*$, whose projection is $I$ by [F1]; therefore the pushforward $F(A):=E(\{p\in\mathcal C_+^*:s(p)\in A\})$ is a normalized PVM on $[0,\infty)$ by strong countable additivity of $E$.

For each Borel $A$, $F(A)$ is the projection $E(\{p\in\mathcal C_+^*:s(p)\in A\})$. The charge-domain reduction in [F1] therefore gives $F(A)D(Q)\subseteq D(Q)$ and $QF(A)\psi=F(A)Q\psi$ for every $\psi\in D(Q)$; the same argument applies to $Q^*$. This proves the spectral-subspace assertion.

Since $s(\Lambda_g^\vee p)=s(p)$, Lorentz covariance of $E$ implies $U(g,0)F(A)U(g,0)^*=F(A)$. Translation unitaries are bounded Borel functions of $E$, so they commute with every $F(A)$; $\Gamma$ commutes with $E$ by [F1]. Hence $\operatorname{ran}F(A)$ is closed and graded, invariant under the integrated even group, and invariant under every charge and adjoint with dense restricted domains: density follows by applying the bounded projection $F(A)$ to a dense operator domain. Irreducibility as defined in [F1] forces $F(A)=0$ or $F(A)=I$.

Choose any nonzero vector and normalize it to a unit vector $\psi\in\mathcal H$; set $\mu(A)=\langle F(A)\psi,\psi\rangle$. By [F3] this is a countably additive probability measure, and by step 2.2 every value is $0$ or $1$. The set $R=\{r\ge0:\mu([0,r])=1\}$ is nonempty: otherwise the countable union $[0,\infty)=\bigcup_{n\ge1}[0,n]$ would have measure zero. Put $m^2=\inf R$, which is a finite nonnegative real.

For every $\varepsilon>0$, the infimum property gives $r\in R$ with $r<m^2+\varepsilon$, so $\mu([0,m^2+\varepsilon])=1$. If $m^2>\varepsilon$, then $m^2-\varepsilon<m^2$ is not in $R$, and the zero-or-one property gives $\mu([0,m^2-\varepsilon])=0$. Thus for all sufficiently large $n$, the nested intervals $I_n=(\max(0,m^2-1/n),m^2+1/n]$ have measure one; when $m^2=0$, use $I_n=[0,1/n]$. Countable additivity of the finite measure gives continuity from above, hence $\mu(\{m^2\})=\lim_n\mu(I_n)=1$. Therefore $F(\{m^2\})\ne0$, and step 2.2 forces $F(\{m^2\})=I$. If $A$ contains $m^2$, monotonicity gives $F(A)=I$; if not, then $\mu(A)=0$ because $A$ is disjoint from $\{m^2\}$, so the zero-or-one property gives $F(A)=0$. This rule also proves uniqueness: any second value with projection $I$ would have to equal $m^2$, since the singleton projections for distinct values are orthogonal.

proof_steps.claim: The rational character formula is [F2]. For the real formula, restrict a smooth character to the coordinate circles; the rational supplier [F2] gives its integer vector \(\mathbf n\). The associated one-dimensional representation \(\mathbb C_{\chi_{\mathbf n}}\) is the tensor product of the coordinate representations \(\mathbb C_{\chi_i}^{\otimes n_i}\), interpreting negative powers as duals; taking associated bundles preserves this tensor-product isomorphism. Additivity and duality in [F3] give \(c_1(L_{\chi_{\mathbf n}})=\sum_i n_i u_i\) over \(\mathbb R\) as well, since the real generators in [F1] are the coefficient images of the same tautological Euler classes. proof_steps.claim: If \(r=0\), \(BT\) is a point and the CW and paracompact assertions reduce to the compact manifold \(F\). For \(r\geq1\), [F1] gives \(BT\) its ordinary product CW topology, and [F3] makes it paracompact Hausdorff. By [F2], choose a finite CW complex \(K\) and a homotopy equivalence \(h:F\to K\). Since \(K\) is finite, its CW product with the CW complex \(BT\) has the ordinary product topology; hence \(BT\times K\) is a CW complex. The maps \(\mathrm{id}_{BT}\times h\) and the product of a homotopy inverse with \(\mathrm{id}_{BT}\) are homotopy inverses, since their coordinate homotopies are continuous in the product topology. Thus \(BT\times F\) has CW type. If \(F=\varnothing\), take \(K=\varnothing\).

If \(F=\varnothing\), the product is empty and paracompact Hausdorff, so assume \(F\ne\varnothing\). To prove paracompactness of \(BT\times F\), let \(\mathcal U\) be an open cover. For each \(x\in BT\) and \(y\in F\), choose a product neighborhood \(O_{x,y}\times V_{x,y}\) of \((x,y)\) contained in some member \(U_{x,y}\in\mathcal U\). Compactness of \(F\) selects finitely many \(y_1,\ldots,y_m\) whose \(V_{x,y_j}\) cover \(F\). Then \(O_x=\bigcap_{j=1}^m O_{x,y_j}\) is an open neighborhood of \(x\), and \(O_x\times F\) is covered by \(U_{x,y_1},\ldots,U_{x,y_m}\). Paracompactness of \(BT\) gives a locally finite open refinement \(\{W_\alpha\}\) of \(\{O_x\}\). For each \(\alpha\), choose \(x_\alpha\) with \(W_\alpha\subseteq O_{x_\alpha}\); the finitely many sets \((W_\alpha\times F)\cap U_{x_\alpha,y_j}\) cover \(W_\alpha\times F\), are open, and refine \(\mathcal U\). They are locally finite because a neighborhood \(N\times F\) meets sets indexed by only those \(\alpha\) for which \(W_\alpha\) meets \(N\), a finite set. Hence \(BT\times F\) is paracompact. It is Hausdorff as a product of Hausdorff spaces. The point and rank-zero cases satisfy the same conclusions.

The map $\nabla:W\to S^2$ extends over the cone on $\beta$ by the definition $\beta=\nabla\alpha$; hence it extends to a map $q:S^2\times S^2=W\cup_\alpha D^4\to C_\beta$. On $W$, $q$ is the fold into the bottom $S^2$ of $C_\beta$, so $q^*x=a+b$. On the open $4$-cell, the extension is the characteristic disk of $C_\beta$ with degree $+1$ by [A1], so $q^*y=ab$.

In the cone $C_\beta$, $x^2=H(\beta)y$ by [F1]. Pulling back with step 1.1 yields $(a+b)^2=H(\beta)ab$. Since $a^2=b^2=0$ and degree-two classes commute, the left side is $2ab$. The class $ab$ is a generator, so $H(\beta)=2$.

Let $i:W\hookrightarrow S^2\times S^2$ be the $2$-skeleton inclusion. The characteristic disk extends $i\alpha$ over $D^4$, so $\Sigma i\circ\Sigma\alpha$ is null. Define
$$r=(\Sigma p_1\vee\Sigma p_2)\circ\operatorname{pinch}:\Sigma(S^2\times S^2)\longrightarrow\Sigma S^2\vee\Sigma S^2,$$
where $p_1,p_2$ are the projections and the pinch is [F3]. On the first suspended wedge summand, the first projection branch is the identity up to linear rescaling of the suspension coordinate and the second branch is constant; on the second summand the roles reverse. Thus $r\circ\Sigma i\simeq\operatorname{id}_{\Sigma W}$. Applying $r$ to the nullhomotopy in the first sentence gives $\Sigma\alpha\simeq *$. Composing with $\Sigma\nabla$ gives $\Sigma\beta\simeq *$. By the definition of the suspension homomorphism, this is $2[\Sigma h]=0$ because $[\beta]=2[h]$ from step 2.1 and [F1] identifies $[h]$ as the generator.

proof_steps.claim: Write $\mathbb{CP}^2=\{[z_0:z_1:z_2]\}$ and use the open cell $z_2\ne0$ with representative $(w_0,w_1,1)$, $w\in\mathbb C^2$. Its characteristic disk can be taken as the unit ball in $\mathbb C^2$ via $w\mapsto[w_0:w_1:\sqrt{1-|w|^2}]$; the interior parametrizes the complement of $\mathbb{CP}^1$, and on $|w|=1$ the boundary map is $[w_0:w_1]=h(w)$. Thus $\mathbb{CP}^2$ is the mapping cone $C_h$. By [F4], the degree-two generator squares to the degree-four generator, so [F5] gives $H(h)=1$.

Let $d_m:S^3\to S^3$ have degree $m$. The radial cone extension $D^4\to D^4$, $ru\mapsto r d_m(u)$, has relative degree $m$ and boundary $d_m$: on collapsing the disk boundary its map is $\Sigma d_m$, whose degree is $m$ by the natural homology suspension in [F6]. Together with the identity on $S^2$, it defines a map $C_{h\circ d_m}\to C_h$, since the boundary attaching maps agree. It pulls the degree-two generator of $C_h$ back to that of $C_{h\circ d_m}$ and the degree-four generator back to $m$ times the latter. Pulling back $x_h^2=y_h$ therefore gives $x_{h\circ d_m}^2=m y_{h\circ d_m}$, which is exactly $H(h\circ d_m)=m$ by [F5].

The coefficient $H(f)$ is invariant under a based homotopy $H_t$ of attaching maps. A comparison $C_{f_0}\to C_{f_1}$ is the identity on $S^2$; on a cone point $[x,t]$ it equals $H_{2t}(x)$ for $0\le t\le1/2$ and the target cone point $[x,2t-1]$ for $1/2\le t\le1$. The formulas agree at the seam, respect the tip, and are continuous by quotient descent. Reversing the homotopy gives its homotopy inverse: the composites insert a path followed by its reverse, which contracts by shrinking its traversed homotopy parameter, and then a linear cone reparametrization removes the constant collar. Both maps restrict to the identity on the bottom sphere and have relative top-cell degree $+1$, so cup-product naturality preserves $H$. Since step 1.1 identifies every homotopy class with $[h\circ d_m]$ for a unique integer $m$, step 2.1 implies that any attachment with $H(f)=m$ has class $m[h]$.

proof_steps.claim: Consider any invariant open set \(W\subseteq V_j\cong T\times_{H_j}D(V_j^0)\). The Borel identification is the homeomorphism \([e,[t,w]]\mapsto[e\cdot t,w]\) from \(ET\times_T(T\times_{H_j}W_0)\) to \(ET\times_{H_j}W_0\), with inverse \([e,w]\mapsto[e,[1,w]]\); the quotient relations show both maps are well-defined. By [F4], \(ET\to B_H\) is locally a principal \(H\)-bundle: over a Milnor \(T\)-chart it has form \(U\times T\to U\times(T/H)\), and local sections of the Lie quotient \(T\to T/H\) give the principal \(H\)-charts. proof_steps.claim: For any given spin four-manifold the local quaternionic model glues by its specified Spin(4) lift. In that quaternionic spin model, right multiplication by a quaternionic unit $j$ is an antiunitary map $J_0$ on $S^+\oplus S^-$, with $J_0^2=-1$. It commutes with the four Clifford matrices and $\Gamma$ and is parallel: the transition and connection matrices act from the left and hence commute with right multiplication. The same operation $J_E$ on the $SU(2)$ twist is parallel, antiunitary and has square $-1$. Define $J_5=\Gamma J_0$ on the spin factor. Then $J_5^2=-1$, it anticommutes with each of the four tangent Clifford matrices, and it anticommutes with $c_5=i\Gamma$ because anti-linearity changes $i$ to $-i$. Thus it is the pseudoreal Spin(5) structure, since even products of Clifford matrices commute with it. On the complex tensor product set $J=J_5\otimes J_E$; it is well-defined and antiunitary, $J^2=1$, and $JD_5=-D_5J$. Hence $J$ preserves the kernel and $iD_5$ commutes with $J$.

Chirality anticommutes with $D_4$ and is parallel, so $D_5^2=D_4^2-\partial_t^2$. It has scalar positive principal symbol and smooth coefficients. Formal symmetry follows from unitary connection compatibility and periodic integration by parts. The same shifted-resolvent argument applies to $D_4$ and $D_5$ on a general compact background: each square has scalar positive principal symbol, and [F2] gives the inverse of its positive shift from $L^2$ to $H^2$; multiplying by $D_j\mp i$ gives surjectivity of $D_j\pm i$ and the $H^1$ selfadjoint domain exactly as in [F1]. An $L^2$ weak chiral cokernel vector also has square zero distributionally; testing against smooth sections and using their $H^2$ density puts it in the adjoint domain of the selfadjoint square, hence in $H^2$, and [F2] then makes it smooth. This justifies identifying the cokernel with the negative-chirality kernel. Weak kernels are smooth by the same argument. For a zero mode $\psi$, integration by parts gives $0=\|D_5\psi\|^2=\|D_4\psi\|^2+\|\partial_t\psi\|^2$. Thus $\psi$ is independent of $t$ and lies in $\ker D_4$; conversely every such spinor gives a periodic product zero mode. In general its complex dimension is $n_++n_-$, identifying the smooth negative-chirality kernel with the cokernel by the formal $L^2$ adjoint. For the concrete round twist this dimension is $1$ by [F1]. This avoids any unproved general spectral-flow identity.

The constant central automorphism acts by $-1$ on both chiral spinor kernels and cokernels, and fixes the background connection. Its scalar on the inverse determinant line is $(-1)^{-n_+}(-1)^{n_-}=(-1)^{n_+-n_-}$. For the actual round twist [F1] gives dimensions one and zero, hence scalar $-1$. Parallel transport along a constant path is the identity for any connection. Closing by the inverse endpoint identification gives $z_*^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}=-1$; tensor powers give $(-1)^N$. This is an actual finite-dimensional exterior-power action, not an assumption equating a periodic eta invariant with holonomy.

For any finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with anti-linear involution $J$, every $v$ has the unique decomposition $v=(v+Jv)/2+i(v-Jv)/(2i)$ with both displayed real components fixed by $J$. Thus $V=V^J\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ and $\dim_{\mathbb R}V^J=\dim_{\mathbb C}V$. Apply this to $V=\ker D_5$ using steps 1.1–1.2. The restriction of $iD_5$ is real and skew-adjoint, because $D_5$ is selfadjoint and $J(iD_5)=(iD_5)J$. Its real kernel has dimension $n_++n_-$. This has the same parity as $n_+-n_-$, since their difference is $2n_-$. For the concrete round twist the real dimension and parity are one by [F1].

Its exact GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form hypotheses are retained in the rank-one raw emptiness deduction. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition.

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step.

proof_steps.claim: On one \(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty}\) factor, apply [F5] with \(G=\mathbb Q\). Thus the rational ring is \(\mathbb Q[u_{\mathbb Q}]\), with \(|u_{\mathbb Q}|=2\).

Apply [F6] to the integral singular chain complex with \(G=\mathbb Q\). Each integral homology group in [F4] is free, so the Tor term vanishes and \(H_n(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty};\mathbb Q)\) is \(\mathbb Q\) for even \(n\) and zero for odd \(n\); it is finite free in every degree.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F5] The normal Thom class represents the oriented Poincaré dual, and integral projective cohomology is generated by the tautological Euler class; its negative is c₁(O(1)).
