Each fixed-point contribution is the reciprocal of its Euler product, so the degree-one coefficient is $E_1^{-1}+E_2^{-1}$. The TikZ drawing only records the two one-box colorings and is not used in this calculation.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] The preceding vanishing lemma reconstructs a three-term monad with dimensions $k,2k+N,k$ from the Ward bundle. [[lem-qftx-asd-twistor-vanishing-and-monad-reconstruction]]

proof_steps.claim: The reconstructed monad in [F1] is linear with locally free middle bundle, trivial on every real line, and has the positive Hermitian Ward pairing and unitary framing fixed in the definition. Its dimensions are those required by [A1]. Thus, assuming the exact supplier [A1], extract the raw tuple from its intrinsic normal form. Its monad composition vanishes, so [F5]'s polynomial identity makes both raw moment coefficients zero. Full fiber rank on each real line and [F5]'s Gram/rank equivalence identify the locus exactly with stable-and-costable regularity. The intrinsic unitary normalization and inverse-extraction clause in [A1] identify the remaining framed monad changes precisely with $(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ for $g\in U(k)$. The compact-rotation and framing chain maps are exactly those in [F5] and [A1]; first-order naturality is used only in [A1]’s locally-free/base-change range. No arbitrary analytic-family algebraization is inferred. No source-coordinate conjugation or nonexistent universal equivalence is invoked.

Conversely, the regular raw monad in [F5] is a global holomorphic bundle, trivial on every real line, with canonical positive reality: its pairing is induced by the standard Hermitian form on K and β(v)=α(σv)*. It is well-defined on cohomology since kerβ(v) is orthogonal to imα(σv), and on a real line its canonical representatives are kerD with the positive restricted metric; at infinity it is W. Apply the proved local Ward construction to obtain a global framed unitary ASD connection. On the finite chart it equals P d: for a kernel representative v along a D=ker(de) direction, β is constant, so its derivative lies in kerβ; the component of dv orthogonal to kerD lies in im a⊕im b, and β=f(−λ₂,λ₁) forces that component to lie in im(aλ₁+bλ₂)=imα. It therefore vanishes in monad cohomology, leaving exactly P dv. Thus evaluation identifies the projection and Ward connections; the Ward construction supplies the smooth extension and framing at infinity. The normalization of [F3] with determinant reduction [F4] gives k=c₂(E)[S⁴]=−q_N. Under [A1], extraction and construction are inverse on U(k) orbits and framed Ward connections, proving the full claim under the exact normal-form, GAGA and coupled-vanishing hypotheses stated above.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F7] Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch on $\mathbb P^3$ gives $\chi(F)=\int_{\mathbb P^3}\operatorname{ch}(F)\operatorname{td}(T\mathbb P^3)$ for the vector bundles and twists in this argument. [[thm-rr-for-projective-space-projections]]

proof_steps.claim: From [A3], $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E(t))=Ne^{tH}-kH^2e^{tH}$ and $\operatorname{td}(T_Z)=1+2H+\tfrac{11}{6}H^2+H^3$. Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch [F7] gives $\chi(\mathcal E(t))=N\binom{t+3}{3}-k(t+2)$, with values $k,-N+2k,0,-k$ for $t=-3,-4,-2,-1$. The Euler sequences $0\to\mathcal O(-4)\to\mathcal O(-3)^{\oplus4}\to\Omega_Z^2\to0$ and $0\to\Omega_Z^1(-1)\to\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus4}\to\mathcal O(-1)\to0$ give Euler characteristics $k,2k+N,k$ for the three monad coefficient bundles. Steps 1.2, 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1 leave only $H^2$ in each, so these values are the dimensions.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] The exact rank-two theorem supplies the ordinary framed ASD connection of a regular rank-two datum by its raw forward monad/projection construction, extends it smoothly over infinity, and proves $q_2=-k$. Its exact GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form hypotheses are retained in the rank-one raw emptiness deduction. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition.

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A2] For $N\ge2$, the zero-FI correspondence supplier identifies the stable-and-costable real quotient with the framed ordinary ASD sector having $q_N=-k$, preserving the specified orientation, unitary framing, compact torus action and exact first-order family qualifications. For $N=1$, the rank-one boundary lemma proves that both ordinary spaces are empty at $k>0$ and are the framed flat point at $k=0$, with compatible compact actions and an explicit first-order groupoid equivalence. Its stabilization proof retains the rank-two supplier's actual GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form prerequisites; it introduces no extra rank-one dictionary premise. The two suppliers therefore cover the ordinary dictionary for every $N\ge1$ under exactly those inherited hypotheses. Neither identifies the positive-FI resolution or its rank-one formal coefficients with ordinary ASD moduli. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]], [[lem-qftx-rank-one-regular-adhm-and-ordinary-asd-boundary]]

proof_steps.claim: For $N\ge2$, the source and target of [A2]'s rank-two-and-higher supplier agree with the zero-FI regular quotient and the framed ASD sector in the conditional dictionary, with $q_N=-k$ and identical framing and orientation. For $N=1$, stabilize by adding one unused framed line as in the boundary lemma: its moment equations, word stability and costability are unchanged. Its proved boundary identifies the two empty spaces at $k>0$ and the unique framed flat points at $k=0$, and its direct first-order gauge argument supplies the corresponding family identification rather than inferring it from an orbit-set bijection. Thus the ordinary dictionary has no uncovered rank-one case; its exact rank-two analytic and normal-form hypotheses remain inherited. This does not place any positive-FI partition fixed point in the open regular ordinary locus. In particular, the positive-FI one-box rank-one contribution is still the formal coefficient of step 1.1 and is not an ordinary positive-charge abelian instanton.

For $k>0$, use the tuple $Y_1=\{(i,0):0\leq i<k\}$ and $Y_\alpha=\varnothing$ for $\alpha>1$; step 1.1 constructs a stable datum. Replacing $B_1$ by $B_1+c\,\mathrm{id}_V$ preserves the complex equation and stability while changing $\operatorname{tr}(B_1)$ by $kc$ for every $c\in\mathbb C$. Trace is invariant under conjugation, so the descended trace function on the geometric quotient has image $\mathbb C$, which is not compact. Thus the quotient is noncompact. The completed Borel carrier matches the compact real-Borel interface in [L1]. The ADHM/monad comparisons in [A1]–[A2] retain their exact analytic and family hypotheses, while step 2.3 has supplied the precise intrinsic localized Borel–Moore pushforward covered by [F6].

fact_uses.text: [F1] The maximal bad cubes $Q_j$ (cubes with $|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|f|>\lambda$, maximal under inclusion) are countable, pairwise disjoint, have union $\{M_df>\lambda\}$, and satisfy $|Q_j|^{-1}\int_{Q_j}|f|\le2^n\lambda$ and $\sum_j|Q_j|\le\lambda^{-1}\|f\|_1$ ([[lem-maximal-dyadic-cubes-at-height-lambda]]).

proof_steps.claim: The functions $g$ and $b_j$ are measurable, $b_j$ is supported in $Q_j$, and $f=g+\sum_jb_j$ everywhere: on $Q_j$ the sum $g+\sum_kb_k$ has the single nonzero term $g+b_j=|Q_j|^{-1}\int_{Q_j}f+f-|Q_j|^{-1}\int_{Q_j}f=f$ by disjointness of the $Q_k$, while off $\bigcup_kQ_k$ one has $g=f$ and every $b_k=0$. Moreover $\int b_j=\int_{Q_j}f-|Q_j|^{-1}\int_{Q_j}f\,|Q_j|=0$ and $\|b_j\|_1\le\int_{Q_j}|f|+|Q_j|^{-1}\bigl|\int_{Q_j}f\bigr||Q_j|\le2\int_{Q_j}|f|\le2\cdot2^n\lambda|Q_j|=2^{n+1}\lambda|Q_j|$.

On each bad cube, $|g|=|Q_j|^{-1}\bigl|\int_{Q_j}f\bigr|\le|Q_j|^{-1}\int_{Q_j}|f|\le2^n\lambda$, so $|g|\le2^n\lambda$ on $\bigcup_jQ_j$; off $\bigcup_jQ_j$ one has $g=f$ and all dyadic cubes through $x$ are good, so the averages of $|f|$ over those cubes are at most $\lambda$. These cubes, indexed by generation and assigned to the parameter $r=2\sqrt n\,2^{-k}$ for the generation-$k$ cube through $x$ and extended constantly on $[2\sqrt n\,2^{-k},2\sqrt n\,2^{-k+1})$, shrink nicely to $x$ with a dimensional constant: each lies in $B(x,r)$ and has measure $2^{-kn}=c_n\lambda(B(x,2\sqrt n2^{-k}))$. Hence [F2] gives $|f(x)|\le\lambda$ for almost every $x\notin\bigcup_jQ_j$, and since $g=f$ there, $|g|\le\max(2^n\lambda,\lambda)=2^n\lambda$ almost everywhere.

From step 2.1, $\|g\|_1\le\int_{\bigcup Q_j}|g|+\int_{\mathbb R^n\setminus\bigcup Q_j}|f|\le\sum_j\int_{Q_j}|f|+\int_{\mathbb R^n\setminus\bigcup Q_j}|f|=\|f\|_1$, and $\|g\|_2^2=\int|g|^2\le\|g\|_\infty\int|g|\le2^n\lambda\|f\|_1$. Together with step 1.1 and the bounds $\sum_j|Q_j|\le\lambda^{-1}\|f\|_1$ and $|Q_j|^{-1}\int_{Q_j}|f|\le2^n\lambda$ from [F1], this is the asserted decomposition.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-qftx-taubes-arbitrary-divisor-plane-vortex]]: for each effective divisor there is a unique scalar $h$ with the stated logarithmic subtractions and decay; the reconstruction is smooth, solves the positive first-order equations, has finite energy, and has flux $2\pi$ times the degree. Negative winding follows by conjugation.

proof_steps.claim: Its multiplicities give degree $N=2+1=3$ and distributional source $4\pi(2\delta_{z_0}+\delta_{z_1})=8\pi\delta_{z_0}+4\pi\delta_{z_1}$. The center subtraction coefficients are $2m_0=4$ and $2m_1=2$. Applying [F2] gives the unique scalar $h$, its smooth subtractions, $h\to0$, and strict negativity away from the divisor.
Apply [F2] to the explicit effective divisor $|n|[0]$ of degree $|n|$ (the empty divisor if $n=0$) and conjugate when $n<0$. Its signed flux is $2\pi n$, and [F3] gives $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|$.

Here $P=(z-z_0)^2(z-z_1)$ and $s=2\log|P|$. The reconstruction in [F2] extends smoothly over both centers, solves the positive critical equations, and has flux $2\pi N=6\pi$. Since it is a fixed-divisor reconstructed solution, [F3] gives its attained absolute transverse energy $2\pi\xi N=6\pi\xi$. The argument determines the profile by the unique scalar boundary-value problem and supplies no elementary closed form.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F8] [[thm-interior-w-two-p-estimate-for-uniformly-elliptic-equations]]: for $p>2$ and $\Delta w=f\in L^p$ on a ball in $\mathbb R^2$, the $W^{2,p}$ norm on the concentric half-ball is bounded by the local $L^p$ norms of $f$ and $w$.

proof_steps.claim: On any smaller compact disk $K\Subset U$, [F8] applied on finitely many nested balls and the uniform $L^\infty$ bound of step 7.1 yields uniform $W^{2,p}$ bounds for $w_R$ for every finite $p>2$, since its Laplacian is bounded. For a prescribed $0<\alpha<1$, choose $p>2/(1-\alpha)$ and then $\beta$ with $\alpha<\beta<1-2/p$; [F6] gives a uniform $C^{1,\beta}$ bound on a slightly larger compact disk. As $e^s$ is smooth and $\Delta w_R=\kappa(e^s e^{w_R}-1)$, the right-hand side has a uniform $C^{0,\alpha}$ bound there; [F9] then yields a uniform $C^{2,\alpha}$ bound on $K$. These bounds are independent of $R$ and are the local compactness estimates used for disk exhaustion.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] For every effective divisor, the scalar Taubes problem has its unique smooth desingularized solution and reconstructs a smooth finite-energy critical connection/Higgs field with the prescribed zeros, flux, and exponential gauge-invariant decay; negative winding uses conjugation. [[thm-qftx-taubes-arbitrary-divisor-plane-vortex]]

proof_steps.claim: For each chosen effective divisor of degree $|n|$, apply [F3] with $e=g$ and $\xi=2v^2$, using its conjugate for negative n. [F4] fixes its finite energy and flux normalization. The polynomial phase correction relative to $n\theta$ is degree zero and tends to zero; the cutoff cleanup used in [F5] removes only this correction globally, preserving the divisor. The resulting embedded fields have a=p=0 and satisfy the appropriate critical equations, so all residuals in step 2.1 vanish and the full-model energy is exactly $T_n$. The same identity bounds every competing full-model profile below by $T_n$, proving absolute minimality. Compactly supported smooth variations preserve the flux/vacuum class, so differentiability of their energy at the minimum gives vanishing first variation. This proves actual existence and stationarity for every divisor, without a radial or unit-winding restriction.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F5] [[pthm-qftx-n2-linear-monopole-bps-vortex-bound]]: in the frozen-metric linear truncation, actual mathematical arbitrary-divisor vortices embed as stationary absolute full-model minima with $T_n=4\pi v^2|n|$; actual canonical full-model collars give $T_nL+O(1)$ for fixed-flux cylinder infima. Its nonlinear stationarity obstruction and screened dual-electric response keep this exact critical result separate from generic nonlinear confinement.

proof_steps.claim:
Under the additional vortex/minimization hypothesis in the Statement,
[F4] gives nonzero quantized original electric flux and a tension
$\sigma>0$. The interior of a translation-invariant tube of length $L$
contains the same transverse profile at each longitudinal coordinate, so
its bulk energy is $\sigma L$. The uniformly bounded endcap contribution
therefore gives $V(L)=\sigma L+O(1)$, which is linear confinement in this
effective model. This last conclusion is conditional: no preceding step establishes existence or minimization of the required profile. Original electric probes correspond to dual magnetic flux; the condensed original magnetic charges are dual electric charges and are screened in the linear response about the dual Higgs vacuum described by [F5]. This conclusion concerns classical effective energy, not a quantum Wilson-loop area law.

In the explicitly linear truncation, assume [A3] and apply [F5] with $\xi=2v^2$ to each chosen effective divisor of degree $|n|$. It supplies an actual smooth stationary full-model minimum of tension $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|=4\pi v^2|n|$, and actual finite collars from every fixed canonical full-model end trace in the stated valid neutral disk. Thus $T_nL\le I_L\le T_n(L-2\ell)+C_0+C_1$, proving $I_L=T_nL+O(1)$; matching minimizing traces attain $T_nL$ exactly. No solution or endcap existence is assumed for this critical boundary problem. The nonlinear obstruction in [F5] prevents extending its exact BPS assertion to generic u.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-qftx-taubes-arbitrary-divisor-plane-vortex]]: for every effective finite divisor of degree $|n|$ there is a smooth finite-energy planar critical pair with flux $2\pi n$ (using conjugation for $n<0$); for the empty divisor it is the vacuum. The local unwound exterior gauge has $q=\sqrt\xi e^{h/2}$ and $A=-\tfrac12*dh$; that degree-changing exterior gauge is not asserted to extend globally. Separately, removing only the smooth degree-zero polynomial phase correction relative to $n\theta$ by a global cutoff gauge yields the canonical winding representative $q=\sqrt\xi e^{h/2}e^{in\theta}$, $A=n\,d\theta-\tfrac12*dh$.

proof_steps.claim: For an end trace with exterior phase $n\theta+\phi$, choose a smooth radial cutoff $\eta$ which is zero on a disk containing the noncanonical region and one outside a larger disk. The real function $\chi=-\eta\phi$ extends smoothly by zero to the whole plane; the allowed gauge transformation $(q,A)\mapsto(e^{i\chi}q,A+d\chi)$ therefore makes the exterior phase exactly $n\theta$. This constructs the asserted degree-zero exterior phase cleanup without attempting to extend a degree-$n$ angular map across the disk. For the planar minimizer in [F2], write $P=|P|e^{i\vartheta}$ on the exterior; $\vartheta-n\theta$ is single-valued, smooth and tends to zero because $P(z)=z^n(1+O(|z|^{-1}))$ for $n\ge0$ (use the conjugate construction for $n<0$). Applying the same cutoff extension to $-(\vartheta-n\theta)$ changes its exterior fields to $q^*=\rho_*e^{in\theta}$ and $A^*=n\,d\theta-\tfrac12*dh$; hence $A^*-n\,d\theta$ decays exponentially.

In canonical exterior gauge write $q=\rho e^{in\theta}$ and $\alpha=A-n\,d\theta$. Directly, $D_Aq=e^{in\theta}(d\rho-i\rho\alpha)$, so the real and imaginary terms are orthogonal and $|D_Aq|^2=|d\rho|^2+\rho^2|\alpha|^2$. Uniform convergence gives $\rho\ge\sqrt\xi/2$ outside a disk; thus finite kinetic energy implies $\alpha\in L^2$ there. Also $|\rho-\sqrt\xi|\le |\rho^2-\xi|/\sqrt\xi$, so finite potential energy gives $\rho-\sqrt\xi\in L^2$ there. On compact disks all fields are smooth and bounded. Consequently, for any two cleaned end traces and the cleaned minimizer, differences of connections and Higgs fields are globally in $L^2$; each Higgs field is bounded.

Apply step 3.1 first to $p_0$ and $p_*$, defining its finite energy to be $C_0$, and then to $p_*$ and $p_1$, defining its finite energy to be $C_1$. For $L\ge2\ell$, place the first collar on $[0,\ell]$, the constant planar minimizer on $[\ell,L-\ell]$, and the second collar on $[L-\ell,L]$. The profiles match smoothly because the collar cutoff is constant near its ends. The middle has no longitudinal energy and contributes exactly $T_n(L-2\ell)$ by [F2]–[F3]. At $L=2\ell$ this middle interval has zero length; the two collars meet at the constant value $p_*$, so the same upper bound holds. This admissible concatenation proves $\inf\mathcal E_L\le C_0+T_n(L-2\ell)+C_1$.

Combining steps 1.1 and 4.1 gives $0\le\inf\mathcal E_L-T_nL\le C_0+C_1-2\ell T_n$ for every $L\ge2\ell$; the right side is a finite constant independent of $L$, proving the bounded-remainder conclusion. If $p_0=p_1=p_*$, the constant extension $(A_1,A_2,q)=(A^*,q^*)$, $A_3=0$, has energy $T_nL$ and satisfies the angular and no-leakage conditions. The lower bound from step 1.1 then proves it is an exact translation-invariant minimum.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-qftx-taubes-arbitrary-divisor-plane-vortex]]: for each effective finite divisor of degree $|n|$, the reconstructed smooth critical fields satisfy the corresponding first-order equations, have finite energy, and have flux $2\pi n$ with sign set by the orientation.

proof_steps.claim: For each fixed divisor, [F2] supplies a smooth pair satisfying the relevant first-order equations. Its square terms in step 1.1 vanish identically; the sequence estimates of steps 1.2–2.1 apply because [F2] gives finite energy and the same boundary sector. Hence its energy is exactly $2\pi\xi|n|$. The lower bound of step 3.1 applies to every admissible same-winding configuration, so this pair is an absolute transverse energy minimum, without radial or unit-winding assumptions.

Let $(a,\eta)$ be a smooth compactly supported variation of a minimizing pair, and set $A_t=A+ta$, $q_t=q+t\eta$; for any field expression $F$, define $\delta F:=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}F(A_t,q_t)$. For sufficiently small $t$, the fields remain in the same boundary sector; outside the compact support they equal the original fields. Thus the boundary-current limit in the disk identity is unchanged and the flux is unchanged by Stokes applied to $d a$. The energy along this variation is the constant $2\pi\xi|n|$ plus the squared $L^2$ norms of the two first-order residuals in step 1.1. Both residuals vanish at $t=0$; differentiating the squared norms gives $E'(0)=0$ and
$$E''(0)=2\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(|\delta(D_{A,1}\pm iD_{A,2})q|^2+\frac{|\delta(B\mp e^2(\xi-|q|^2))|^2}{2e^2}\right)dx_1dx_2\ge0,$$
with the upper signs for $n\ge0$ and lower signs for $n\le0$ (either choice when $n=0$). Therefore the first variation vanishes and no smooth compactly supported same-sector perturbation lowers the energy. Distinct divisors give distinct possible minimizing fields, so no cross-divisor uniqueness follows.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] [[thm-interior-w-two-p-estimate-for-uniformly-elliptic-equations]]: for $p>2$ on a two-dimensional ball, the interior $W^{2,p}$ norm is bounded by the local $L^p$ norms of the solution and its Laplacian.

proof_steps.claim: To obtain derivative decay, fix $\alpha<\alpha'<\sqrt\kappa$ and use step 3.3 at rate $\alpha'$. On each unit ball centered at large $z$, both $w$ and $\Delta w=\kappa(1-e^{-w})$ are $O(e^{-\alpha'|z|})$. By [F3] and [F5], $w$ has a $C^{1,\beta}$ norm of that order on the concentric half-ball for some $\beta>0$. Thus the right-hand side has a $C^{0,\beta}$ norm of the same order, and [F4] gives $C^{2,\beta}$ decay on a smaller ball. Inductively, for each multi-index $\gamma$, differentiating $\Delta w=\kappa(1-e^{-w})$ gives $\Delta D^\gamma w=\kappa e^{-w}D^\gamma w+G_\gamma$, where $G_\gamma$ is a finite sum of products of lower derivatives of $w$ and is exponentially small by the induction hypothesis. Applying [F3] and [F4] on nested unit balls gives the same $e^{-\alpha'|z|}$ bound for two more derivatives. Since $e^{-\alpha'|z|}\le e^{-\alpha|z|}$ outside a fixed disk, every finite derivative has the stated rate.

fact_uses.text: [F5] For $X=\mathbb P^n_k$ and every integer $d$ and every $q$ the evaluation pairing $H^q(X,\mathcal O(d))\times H^{n-q}(X,\mathcal O(-d-n-1))\to k$, $(\alpha,\eta)\mapsto t_X(\alpha\cup\eta)$, formed with the cup product for $\mathcal O(d)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathcal O(-d-n-1)\to\omega_X$, is a perfect pairing; for $q=0$ and $d\ge0$ it is the residue pairing of monomials, i.e. the coefficient of $(x_0\cdots x_n)^{-1}$, and it is compatible with multiplication by homogeneous polynomials. ([[thm-serre-duality-projective-space-twisting-sheaves]], [[lem-projective-space-top-cohomology-residue-pairing]], [[def-cup-product-sheaf-cohomology]])

proof_steps.claim: The case of a single twisting sheaf. Let $e\in\mathbb Z$ and put $d=-e-n-1$, so that $\omega_X(-e)=\mathcal O(-n-1-e)=\mathcal O(d)$ and $\mathcal O(-d-n-1)=\mathcal O(e)$. Under the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O(e),\omega_X)\cong\Gamma(X,\omega_X(-e))=H^0(X,\mathcal O(d))$ of [F9] a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal O(e)\to\omega_X$ corresponds to the global section $s$ giving multiplication by $s$, and the induced map $H^n(X,\varphi):H^n(X,\mathcal O(e))\to H^n(X,\omega_X)$ is the cup product $H^0(X,\mathcal O(d))\times H^n(X,\mathcal O(e))\to H^n(X,\omega_X)$ of [F12] with the global section $s$; this is the composite $H^n(X,\mathcal O(e))\to H^n(X,\mathcal O(d)\otimes\mathcal O(e))=H^n(X,\omega_X)$ under the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O(d)\otimes\mathcal O(e)\cong\omega_X$. Therefore $\Phi^0_{\mathcal O(e)}$ is, under these identifications, the pairing of [F5] in degree $q=0$ and with twist $e$, namely $H^0(X,\mathcal O(d))\times H^n(X,\mathcal O(-d-n-1))\to k$, which is perfect: for $d\ge0$ it is the residue pairing of [F5], and for $d<0$ both spaces are zero by [F6]. Hence $\Phi^0_{\mathcal O(e)}$ is an isomorphism for every $e$.

fact_uses.text: [F3] For $n\ge1$ and $d\ge0$ the pairing $H^0(\mathbb P^n_k,\mathcal O(d))\times H^n(\mathbb P^n_k,\mathcal O(-n-1-d))\to k$ given by the cup product for $\mathcal O(d)\otimes\mathcal O(-n-1-d)\to\mathcal O(-n-1)$ followed by $t_{\mathbb P^n}$, equivalently by the coefficient of $(x_0\cdots x_n)^{-1}$ in the product of monomials, is a perfect $k$-bilinear pairing, compatible with multiplication by homogeneous polynomials; for $n=0$ it is ordinary multiplication $k\times k\to k$. ([[lem-projective-space-top-cohomology-residue-pairing]])

proof_steps.claim: The case $q=0$. If $d\ge0$, this is precisely the perfect residue pairing of [F3]. If $d<0$, then $H^0(\mathcal O(d))=0$ by [F5], while $-d-n-1>-n-1$, so $H^n(\mathcal O(-d-n-1))=0$ by [F5]; the pairing of two zero spaces is perfect.

The case $q=n$. If $d\le-n-1$, put $d'=-d-n-1\ge0$. For $s\in H^0(\mathcal O(d'))$ and $\eta\in H^n(\mathcal O(-n-1-d'))$, [F3] identifies $t_{\mathbb P^n}(s\cup\eta)$ with the perfect residue pairing. The exchanged cup product $\eta\cup s$ has the same image: the section $s$ defines a sheaf map $\sigma_s:\mathbb Z_{\mathbb P^n}\to\mathcal O(d')$ and multiplication $\mu_s:\mathcal O(-n-1-d')\to\mathcal O(-n-1)$; naturality in [F2] applied to $\operatorname{id}\otimes\sigma_s$ and the right-unit class gives $\eta\cup s=H^n(\mu_s)(\eta)$, while the left-unit argument of [F3] gives $s\cup\eta=H^n(\mu_s)(\eta)$ because sheaf multiplication is commutative. Thus the exchanged pairing is perfect. If $d>-n-1$, then $H^n(\mathcal O(d))=0$ and $-d-n-1<0$ gives $H^0(\mathcal O(-d-n-1))=0$ by [F5], so the pairing is perfect vacuously.

The case $n=0$. By [F5], $\mathbb P^0_k=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and every twist has $H^0\cong k$ with no higher cohomology. The trace [F1] and degree-zero cup product [F2] make the pairing ordinary multiplication $k\times k\to k$, perfect with dual basis $1$, as also recorded in [F3].

Conclusion. Steps 1.1–1.5 cover bilinearity, the middle degrees, both extremes for $n\ge1$, and $n=0$. AC [F4] is inherited through the cup product [F2] and the projective-space cohomology and residue suppliers [F3, F5]; no additional selection is made.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-adhm-fixed-point-instanton-count]]: the fixed points for $N=1,k=1$ are indexed by the one one-box partition, and their tangent character is computed from the ADHM deformation complex.

proof_steps.claim: There is exactly one partition of $k=1$ for $N=1$, namely $Y_1=\{(0,0)\}$, so [F2] gives the unique fixed point. Here $\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=e_1$ and $\mathbf W=e_1^{-1}$, whence $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf V=1$, $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf W^\vee=1$, and $t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V=t_1t_2$. Substitution in the tangent character gives $t_1+t_2$; the two additive weights are $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$, so the Euler class is $\epsilon_1\epsilon_2$.

The degree-one coefficient is the sum over the single fixed point, so it equals $(\epsilon_1\epsilon_2)^{-1}$. This is a formal equivariant fixed-point contribution, not an asserted continuum path-integral value.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-adhm-fixed-point-instanton-count]]: fixed points are indexed by two-tuples of partitions of total size one, and the tangent character is $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf V(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V$.

proof_steps.claim: A two-tuple of partitions with total size one places its single box in exactly one of the two colors, so the only possibilities are $(\{(0,0)\},\varnothing)$ and $(\varnothing,\{(0,0)\})$. Their quotient representatives have $V$-characters $e_1$ and $e_2$, respectively.

For the first point, the ADHM convention [F1] gives $\mathbf W=e_1^{-1}+e_2^{-1}$ and $\mathbf W^\vee=e_1+e_2$, while $\mathbf V=e_1$. Substitution in [F2] gives $$t_1+t_2+\frac{e_2}{e_1}+t_1t_2\frac{e_1}{e_2}.$$ The corresponding additive weights are $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_2-a_1,\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2+a_1-a_2$, so their product is $E_1$. Interchanging the two colors gives the second displayed character and $E_2$.

Each fixed-point contribution is the reciprocal of its Euler product, so the degree-one coefficient is $E_1^{-1}+E_2^{-1}$. The TikZ drawing only records the two one-box colorings and is not used in this calculation.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] Stable data yield the stated framed monad, and its sheaf is locally free exactly for costable data. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: At zero real level, $J=0$ still follows from $I\ne0$ and $IJ=0$, while the real equation becomes $|I|^2=0$. This contradicts $I\ne0$, so the stable zero-level locus is empty. In the positive chamber, $J=0$ makes all of $V$ a nonzero invariant subspace in $\ker J$; the data are not costable. By [F3], their framed sheaves are not locally free.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] The ADHM-to-monad construction uses source $V\mathcal O(-1)$, middle $(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O$, target $V\mathcal O(1)$, and the displayed Hilbert polynomial. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Substituting $V=0$ into the monad leaves $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its kernel at the right is $W\mathcal O$ and the image at the left is zero, so the middle cohomology is canonically $W\mathcal O$. Restriction to $L_\infty$ is the identity framing on the prescribed basis of $W$. Since $\chi(\mathcal O(m))=\binom{m+2}{2}$, its Hilbert polynomial is $N\binom{m+2}{2}$, the case $k=0$ of [F2]. No Euler-block or empty-matrix convention changes these calculations.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] For a stable complex datum the framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad has maps $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0B_2+z_2,z_0B_1-z_1,z_0I)$, and its middle cohomology is a framed torsion-free sheaf; local freeness is equivalent to costability. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Substituting that representative in [F3] gives $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ and $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,z_0)$. Their product is $-z_2z_1+z_1z_2=0$. The row $\beta$ is surjective at every projective point because its three entries have no common zero, and $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map because it is nonzero away from $p$. Let $K=\ker\beta$. Projection to the third coordinate restricts to a morphism $\gamma:K\to\mathcal O$. On the affine chart $z_0=1$, put $x=z_1$ and $y=z_2$; a vector in $K$ has the form $(u,v,-yu+xv)$, so $\gamma(K)=(x,y)$ and its kernel is generated by $(-x,-y,0)$, the image of $\alpha$. On any chart away from $p$ where $z_1$ or $z_2$ is a unit, the same equations show that $\gamma$ is onto and its kernel is generated by $\alpha$. Hence $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha\cong I_p$ globally, where $I_p$ is the ideal sheaf of $p$.

At $p$, the local ideal $(x,y)$ is not principal: if it were generated by one element in the regular local ring $\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x,y)}$, its quotient by the maximal ideal would have dimension at most one, whereas $(x,y)/(x,y)^2$ has dimension two. Therefore $I_p$ is not locally free at $p$. Its framing on $L_\infty$ is the canonical trivialization because $p\notin L_\infty$. This exhibits a positive-FI stable point outside the costable, locally-free zero-FI locus; the correspondence with ordinary ASD moduli is restricted to that zero-FI locus and does not absorb this boundary point.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] The preceding vanishing lemma reconstructs a three-term monad with dimensions $k,2k+N,k$ from the Ward bundle. [[lem-qftx-asd-twistor-vanishing-and-monad-reconstruction]]

proof_steps.claim: The reconstructed monad in [F1] is linear with locally free middle bundle, trivial on every real line, and has the positive Hermitian Ward pairing and unitary framing fixed in the definition. Its dimensions are those required by [A1]. Thus, assuming the exact supplier [A1], extract the raw tuple from its intrinsic normal form. Its monad composition vanishes, so [F5]'s polynomial identity makes both raw moment coefficients zero. Full fiber rank on each real line and [F5]'s Gram/rank equivalence identify the locus exactly with stable-and-costable regularity. The intrinsic unitary normalization and inverse-extraction clause in [A1] identify the remaining framed monad changes precisely with $(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ for $g\in U(k)$. The compact-rotation and framing chain maps are exactly those in [F5] and [A1]; first-order naturality is used only in [A1]’s locally-free/base-change range. No arbitrary analytic-family algebraization is inferred. No source-coordinate conjugation or nonexistent universal equivalence is invoked.

Conversely, the regular raw monad in [F5] is a global holomorphic bundle, trivial on every real line, with canonical positive reality: its pairing is induced by the standard Hermitian form on K and β(v)=α(σv)*. It is well-defined on cohomology since kerβ(v) is orthogonal to imα(σv), and on a real line its canonical representatives are kerD with the positive restricted metric; at infinity it is W. Apply the proved local Ward construction to obtain a global framed unitary ASD connection. On the finite chart it equals P d: for a kernel representative v along a D=ker(de) direction, β is constant, so its derivative lies in kerβ; the component of dv orthogonal to kerD lies in im a⊕im b, and β=f(−λ₂,λ₁) forces that component to lie in im(aλ₁+bλ₂)=imα. It therefore vanishes in monad cohomology, leaving exactly P dv. Thus evaluation identifies the projection and Ward connections; the Ward construction supplies the smooth extension and framing at infinity. The normalization of [F3] with determinant reduction [F4] gives k=c₂(E)[S⁴]=−q_N. Under [A1], extraction and construction are inverse on U(k) orbits and framed Ward connections, proving the full claim under the exact normal-form, GAGA and coupled-vanishing hypotheses stated above.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F5] On $\mathbb P^3$, Serre duality identifies $H^q(F)^*$ with $\operatorname{Ext}^{3-q}(F,\mathcal O(-4))$; for locally free $F$ this is $H^{3-q}(F^*(-4))$. [[thm-serre-duality-projective-space-coherent-sheaves]]

proof_steps.claim: Let $L\cong\mathbb P^1$ be any real twistor line. Its normal bundle in $\mathbb P^3$ is $\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$, and the conormal sequence splits because its extension group is $H^1(\mathcal O(1))^{\oplus2}=0$. Hence $\Omega_Z^1|_L\cong\mathcal O(-2)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}$ and $T_Z|_L\cong\mathcal O(2)\oplus\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$. Since $\Omega_Z^2\cong T_Z(-4)$, each of $\mathcal E(-1)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-3)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-2)|_L$, $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))|_L$, and $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)|_L$ is a sum of negative line bundles. The Serre-dual bundles restrict respectively to $\mathcal E^*(-3)$, $\mathcal E^*(-1)$, $\mathcal E^*(-2)$, $\mathcal E^*\otimes T_Z(-3)$, and $\mathcal E^*\otimes\Omega_Z^1$, also sums of negative line bundles. Every point of $Z$ lies on a real line, so negativity on every such line makes every global section zero. Thus [F6] gives $H^0(Z,F)=0$ and [F5] gives $H^3(Z,F)=0$ for all the listed coefficient bundles $F$.

Tensor $0\to\Omega_Z^1(-1)\to\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus4}\to\mathcal O(-1)\to0$ by $\mathcal E$. Step 1.2 gives $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=H^0(\mathcal E(-1))=0$, and step 1.1 gives $H^1(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. The long exact sequence yields $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))=0$. Serre duality and step 1.1 also give $H^2(\mathcal E(-2))=0$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F4] For coherent $\mathcal F$ on $\mathbb P^2$, $H^2(\mathcal F)^*\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal O(-3))$, with the coherent-sheaf Ext interpretation. [[thm-serre-duality-projective-space-coherent-sheaves]]

proof_steps.claim: A nonzero section of $\mathcal E(-d)$ for $d=1,2$ would give a rank-one subsheaf of $\mathcal E$ whose determinant has degree at least $d>0$, contrary to step 2.1. Hence $H^0(\mathcal E(-1))=H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. A nonzero map $\mathcal E\to\mathcal O(-d)$ for $d=1,2$ would have a torsion-free image that is a quotient of $\mathcal E$ of slope at least zero: its kernel is a subsheaf of the slope-zero semistable sheaf, so has degree at most zero, while $\deg\mathcal E=0$. The same image is a subsheaf of $\mathcal O(-d)$ of degree at most $-d$. This is impossible. By coherent Serre duality [F4], these Hom vanishings give $H^2(\mathcal E(-1))=H^2(\mathcal E(-2))=0$.

Serre duality identifies $H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)^*$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal E,T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3))$. The twisted Euler sequence is $0\to\mathcal O(-3-d)\to\mathcal O(-2-d)^3\to T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3-d)\to0$. For $d\ge-1$, both $H^0$ terms on the left vanish and $H^1(\mathcal O(-3-d))=0$ by [F5], hence $H^0(T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3-d))=0$. Any rank-one torsion-free subsheaf of $T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3)$ of degree at least $-1$ would extend by double dual to a nonzero map $\mathcal O(d)\to T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3)$ for some $d\ge-1$, a contradiction. Thus $T_{\mathbb P^2}(-3)$ is stable of slope $-3/2$. A nonzero map from the slope-zero semistable $\mathcal E$ to this stable sheaf would have image both a quotient of slope at least zero and a subsheaf of negative slope, impossible. Consequently $H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=0$. From the Euler sequence and the Hilbert polynomial, $\chi(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=3\chi(\mathcal E(-1))-\chi(\mathcal E)=-(2k+N)$, so $h^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=2k+N$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] The exact rank-two theorem supplies the ordinary framed ASD connection of a regular rank-two datum by its raw forward monad/projection construction, extends it smoothly over infinity, and proves $q_2=-k$. Its exact GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form hypotheses are retained in the rank-one raw emptiness deduction. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition.

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] The exact framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad theorem gives the stable-data/framed torsion-free-sheaf correspondence, with rank $N\ge1$, Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, framing character $\sum e_\alpha^{-1}$, inverse extraction, and tangent correspondence in its stated locally-free/base-change family range. Combined with the finite real/complex quotient theorem, its positive-FI clause has the quotient used here. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: The quotient in [A1] has exactly the raw equation, stability, dual framing representation, rank and Hilbert polynomial of the Statement. Its normalized construction is equivariant for those framing and rotation characters, and the first-order family clause identifies tangent representations in its stated base-change range. Thus [A1] transfers the fixed-point bijection and tangent characters of step 1.1 to the Gieseker space.

For $k>0$, use the tuple $Y_1=\{(i,0):0\leq i<k\}$ and $Y_\alpha=\varnothing$ for $\alpha>1$; step 1.1 constructs a stable datum. Replacing $B_1$ by $B_1+c\,\mathrm{id}_V$ preserves the complex equation and stability while changing $\operatorname{tr}(B_1)$ by $kc$ for every $c\in\mathbb C$. Trace is invariant under conjugation, so the descended trace function on the geometric quotient has image $\mathbb C$, which is not compact. Thus the quotient is noncompact. The completed Borel carrier matches the compact real-Borel interface in [L1]. The ADHM/monad comparisons in [A1]–[A2] retain their exact analytic and family hypotheses, while step 2.3 has supplied the precise intrinsic localized Borel–Moore pushforward covered by [F6].

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F5] The coherent-sheaf Serre pairing for $H^2$ and the projective twisting-sheaf cohomology have the exact P² hypotheses used here. [[thm-serre-duality-projective-space-coherent-sheaves]], [[thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves]]

proof_steps.claim: Conversely, let $\mathcal E$ be a framed torsion-free sheaf with the stated Hilbert polynomial. The preceding Beilinson lemma constructs its monad, with terms $V_1\mathcal O(-1)$, $M\mathcal O$, and $V_2\mathcal O(1)$ of ranks $k,2k+N,k$. Its restriction to $L_\infty$ remains exact at the ends because $\mathcal E$ is locally free there. Put $K=\ker\beta|_{L_\infty}$. The sequence $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to W\mathcal O\to0$ splits since $\operatorname{Ext}^1(W\mathcal O,V_1\mathcal O(-1))=V_1\otimes W^*\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$.

The remaining line extension $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\oplus W\mathcal O\to M\mathcal O\to V_2\mathcal O(1)\to0$ has class in $\operatorname{Hom}(V_2,V_1)\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$, since $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$. Twist by $\mathcal O(-1)$ and take cohomology. The connecting map $V_2\to V_1\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$ is an isomorphism: the adjacent groups $H^0(\mathcal O(-1))$ and $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))$ vanish, while $H^1(\mathcal O(-2))\cong\mathbb C$. Thus $V_2$ is identified with $V_1$ by this canonical extension class. Choosing a basis of $V_1$ and using the fixed framed basis of $W$ identifies $M=V\oplus V\oplus W$ and the line maps with the two Euler blocks in the Statement. Any other such choice differs by one simultaneous element of $GL(V)$.

On $L_\infty$, the complex is $0\to V\mathcal O_{L_\infty}(-1)\xrightarrow{(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T}(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O_{L_\infty}\xrightarrow{(z_2,-z_1,0)}V\mathcal O_{L_\infty}(1)\to0$. The first two $V$ summands form the Euler resolution of the zero sheaf on the line, while the $W$ summand passes unchanged to middle cohomology. The framing is therefore the canonical identification $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}=W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. In the Grothendieck group, the monad gives $[\mathcal E]=[(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O]-[V\mathcal O(-1)]-[V\mathcal O(1)]$. Taking Euler characteristics after twisting by $\mathcal O(m)$ and using $\chi(\mathcal O(d))=\binom{d+2}{2}$ yields $\chi(\mathcal E(m))=N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$.

If $k=0$, $V=0$, all four maps and both equations are the unique zero-dimensional maps, stability and costability are vacuous, and the monad is $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its middle cohomology is the framed bundle $W\mathcal O$ with Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}$. Conversely, [F3] constructs this same zero-term monad from every framed sheaf with that polynomial, so the framing identifies each such sheaf with $W\mathcal O$. Thus both moduli spaces are points, and all empty-matrix and Euler-block conventions are satisfied.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A2] The current framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad carrier identifies stable complex ADHM data with framed torsion-free sheaves of rank $N$ and Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and identifies costability with local freeness; its family and tangent clause requires the stated relative base-change maps. Its analytic dictionary uses the exact GAGA comparison in [A3]. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: By [A2], every stable complex orbit gives one framed torsion-free $\mathbb P^2$ sheaf with the stated rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial, and the converse recovers the same orbit. Its locally-free locus is exactly the costable locus. Thus restricting [A1]'s complex quotient to regular orbits gives exactly that locally-free sheaf locus; the positive-FI stable quotient still contains the non-locally-free boundary. The family and first-order version is conditional on [A2]'s displayed base-change hypotheses and [A3], so no tangent claim is inferred outside that range.

The finite-dimensional quotient and $\mathbb P^2$ sheaf maps are $T$-equivariant by [A1]–[A2]. The Ward construction is natural under rotations and framing transformations by [A4]; the exact raw monad torus factors are directly calculated in the new block lemma cited by [A5], while the equivariance of inverse normalization remains part of [A5]. These exact interfaces make the composite $T$-equivariant. The same composition on first-order families is valid only under the base-change hypotheses of [A2]–[A4] and the deformation compatibility of [A5]. This proves the stated conditional torus and tangent clauses and leaves the positive-FI boundary separate.

fact_uses.text: [L3] Proper pushforward of a closed point $x$ to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $[\kappa(x):k]$ times the fundamental class of the point, by the norm-degree definition ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]], [[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]]).

proof_steps.claim: Independence. Fix $d$ with $0\le d\le n$ and let $c_1=c_1(\mathcal O(1))\cap-$; by [L2] the iterated cap $c_1^d$ maps $A_m(\mathbb P^n)$ to $A_{m-d}(\mathbb P^n)$, is additive, and is defined by cutting with $d$ coordinate hyperplanes in general position. On the linear subspace $\mathbb P^d$, the $d$ coordinate hyperplanes cut it in a single $k$-rational point, so $c_1^d[\mathbb P^d]=[\mathbb P^0]$, and the degree homomorphism $\deg:A_0(\mathbb P^n)\to\mathbb Z$ of [L3] sends $[\mathbb P^0]$ to $1$; hence $\deg\circ c_1^d$ is a homomorphism $A_d(\mathbb P^n)\to\mathbb Z$ sending the generator $[\mathbb P^d]$ of step 2.1 to $1$. A cyclic group admitting a homomorphism onto $\mathbb Z$ with generator mapping to $1$ is infinite cyclic, so $A_d(\mathbb P^n)=\mathbb Z\cdot[\mathbb P^d]$.

The degree isomorphism and closed points. By steps 2.1 and 3.1, $A_0(\mathbb P^n)$ is generated by $[\mathbb P^0]$ for a $k$-rational point; for a closed point $x$ with residue field $\kappa(x)$, proper pushforward to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is multiplication by $[\kappa(x):k]$ by [L3], so $[x]=[\kappa(x):k][\mathbb P^0]$ and $\deg$ is the stated isomorphism; a $0$-cycle supported on $k$-rational points has class $(\sum_xm_x)[\mathbb P^0]$. The computation over $\mathbb C$ is the classical cellular decomposition under the same identification.

fact_uses.text: [L2] The closed immersion $j$ is proper, so $j_*$ is defined on cycles and descends to Chow groups; the open immersion $u$ is flat of relative dimension $0$, so $u^*$ is restriction of cycles ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]], [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]]).

proof_steps.claim: Localization. The composite $u^*j_*$ is zero because a cycle supported on $Z$ restricts to zero on $U$. Every integral closed $V\subseteq U$ is a dense open subscheme of its closure $\overline V\subseteq T$, with the same function field, so $u^*[\overline V]=[V]$ and $u^*$ is surjective. If a cycle $\alpha$ represents a class whose restriction to $A_*(U)$ is zero, then as cycles on $U$ it is a finite (or locally finite) sum $$u^*\alpha=\sum_a(i_{V_a})_*\operatorname{div}_{V_a}(r_a).$$ The functions extend to the same function fields on the closures $\overline V_a$, and their divisors restrict to the displayed divisors on $U$. Hence $$\gamma=\alpha-\sum_a(i_{\overline V_a})_*\operatorname{div}_{\overline V_a}(r_a)$$ restricts to the zero cycle on $U$ and is supported on $Z$. The family of closures is locally finite: for every affine open $N\subseteq T$, the open $N\cap U$ is quasi-compact because $N$ is noetherian; a locally finite family meets a quasi-compact open in only finitely many members, and if $N$ meets $\overline V_a$, then openness of $N$ implies it meets $V_a$. Thus only finitely many closures meet each such $N$, and $\gamma=j_*\gamma_Z$ for a (locally finite) cycle $\gamma_Z$ on $Z$. This proves exactness in the middle, also for locally finite cycles.

fact_uses.text: [L3] Proper pushforward of cycles is functorial under composition and shifts degrees by the dimension difference; flat pullback is functorial and preserves codimension ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]], [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]]).

proof_steps.claim: Agreement with flat pullback. If $f$ is flat, apply the regular-immersion/smooth-projection identity of [L2] to $\Gamma_f:X\hookrightarrow X\times_kY$ followed by $\operatorname{pr}_Y:X\times_kY\to Y$. Its composite is $f$, flat of relative dimension $\dim X-\dim Y$, so the identity gives $\Gamma_f^!\operatorname{pr}_Y^*=f^*$ for the flat pullback; hence $f^*$ agrees with the flat pullback of [L3] on classes of the stated dimensions.

Proper pushforward. If $f$ is proper, [L3] gives functoriality $(gf)_*=g_*f_*$ and the codimension shift $\dim Y-\dim X$ on nonzero cycle classes, since a proper pushforward of a $p$-dimensional class is supported on images of dimension at most $p$ and the norm-degree formula is multiplicative in towers. The projection formula is the corresponding statement of [L1], with the identification $A^p=A_{\dim-p}$: writing $\alpha=c[Y]$ in operational form, $f_*(c\beta)=c\,f_*\beta$ is the proper axiom of bivariant classes, which is exactly $f_*(f^*\alpha\,\beta)=\alpha\,f_*\beta$.

fact_uses.text: [L5] Proper pushforward of cycles descends to Chow groups and if $i:Z\to X$ is a closed immersion then $i_*$ is the induced map on cycles ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]).

proof_steps.claim: Localization. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion and $i:Z=X\setminus U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary reduced closed subscheme. A cycle supported on $Z$ restricts to zero. Every integral closed $V\subseteq U$ is a dense open subscheme of its closure $\overline V\subseteq X$, with the same function field, so $j^*[\overline V]=[V]$ and restriction is surjective. If a cycle $\alpha$ represents a class restricting to zero, then as cycles on $U$ it is a finite (or locally finite) sum $\sum_a(i_{V_a})_*\operatorname{div}_{V_a}(r_a)$. The functions extend to the same function fields on the closures $\overline V_a$, and their divisors restrict to the stated divisors on $U$. Hence $$\gamma=\alpha-\sum_a(i_{\overline V_a})_*\operatorname{div}_{\overline V_a}(r_a)$$ restricts to the zero cycle on $U$ and is supported on $Z$. The family of closures is locally finite: for every affine open $N\subseteq X$, the open $N\cap U$ is quasi-compact because $N$ is noetherian. A locally finite family meets a quasi-compact open in only finitely many members, and if $N$ meets $\overline V_a$, then the open set $N$ meets $V_a$. Thus only finitely many closures meet each such $N$. Hence $\gamma=i_*\gamma_Z$ for a (locally finite) cycle on $Z$, proving exactness in the middle.

fact_uses.text: [L3] Proper pushforward and flat pullback of the relevant degrees, and the fact that a line bundle $L$ has $\mathbb P(L)\cong T'$ with $\xi=c_1(L)$ ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]], [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]], [[def-projective-bundle-scheme]], [[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]).

proof_steps.claim: Definition by the projective bundle relation. For rank zero set $c_0=1$ and all positive Chern operators to zero; the Whitney and section assertions in this case are identities, and no projective bundle of rank zero is used. Assume now $r\ge1$. For every base change $T'\to T$ and every class $\alpha\in A_m(T')$, expand $\xi^r\cap\pi^*\alpha=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}\xi^j\cap\pi^*\beta_j$ with $\beta_j\in A_{m-r+j}(T')$, which exists and is unique by [L1], and define $c_i(E)\cap\alpha:=(-1)^{i+1}\beta_{r-i}$ for $1\le i\le r$; explicitly the defining relation is $\sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^j\xi^{r-j}\cap\pi^*(c_j(E)\cap\alpha)=0$, with $c_0=1$ and $c_j=0$ for $j>r$ by convention. All terms have the same dimension, so the relation determines the $c_j(E)\cap\alpha$ uniquely by the basis part of [L1]. For a line bundle $L$, $\mathbb P(L)=T'$ and the relation reads $\xi\cap\alpha-c_1(L)\cap\alpha=0$, giving $c(L)=1+c_1(L)$ by [L3].

fact_uses.text: [L2] Proper pushforward of cycles is the norm-degree pushforward on integral cycles and descends to Chow groups; flat pullback of cycles is defined for flat morphisms of pure relative dimension $n$ and descends to Chow groups ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]], [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]]).

proof_steps.claim: Proper pushforward of the cycle of a sheaf. Let $\mathcal F$ be coherent on $X$ with support of dimension at most $d$. Then $f_*[\mathcal F]_d=[f_*\mathcal F]_d$ in $Z_d(Y)$. Indeed, let $\eta$ be the generic point of a $d$-dimensional component of $\operatorname{Supp}(f_*\mathcal F)$; every point of $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F$ mapping to $\eta$ is generic in a $d$-dimensional support component, because otherwise its closure would have dimension less than $d$ and map onto a neighbourhood of $\eta$ of dimension $d$, which is impossible; hence the fibre of the support over $\eta$ is finite. Give that support the closed scheme structure defined by $\operatorname{Ann}\mathcal F$; $\mathcal F$ is a coherent sheaf on this closed subscheme. Its restricted morphism to $Y$ is proper and is quasi-finite over $\eta$, so after removing the closed image of its non-quasi-finite locus it is finite near $\eta$ by [L3]. Then $(f_*\mathcal F)_\eta\cong\bigoplus_{\xi\mapsto\eta}\mathcal F_\xi$ is a finite module of finite length over the local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$, and a composition series over each local ring gives $\ell_{\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}}((f_*\mathcal F)_\eta)=\sum_{\xi\mapsto\eta}[\kappa(\xi):\kappa(\eta)]\ell_{\mathcal O_{X,\xi}}(\mathcal F_\xi)$, with the residue degree weights because the simple factors of $\mathcal F_\xi$ acquire composition factors of $\kappa(\xi)$ over $\kappa(\eta)$; comparing with the norm-degree definition of $f_*[\mathcal F]_d$ proves the identity. If the image of a component has dimension less than $d$, both $d$-cycles vanish at that component.

Flat pullback of the cycle of a sheaf. For $\mathcal F$ coherent on $Y$ supported in dimension at most $d$ one has $g^*[\mathcal F]_d=[g^*\mathcal F]_{d+n}$ in $Z_{d+n}(Y')$: at a generic point $\xi$ of a top-dimensional component of the preimage of its support, with $\eta=g(\xi)$, the stalk of $g^*\mathcal F$ is $\mathcal F_\eta\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}}\mathcal O_{Y',\xi}$. Tensoring a composition series of the finite-length module $\mathcal F_\eta$ with this flat local algebra shows that its length is $\ell_{\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}}(\mathcal F_\eta)\,\ell_{\mathcal O_{Y',\xi}}(\mathcal O_{Y',\xi}/\mathfrak m_\eta\mathcal O_{Y',\xi})$. The second factor is the generic fibre multiplicity and can exceed one for a nonreduced fibre.

Compatibility on cycles. Apply steps 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 to $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_V$ for an integral closed subscheme $V\subseteq X$ of dimension $d$: $g^*f_*[V]=g^*[f_*\mathcal O_V]_d=[g^*f_*\mathcal O_V]_{d+n}=[f'_*g'^*\mathcal O_V]_{d+n}=f'_*[g'^*\mathcal O_V]_{d+n}=f'_*g'^*[V]$, where the middle equality is step 1.3 applied to the quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal O_V$ and the outer equalities are steps 1.1 and 1.2; the finite-support and locally finite cases are handled by the same identities term by term. Since both sides are additive, $g^*f_*=f'_*g'^*$ on cycles and therefore on Chow groups by [L2].

fact_uses.text: [F3] For a finite extension of one-dimensional local domains, the norm-order formula computes the order of a norm, with residue-field degree weights ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]).

proof_steps.claim: Multiplier identities. Let $M$ be a finite module over a Noetherian local ring, with commuting endomorphisms $a,b,x$, $abM=0$, finite-length $x$-power torsion, and $M/xM$ supported at the closed point. Removing that torsion leaves $x$ injective, so $\ker(xa)=\ker a$ and the exact sequence $0\to aM/xaM\to\ker b/xaM\to\ker b/aM\to0$ gives $e(M,xa,b)=e(M,a,b)-e(aM,0,x)$; the same argument gives $e(M,a,xb)=e(M,a,b)+e(bM,0,x)$. If $N$ is supported at the closed point and a height-one prime $q$ of a two-dimensional local domain $R$, with $x\notin q$, then $$e_R(N,0,x)=\ell_{R_q}(N_q)\operatorname{ord}_{R/q}(x).$$ Indeed, additivity and a finite filtration by powers of $q$ reduce to a finite module over the one-dimensional local domain $R/q$; its finite-length torsion contributes zero by step 1.1. The torsion-free quotient is a full lattice of rank $h=\ell_{R_q}(N_q)$, and there $e(N,0,x)=\ell(N/xN)=\operatorname{ord}_{R/q}(\det(x\operatorname{id}))=h\operatorname{ord}_{R/q}(x)$ by the lattice-index calculation in [F3]. Now let $M$ also satisfy $M_q\cong R_q/(\pi^{e+f})$ and $a=u\pi^e$, $b=v\pi^f$ in $R_q$, with $\pi$ a uniformizer and $u,v$ units. The nilpotent identity gives $e(M,\pi^e,\pi^f)=0$, while $\pi^eM$ and $\pi^fM$ have generic lengths $f$ and $e$. If $\pi,u,v\in R$, the multiplier identities yield $$e_R(M,a,b)=-f\operatorname{ord}_{R/q}(u)+e\operatorname{ord}_{R/q}(v)=-\operatorname{ord}_{R/q}((-1)^{ef}u^fv^{-e}).$$ For parameters initially in $R_q$, first replace $\pi,u,v$ by $c\pi,c^{-e}u,c^{-f}v$ for some $c\in R\setminus q$ so $c\pi\in R$, then choose $d\in R\setminus q$ with $du,dv\in R$ and apply the formula to $da,db$. The multiplier identities account for the factors $e_R(aM,0,d)$ and $e_R(bM,0,d)$, whose generic lengths are $f$ and $e$; these are exactly the order correction from scaling the tame symbol by $d^{f-e}$. Thus the formula also holds for the original $a,b\in R$.

The non-normal case. For general $A$, let $B$ be the finite normalization of $A$, a semilocal normal Noetherian domain by [F1], with maximal ideals $\mathfrak n$ and residue fields $\kappa(\mathfrak n)$ finite over $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$. By step 4.1 applied to each local factor $B_{\mathfrak n}$, $\sum_{Q\subseteq\mathfrak n}\operatorname{ord}_{(B/Q)_{\mathfrak n}}(\partial_Q(f,g))=0$ for the height-one primes $Q$ of $B$ inside $\mathfrak n$; multiplying by $[\kappa(\mathfrak n):\kappa(\mathfrak m)]$ and summing over $\mathfrak n$, the norm-order formula of [F3] identifies the sum over the height-one primes $Q$ above a fixed height-one prime $q$ of $A$ with $\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}\bigl(\prod_{Q\mid q}N_{\kappa(Q)/\kappa(q)}\partial_Q(f,g)\bigr)$, which is the normalizing definition of $\partial_q(f,g)$. Hence the weighted sum of the local identities is exactly $\sum_q\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}(\partial_q(f,g))=0$. Since $\partial_q$ and $\operatorname{ord}_{A/q}$ are bimultiplicative in $f$ and $g$, writing $f$ and $g$ as quotients of elements of $A$ extends the identity from elements to arbitrary $f,g\in K^\times$.

The rational-section key formula. On an integral scheme $W$ of dimension $n$ locally of finite type over the field, let $s,t$ be nonzero rational sections of invertible sheaves $L,M$. Choose a locally finite family of prime divisors $Z_i$ outside whose union both sections are generators. At the generic point of $Z_i$, put $B_i=\mathcal O_{W,Z_i}$, choose local generators $s_i,t_i$, and write $s=f_i s_i$, $t=g_i t_i$. Representatives of the two iterated first Chern cycles differ by the cycle $$\sum_i\left(\operatorname{ord}_{B_i}(f_i)\operatorname{div}_{M|_{Z_i}}(t_i|_{Z_i})-\operatorname{ord}_{B_i}(g_i)\operatorname{div}_{L|_{Z_i}}(s_i|_{Z_i})\right)=\sum_i\operatorname{div}_{Z_i}(\partial_{B_i}(f_i,g_i)),$$ with all terms pushed to $W$. To verify this equality, compare coefficients at a codimension-two point and trivialize $L,M$ there. Rescaling $s_i$ by a unit $u_i$ replaces $f_i$ by $u_i^{-1}f_i$: both sides change by $-\operatorname{ord}_{B_i}(g_i)\operatorname{div}(u_i|_{Z_i})$, since the normalized DVR symbol satisfies $\partial(u_i^{-1},g_i)=\bar u_i^{-\operatorname{ord}_{B_i}(g_i)}$; norms give the same identity for nonnormal $B_i$ by the finite norm-order computation in [[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]. The analogous rescaling of $t_i$ also preserves the equality. We may therefore take the generators to be these trivializations, when the left side is zero and the right coefficient is zero by step 5.1. This proves the key formula without restricting a section that vanishes identically on $Z_i$.

First Chern descent and commutation. The right side of the key formula is a locally finite sum of principal divisors, so the two iterated first Chern classes on $[W]$ agree in $A_{n-2}(W)$. Taking $M=\mathcal O_W$ and $t=r\in k(W)^*$ gives $c_1(L)\cap\operatorname{div}_W(r)=c_1(\mathcal O_W)\cap\operatorname{div}_L(s)=0$: the section $1$ of the trivial bundle has zero divisor on every integral cycle. Thus first Chern operators annihilate each rational-equivalence generator and commute on Chow groups. Pushforward along integral closed subschemes and linear extension give the same conclusions on arbitrary locally finite type schemes.

Cartier Gysin descent with support. Let $D=Z(s)$ for a global section of $L$, and test on an integral $W$. If $W\subseteq D$, its Gysin is the first Chern operator on $W$, which descends by step 7.1. Otherwise $D|_W$ is Cartier. For a rational section $t$ of $M|_W$, apply step 6.1, including the components of $D|_W$ among the $Z_i$, and choose $s_i=s|_W$ when $Z_i\not\subseteq D$. Then $f_i=1$ for these indices, so their tame symbols are $1$. The remaining principal divisors are on $Z_i\subseteq D$, and therefore give a rational equivalence on $D\cap W$, proving $$D^!\operatorname{div}_{M|_W}(t)=c_1(M|_{D\cap W})\cap[D\cap W].$$ For $M=\mathcal O_W$ and $t=r$ the right side is zero. Hence Cartier Gysin annihilates principal-divisor relations in its target Chow group, including after base change when the pulled-back section is not Cartier. Proper compatibility used to push these computations to the ambient zero scheme is the norm-order formula in [F3] when a cycle is not contained in $D$, and the same formula applied to rational sections when it is contained.

fact_uses.text: [L3] Cycles, fundamental cycles, flat pullback and proper pushforward are as in [[lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme]], [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]] and [[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]; exterior product on cycles is the assignment on integral cycles $[V]\times[W]\mapsto[V\times_kW]$.

proof_steps.claim: Exterior product. For integral closed subschemes $V\subseteq X$, $W\subseteq X'$ define $[V]\times[W]:=[V\times_kW]$, the fundamental cycle of the product, taken with all irreducible components and their generic lengths by [L3]; this is the product of the cycle classes and is bilinear. For a fixed integral $W\subseteq X'$, it is the flat pullback along $X\times W\to X$ followed by the closed-immersion pushforward $X\times W\hookrightarrow X\times X'$; the symmetric description handles the other variable. Hence descends to rational equivalence in either variable and commutes with all bivariant operations by [L1]; symmetry of the construction and of the generic lengths makes the product symmetric, and associativity is checked on fundamental cycles of triple products, where both iterated flat pullbacks compute the same generic length by associativity of tensor products and the flat length multiplicity computation. Extension is bilinear and the components are retained with their multiplicities, so no integrality hypothesis on the field is used.

fact_uses.text: [L4] Proper pushforward of an integral cycle $W$ with $\dim\pi(W)<\dim W$ is zero, and pullback of classes along the flat morphism $\pi$ shifts degree by $r-1$ ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]], [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]], [[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]]).

proof_steps.claim: Pushforward identities. Let $V\subseteq X$ be an integral closed subscheme of dimension $m$, so that $\pi^*[V]=[\mathbb P(\mathcal E|_V)]$ is an $(m+r-1)$-cycle. First suppose $\mathcal E|_V$ is trivial. The zero schemes of $r-1$ coordinate sections of $\mathcal O(1)$ are relative hyperplanes meeting in a section $\sigma:V\to\mathbb P(\mathcal E|_V)$, so $\xi^{r-1}\cap\pi^*[V]=\sigma_*[V]$ and $\pi_*\sigma_*[V]=[V]$. For any $\mathcal E$ and $0\le s<r-1$, the cycle $\xi^s\cap\pi^*[V]$ has dimension $m+r-1-s>m$ and is supported on $\mathbb P(\mathcal E|_V)$, whose image has dimension $m$; hence its components push to zero by [L4]. For the top power with general $\mathcal E$, choose a dense open $U\subseteq V$ trivializing the bundle. The identity $\pi_*(\xi^{r-1}\cap\pi^*[V])=[V]$ holds over $U$, and its difference is in $A_m(V)$ supported on $V\setminus U$. This complement has dimension less than $m$, so localization [L3] makes the difference zero. Both identities extend by linearity to all $\alpha\in A_*(X)$.

fact_uses.text: [L3] Projective pushforward of Chow classes is functorial and satisfies the projection formula ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]], [[lem-chow-ring-naturality-and-projection-formula]], [[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]); degrees on projective space are computed by the degree isomorphism of [[lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space]] and flat pullback is compatible with degree ([[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]]).

proof_steps.claim: The fibre computation. Let $\tau=\operatorname{ch}\cdot\operatorname{td}$; for the generator $\alpha=p_Y^*\beta\otimes p_{\mathbb P}^*[\mathcal O(m)]$ the left-hand side is $\tau(p_!\alpha)=\binom{m+n}{n}\operatorname{ch}(\beta)\operatorname{td}(T_Y)$ by step 1.1 and additivity/multiplicativity of $\tau$ on the base [L2]. The right-hand side is $p_*(\operatorname{ch}(\beta)\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal O(m))\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n\times_kY}))$; the tangent bundle of the product is the direct sum of the pullbacks of the tangent bundles, so its Todd class is $\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n})\operatorname{td}(T_Y)$ by [L2], and the projection formula for $p_*$ [L3] moves $\operatorname{ch}(\beta)\operatorname{td}(T_Y)$ out, leaving the fibre integral $p_*(\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal O(m))\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n}))$. The Euler sequence $0\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O(1)^{n+1}\to T_{\mathbb P^n}\to0$ follows on standard charts by differentiating the ratios $x_i/x_j$: its first map is the coordinate vector, and these derivatives identify the quotient with the tangent bundle. Consequently $\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n})=(h/(1-e^{-h}))^{n+1}$ modulo $h^{n+1}$, so this fibre integral is the formal residue $\operatorname{Res}_{h=0}e^{mh}(1-e^{-h})^{-n-1}dh$, computed by substituting $z=1-e^{-h}$: then $dh=dz/(1-z)$ and $e^{mh}=(1-z)^{-m}$, and the residue equals the coefficient $[z^n](1-z)^{-m-1}=\binom{m+n}{n}$. Comparing with the left-hand side, the identity holds on every generator.

General projective bundles, and conclusion. A rank-zero bundle has empty projectivization and both Riemann-Roch sides are zero; assume positive rank for the following computation. The same computation applies to a general projective bundle projection $\pi:P=\mathbb P(\mathcal E)\to Y$ using the relative projective bundle generators of [L1] and the relative Euler sequence: after splitting $\mathcal E$ by a flag bundle the pushforward coefficient of a relative twist is the divided difference $\sum_iF(-x_i)/\prod_{j\ne i}(x_j-x_i)$ in the formal roots $x_i$. The relative Euler sequence in the lines convention is $0\to\mathcal O\to\pi^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal O(1)\to T_{P/Y}\to0$, from first-order deformations of a line. The pushforward formula follows algebraically from the projective relation $\prod_i(h+x_i)=0$ and $\pi_*h^{r-1}=1$: Lagrange interpolation on the nodes $-x_i$ reads its top remainder coefficient as that divided difference. The generator integrand is $e^{mh}\prod_j(h+x_j)/(1-e^{-x_j-h})$, whose divided-difference sum is the character of the relative symmetric power by the partial-fraction identity $\prod_j(1-ze^{-x_j})^{-1}=\sum_i\prod_{j\ne i}(1-e^{x_i-x_j})^{-1}(1-ze^{-x_i})^{-1}$; work initially with independent formal roots and invert their differences to justify interpolation and partial fractions. The resulting coefficients of the symmetric-power series are symmetric polynomials, so denominators cancel; truncation in the Chow grading then specializes correctly even when roots coincide. Thus with injective flag pullback and the base Todd projection formula the identity descends. Since the identity is additive in $\alpha$ and holds on the generators of $K_0$ for every $Y$ in the stated hypotheses, the diagram commutes; the case $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch for $\mathbb P^n$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-adhm-fixed-point-instanton-count]]: the fixed points for $N=1,k=1$ are indexed by the one one-box partition, and their tangent character is computed from the ADHM deformation complex.

proof_steps.claim: There is exactly one partition of $k=1$ for $N=1$, namely $Y_1=\{(0,0)\}$, so [F2] gives the unique fixed point. Here $\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=e_1$ and $\mathbf W=e_1^{-1}$, whence $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf V=1$, $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf W^\vee=1$, and $t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V=t_1t_2$. Substitution in the tangent character gives $t_1+t_2$; the two additive weights are $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$, so the Euler class is $\epsilon_1\epsilon_2$.

The degree-one coefficient is the sum over the single fixed point, so it equals $(\epsilon_1\epsilon_2)^{-1}$. This is a formal equivariant fixed-point contribution, not an asserted continuum path-integral value.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-adhm-fixed-point-instanton-count]]: fixed points are indexed by two-tuples of partitions of total size one, and the tangent character is $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf V(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V$.

proof_steps.claim: A two-tuple of partitions with total size one places its single box in exactly one of the two colors, so the only possibilities are $(\{(0,0)\},\varnothing)$ and $(\varnothing,\{(0,0)\})$. Their quotient representatives have $V$-characters $e_1$ and $e_2$, respectively.

For the first point, the ADHM convention [F1] gives $\mathbf W=e_1^{-1}+e_2^{-1}$ and $\mathbf W^\vee=e_1+e_2$, while $\mathbf V=e_1$. Substitution in [F2] gives $$t_1+t_2+\frac{e_2}{e_1}+t_1t_2\frac{e_1}{e_2}.$$ The corresponding additive weights are $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_2-a_1,\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2+a_1-a_2$, so their product is $E_1$. Interchanging the two colors gives the second displayed character and $E_2$.

Each fixed-point contribution is the reciprocal of its Euler product, so the degree-one coefficient is $E_1^{-1}+E_2^{-1}$. The TikZ drawing only records the two one-box colorings and is not used in this calculation.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] Stable data yield the stated framed monad, and its sheaf is locally free exactly for costable data. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: At zero real level, $J=0$ still follows from $I\ne0$ and $IJ=0$, while the real equation becomes $|I|^2=0$. This contradicts $I\ne0$, so the stable zero-level locus is empty. In the positive chamber, $J=0$ makes all of $V$ a nonzero invariant subspace in $\ker J$; the data are not costable. By [F3], their framed sheaves are not locally free.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] The ADHM-to-monad construction uses source $V\mathcal O(-1)$, middle $(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O$, target $V\mathcal O(1)$, and the displayed Hilbert polynomial. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Substituting $V=0$ into the monad leaves $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its kernel at the right is $W\mathcal O$ and the image at the left is zero, so the middle cohomology is canonically $W\mathcal O$. Restriction to $L_\infty$ is the identity framing on the prescribed basis of $W$. Since $\chi(\mathcal O(m))=\binom{m+2}{2}$, its Hilbert polynomial is $N\binom{m+2}{2}$, the case $k=0$ of [F2]. No Euler-block or empty-matrix convention changes these calculations.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] For a stable complex datum the framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad has maps $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0B_2+z_2,z_0B_1-z_1,z_0I)$, and its middle cohomology is a framed torsion-free sheaf; local freeness is equivalent to costability. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Substituting that representative in [F3] gives $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ and $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,z_0)$. Their product is $-z_2z_1+z_1z_2=0$. The row $\beta$ is surjective at every projective point because its three entries have no common zero, and $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map because it is nonzero away from $p$. Let $K=\ker\beta$. Projection to the third coordinate restricts to a morphism $\gamma:K\to\mathcal O$. On the affine chart $z_0=1$, put $x=z_1$ and $y=z_2$; a vector in $K$ has the form $(u,v,-yu+xv)$, so $\gamma(K)=(x,y)$ and its kernel is generated by $(-x,-y,0)$, the image of $\alpha$. On any chart away from $p$ where $z_1$ or $z_2$ is a unit, the same equations show that $\gamma$ is onto and its kernel is generated by $\alpha$. Hence $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha\cong I_p$ globally, where $I_p$ is the ideal sheaf of $p$.

This exhibits a positive-FI stable point outside the costable, locally-free zero-FI locus; the correspondence with ordinary ASD moduli is restricted to that zero-FI locus and does not absorb this boundary point.

proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition.

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step.
