For $k>0$, use the tuple $Y_1=\{(i,0):0\leq i<k\}$ and $Y_\alpha=\varnothing$ for $\alpha>1$; step 1.1 constructs a stable datum. proof_steps.claim: Conversely, let $\mathcal E$ be a framed torsion-free sheaf with the stated Hilbert polynomial. The preceding Beilinson lemma constructs its monad, with terms $V_1\mathcal O(-1)$, $M\mathcal O$, and $V_2\mathcal O(1)$ of ranks $k,2k+N,k$. Its restriction to $L_\infty$ remains exact at the ends because $\mathcal E$ is locally free there. Put $K=\ker\beta|_{L_\infty}$. The sequence $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to W\mathcal O\to0$ splits since $\operatorname{Ext}^1(W\mathcal O,V_1\mathcal O(-1))=V_1\otimes W^*\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$.

The remaining line extension $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\oplus W\mathcal O\to M\mathcal O\to V_2\mathcal O(1)\to0$ has class in $\operatorname{Hom}(V_2,V_1)\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$, since $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$. Twist by $\mathcal O(-1)$ and take cohomology. The connecting map $V_2\to V_1\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$ is an isomorphism: the adjacent groups $H^0(\mathcal O(-1))$ and $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))$ vanish, while $H^1(\mathcal O(-2))\cong\mathbb C$. Thus $V_2$ is identified with $V_1$ by this canonical extension class. Choosing a basis of $V_1$ and using the fixed framed basis of $W$ identifies $M=V\oplus V\oplus W$ and the line maps with the two Euler blocks in the Statement. Any other such choice differs by one simultaneous element of $GL(V)$.

The remaining coefficients of the two linear maps are their $z_0$ coefficients, so write $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0C_1+z_2,z_0C_2-z_1,z_0I)$. The coefficients of $z_0z_1$ and $z_0z_2$ in $\beta\alpha=0$ force $C_1=B_2$ and $C_2=B_1$; the $z_0^2$ coefficient is then $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. This recovers the stated ADHM form. The surjectivity of $\beta$ implies stability: if $U=\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(W)\}$ were proper, it is invariant and the induced $B_1,B_2$ on $V/U$ commute because $[B_1,B_2]=-IJ$ has image in $U$. Their dual actions on the nonzero annihilator $U^\perp\subset V^*$ commute, so [F6] gives a common eigen-covector $\lambda\ne0$ with $\lambda I=0$. At the corresponding affine point, $\lambda\beta=0$, contradicting surjectivity.

The Beilinson construction is natural under framed sheaf isomorphisms, so an isomorphism of framed sheaves induces maps on the cohomology vector spaces used in steps 1.2–6.2 and hence a single change of basis $g\in GL(V)$; the normalized Euler blocks force the recovered tuples to differ by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)$. Conversely such a $g$ is an isomorphism of monads acting trivially on $W$, and therefore induces a framed sheaf isomorphism. This proves the pointwise inverse equivalence modulo $GL(V)$. For a finite-type data family, step 2.1 makes $\beta$ surjective on the total space, so $K=\ker\beta$ is locally free. The sequence $0\to V\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to\mathcal E\to0$ is exact and its terms before $\mathcal E$ are flat over the base. After tensoring with any residue field of the base, the first map remains sheaf-injective by step 1.1; hence $\operatorname{Tor}_1(k(s),\mathcal E)=0$. Since $\mathcal E$ is finite over each local ring of $\mathbb P^2\times S$ and its residue fiber is a vector space over the residue field, [F8] gives flatness over $S$. Under the stated relative cohomology and base-change hypotheses, the same constructions use vector bundles and are inverse for families.

Apply the family equivalence to $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. A first-order deformation of the ADHM data is $(\dot B_1,\dot B_2,\dot I,\dot J)$ satisfying $d\mu_{\mathbb C}=0$; infinitesimal changes of basis are $d_0(\xi)=([\xi,B_1],[\xi,B_2],\xi I,-J\xi)$. Differentiating the monad gives the chain perturbation $(\dot\alpha,\dot\beta)$ with $\beta\dot\alpha+\dot\beta\alpha=0$, and a change by $d_0(\xi)$ is the corresponding chain homotopy. Since the family construction and its inverse commute with this dual-number base change, they induce inverse linear maps on first-order framed deformations and on the quotient tangent spaces $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$.

If $k=0$, $V=0$, all four maps and both equations are the unique zero-dimensional maps, stability and costability are vacuous, and the monad is $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its middle cohomology is the framed bundle $W\mathcal O$ with Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}$. Conversely, [F3] constructs this same zero-term monad from every framed sheaf with that polynomial, so the framing identifies each such sheaf with $W\mathcal O$. Thus both moduli spaces are points, and all empty-matrix and Euler-block conventions are satisfied.

proof_steps.claim: The framing makes $\det\mathcal E$ trivial on $L_\infty$, so $c_1(\mathcal E)\cdot L_\infty=0$ and $\mu(\mathcal E)=0$. Each fixed-point contribution is the reciprocal of its Euler product, so the degree-one coefficient is $E_1^{-1}+E_2^{-1}$. The TikZ drawing only records the two one-box colorings and is not used in this calculation.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] For a stable complex datum the framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad has maps $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0B_2+z_2,z_0B_1-z_1,z_0I)$, and its middle cohomology is a framed torsion-free sheaf; local freeness is equivalent to costability. proof_steps.claim: Substituting that representative in [F3] gives $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ and $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,z_0)$. Their product is $-z_2z_1+z_1z_2=0$. The row $\beta$ is surjective at every projective point because its three entries have no common zero, and $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map because it is nonzero away from $p$. Let $K=\ker\beta$. Projection to the third coordinate restricts to a morphism $\gamma:K\to\mathcal O$. On the affine chart $z_0=1$, put $x=z_1$ and $y=z_2$; a vector in $K$ has the form $(u,v,-yu+xv)$, so $\gamma(K)=(x,y)$ and its kernel is generated by $(-x,-y,0)$, the image of $\alpha$. On any chart away from $p$ where $z_1$ or $z_2$ is a unit, the same equations show that $\gamma$ is onto and its kernel is generated by $\alpha$. Hence $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha\cong I_p$ globally, where $I_p$ is the ideal sheaf of $p$.

At $p$, the local ideal $(x,y)$ is not principal: if it were generated by one element in the regular local ring $\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x,y)}$, its quotient by the maximal ideal would have dimension at most one, whereas $(x,y)/(x,y)^2$ has dimension two. Therefore $I_p$ is not locally free at $p$. Its framing on $L_\infty$ is the canonical trivialization because $p\notin L_\infty$. This exhibits a positive-FI stable point outside the costable, locally-free zero-FI locus; the correspondence with ordinary ASD moduli is restricted to that zero-FI locus and does not absorb this boundary point.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F9] On a regular Noetherian surface, the double dual of a rank-one exterior power is a line bundle and determinant maps extend across codimension two. [[lem-regular-surface-reflexive-modules-and-codimension-one-lattices]]

proof_steps.claim: The framing makes $\det\mathcal E$ trivial on $L_\infty$, so $c_1(\mathcal E)\cdot L_\infty=0$ and $\mu(\mathcal E)=0$. For a positive-rank subsheaf $\mathcal F\subset\mathcal E$, replace it by its saturation. At the generic point of $L_\infty$, use the chart $z_1\ne0$ with coordinates $x=z_0/z_1$, $y=z_2/z_1$; the local ring is $\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x)}$, a discrete valuation ring because every nonzero polynomial is a power of $x$ times a polynomial not divisible by $x$, and the latter is a unit after localization. Saturation makes both $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal E/\mathcal F$ torsion-free there, hence free by [F7]. Thus reducing the inclusion modulo $x$ remains injective at that generic point. Taking the double dual of its top exterior power gives a morphism from the determinant line of $\mathcal F$ to the corresponding exterior power of $\mathcal E$ near the line; [F9] makes this extension a morphism across the finite non-locally-free set. It is nonzero at the generic point and therefore restricts to a nonzero map $\det(\mathcal F)|_{L_\infty}\to\bigwedge^{\mathrm{rk}\mathcal F}(W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty})$. Some component into a trivial line bundle is a nonzero section of $(\det(\mathcal F)|_{L_\infty})^*$, forcing $\deg(\det(\mathcal F)|_{L_\infty})\le0$. This proves slope-semistability of $\mathcal E$ of slope zero.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] The exact rank-two theorem supplies the ordinary framed ASD connection of a regular rank-two datum by its raw forward monad/projection construction, extends it smoothly over infinity, and proves $q_2=-k$. Its exact GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form hypotheses are retained in the rank-one raw emptiness deduction. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition.

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] The exact framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad theorem gives the stable-data/framed torsion-free-sheaf correspondence, with rank $N\ge1$, Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, framing character $\sum e_\alpha^{-1}$, inverse extraction, and tangent correspondence in its stated locally-free/base-change family range. Combined with the finite real/complex quotient theorem, its positive-FI clause has the quotient used here. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: The quotient in [A1] has exactly the raw equation, stability, dual framing representation, rank and Hilbert polynomial of the Statement. Its normalized construction is equivariant for those framing and rotation characters, and the first-order family clause identifies tangent representations in its stated base-change range. Thus [A1] transfers the fixed-point bijection and tangent characters of step 1.1 to the Gieseker space.

For $k>0$, use the tuple $Y_1=\{(i,0):0\leq i<k\}$ and $Y_\alpha=\varnothing$ for $\alpha>1$; step 1.1 constructs a stable datum. Replacing $B_1$ by $B_1+c\,\mathrm{id}_V$ preserves the complex equation and stability while changing $\operatorname{tr}(B_1)$ by $kc$ for every $c\in\mathbb C$. Trace is invariant under conjugation, so the descended trace function on the geometric quotient has image $\mathbb C$, which is not compact. Thus the quotient is noncompact. The completed Borel carrier matches the compact real-Borel interface in [L1]. The ADHM/monad comparisons in [A1]–[A2] retain their exact analytic and family hypotheses, while step 2.3 has supplied the precise intrinsic localized Borel–Moore pushforward covered by [F6].

[[lem-qftx-p2-beilinson-diagonal-and-framed-vanishing]]

proof_steps.claim: Conversely, let $\mathcal E$ be a framed torsion-free sheaf with the stated Hilbert polynomial. The preceding Beilinson lemma constructs its monad, with terms $V_1\mathcal O(-1)$, $M\mathcal O$, and $V_2\mathcal O(1)$ of ranks $k,2k+N,k$. Its restriction to $L_\infty$ remains exact at the ends because $\mathcal E$ is locally free there. Put $K=\ker\beta|_{L_\infty}$. The sequence $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to W\mathcal O\to0$ splits since $\operatorname{Ext}^1(W\mathcal O,V_1\mathcal O(-1))=V_1\otimes W^*\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$.

The remaining line extension $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\oplus W\mathcal O\to M\mathcal O\to V_2\mathcal O(1)\to0$ has class in $\operatorname{Hom}(V_2,V_1)\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$, since $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$. Twist by $\mathcal O(-1)$ and take cohomology. The connecting map $V_2\to V_1\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$ is an isomorphism: the adjacent groups $H^0(\mathcal O(-1))$ and $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))$ vanish, while $H^1(\mathcal O(-2))\cong\mathbb C$. Thus $V_2$ is identified with $V_1$ by this canonical extension class. Choosing a basis of $V_1$ and using the fixed framed basis of $W$ identifies $M=V\oplus V\oplus W$ and the line maps with the two Euler blocks in the Statement. Any other such choice differs by one simultaneous element of $GL(V)$.

The remaining coefficients of the two linear maps are their $z_0$ coefficients, so write $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0C_1+z_2,z_0C_2-z_1,z_0I)$. The coefficients of $z_0z_1$ and $z_0z_2$ in $\beta\alpha=0$ force $C_1=B_2$ and $C_2=B_1$; the $z_0^2$ coefficient is then $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. This recovers the stated ADHM form. The surjectivity of $\beta$ implies stability: if $U=\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(W)\}$ were proper, it is invariant and the induced $B_1,B_2$ on $V/U$ commute because $[B_1,B_2]=-IJ$ has image in $U$. Their dual actions on the nonzero annihilator $U^\perp\subset V^*$ commute, so [F6] gives a common eigen-covector $\lambda\ne0$ with $\lambda I=0$. At the corresponding affine point, $\lambda\beta=0$, contradicting surjectivity.

The Beilinson construction is natural under framed sheaf isomorphisms, so an isomorphism of framed sheaves induces maps on the cohomology vector spaces used in steps 1.2–6.2 and hence a single change of basis $g\in GL(V)$; the normalized Euler blocks force the recovered tuples to differ by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)$. Conversely such a $g$ is an isomorphism of monads acting trivially on $W$, and therefore induces a framed sheaf isomorphism. This proves the pointwise inverse equivalence modulo $GL(V)$. For a finite-type data family, step 2.1 makes $\beta$ surjective on the total space, so $K=\ker\beta$ is locally free. The sequence $0\to V\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to\mathcal E\to0$ is exact and its terms before $\mathcal E$ are flat over the base. After tensoring with any residue field of the base, the first map remains sheaf-injective by step 1.1; hence $\operatorname{Tor}_1(k(s),\mathcal E)=0$. Since $\mathcal E$ is finite over each local ring of $\mathbb P^2\times S$ and its residue fiber is a vector space over the residue field, [F8] gives flatness over $S$. Under the stated relative cohomology and base-change hypotheses, the same constructions use vector bundles and are inverse for families.

Apply the family equivalence to $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. A first-order deformation of the ADHM data is $(\dot B_1,\dot B_2,\dot I,\dot J)$ satisfying $d\mu_{\mathbb C}=0$; infinitesimal changes of basis are $d_0(\xi)=([\xi,B_1],[\xi,B_2],\xi I,-J\xi)$. Differentiating the monad gives the chain perturbation $(\dot\alpha,\dot\beta)$ with $\beta\dot\alpha+\dot\beta\alpha=0$, and a change by $d_0(\xi)$ is the corresponding chain homotopy. Since the family construction and its inverse commute with this dual-number base change, they induce inverse linear maps on first-order framed deformations and on the quotient tangent spaces $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$.

If $k=0$, $V=0$, all four maps and both equations are the unique zero-dimensional maps, stability and costability are vacuous, and the monad is $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its middle cohomology is the framed bundle $W\mathcal O$ with Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}$. Conversely, [F3] constructs this same zero-term monad from every framed sheaf with that polynomial, so the framing identifies each such sheaf with $W\mathcal O$. Thus both moduli spaces are points, and all empty-matrix and Euler-block conventions are satisfied.

fact_uses.text: [F1] $|K_j(x)|\le c_n|x|^{-n}$ for $x\ne0$; $|K_j(x-h)-K_j(x)|\le C_n|h|\,|x|^{-(n+1)}$ with $C_n=c_n2^{n+1}(3n+4)$ whenever $|h|\le|x|/2$; and $\int_{S^{n-1}}K_j(r\omega)\,d\sigma(\omega)=0$ for every $r>0$ ([[lem-riesz-transform-kernels-have-explicit-size-difference-and-spherical-cancellation-bounds]]).

proof_steps.claim: The published estimates give the size bound $|K_j(x)|\le c_n|x|^{-n}$, the first-difference bound $|K_j(x-h)-K_j(x)|\le C_n|h||x|^{-(n+1)}$ for $|h|\le|x|/2$, and the vanishing of every spherical mean. [[thm-qftx-taubes-arbitrary-divisor-plane-vortex]]

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F5] [[pthm-qftx-n2-linear-monopole-bps-vortex-bound]]: in the frozen-metric linear truncation, actual mathematical arbitrary-divisor vortices embed as stationary absolute full-model minima with $T_n=4\pi v^2|n|$; actual canonical full-model collars give $T_nL+O(1)$ for fixed-flux cylinder infima. proof_steps.claim:
Under the additional vortex/minimization hypothesis in the Statement,
[F4] gives nonzero quantized original electric flux and a tension
$\sigma>0$. The interior of a translation-invariant tube of length $L$
contains the same transverse profile at each longitudinal coordinate, so
its bulk energy is $\sigma L$. The uniformly bounded endcap contribution

effective model. This last conclusion is conditional: no preceding step establishes existence or minimization of the required profile. The nonlinear obstruction in [F5] prevents extending its exact BPS assertion to generic u.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-qftx-taubes-arbitrary-divisor-plane-vortex]]: for every effective finite divisor of degree $|n|$ there is a smooth finite-energy planar critical pair with flux $2\pi n$ (using conjugation for $n<0$); for the empty divisor it is the vacuum. The local unwound exterior gauge has $q=\sqrt\xi e^{h/2}$ and $A=-\tfrac12*dh$; that degree-changing exterior gauge is not asserted to extend globally. Separately, removing only the smooth degree-zero polynomial phase correction relative to $n\theta$ by a global cutoff gauge yields the canonical winding representative $q=\sqrt\xi e^{h/2}e^{in\theta}$, $A=n\,d\theta-\tfrac12*dh$.

proof_steps.claim: For an end trace with exterior phase $n\theta+\phi$, choose a smooth radial cutoff $\eta$ which is zero on a disk containing the noncanonical region and one outside a larger disk. The real function $\chi=-\eta\phi$ extends smoothly by zero to the whole plane; the allowed gauge transformation $(q,A)\mapsto(e^{i\chi}q,A+d\chi)$ therefore makes the exterior phase exactly $n\theta$. This constructs the asserted degree-zero exterior phase cleanup without attempting to extend a degree-$n$ angular map across the disk. For the planar minimizer in [F2], write $P=|P|e^{i\vartheta}$ on the exterior; $\vartheta-n\theta$ is single-valued, smooth and tends to zero because $P(z)=z^n(1+O(|z|^{-1}))$ for $n\ge0$ (use the conjugate construction for $n<0$). In canonical exterior gauge write $q=\rho e^{in\theta}$ and $\alpha=A-n\,d\theta$. Directly, $D_Aq=e^{in\theta}(d\rho-i\rho\alpha)$, so the real and imaginary terms are orthogonal and $|D_Aq|^2=|d\rho|^2+\rho^2|\alpha|^2$. Uniform convergence gives $\rho\ge\sqrt\xi/2$ outside a disk; thus finite kinetic energy implies $\alpha\in L^2$ there. Also $|\rho-\sqrt\xi|\le |\rho^2-\xi|/\sqrt\xi$, so finite potential energy gives $\rho-\sqrt\xi\in L^2$ there. On compact disks all fields are smooth and bounded. Consequently, for any two cleaned end traces and the cleaned minimizer, differences of connections and Higgs fields are globally in $L^2$; each Higgs field is bounded.

Apply step 3.1 first to $p_0$ and $p_*$, defining its finite energy to be $C_0$, and then to $p_*$ and $p_1$, defining its finite energy to be $C_1$. Combining steps 1.1 and 4.1 gives $0\le\inf\mathcal E_L-T_nL\le C_0+C_1-2\ell T_n$ for every $L\ge2\ell$; the right side is a finite constant independent of $L$, proving the bounded-remainder conclusion. proof_steps.claim: To obtain derivative decay, fix $\alpha<\alpha'<\sqrt\kappa$ and use step 3.3 at rate $\alpha'$. On each unit ball centered at large $z$, both $w$ and $\Delta w=\kappa(1-e^{-w})$ are $O(e^{-\alpha'|z|})$. By [F3] and [F5], $w$ has a $C^{1,\beta}$ norm of that order on the concentric half-ball for some $\beta>0$. Thus the right-hand side has a $C^{0,\beta}$ norm of the same order, and [F4] gives $C^{2,\beta}$ decay on a smaller ball. Inductively, for each multi-index $\gamma$, differentiating $\Delta w=\kappa(1-e^{-w})$ gives $\Delta D^\gamma w=\kappa e^{-w}D^\gamma w+G_\gamma$, where $G_\gamma$ is a finite sum of products of lower derivatives of $w$ and is exponentially small by the induction hypothesis. Applying [F3] and [F4] on nested unit balls gives the same $e^{-\alpha'|z|}$ bound for two more derivatives. Since $e^{-\alpha'|z|}\le e^{-\alpha|z|}$ outside a fixed disk, every finite derivative has the stated rate.

fact_uses.text: [L3] The deformation blowup $M$ is smooth and quasi-projective with strict transform $F$ isomorphic to $X\times\mathbb P^1$; it is flat over $\mathbb P^1$ with ordinary fibres $Y$; the open $M\setminus B$ has special fibre $C_XY$, while the complete fibre at infinity is the union $B+\mathbb P(N\oplus1)$ with intersection $\mathbb P(N)$ ([[def-deformation-to-the-normal-cone-and-specialization]], [[lem-smooth-immersion-normal-sequence-and-deformation-charts]]).

proof_steps.claim: The deformation blowup. By [L3], $M$ is smooth and quasi-projective over the field, so every coherent sheaf on $M$ has a finite locally free resolution by [L2]; the strict transform $F$ is isomorphic to $X\times\mathbb P^1$ and meets the fibre at infinity in the section $[0:1]$ of $P=\mathbb P(N\oplus1)$, while it is disjoint from $B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, since $B$ meets $P$ in $\mathbb P(N)$ and the strict transform of $X\times\mathbb P^1$ lies over $X\times\{\infty\}$ inside the exceptional component. On the chart where the infinity fibre is Cartier with equation $t$, the ordinary fibre $Y$ has equation $t-1$, and both act injectively on the coherent sheaf $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$, since on its support $F\cong X\times\mathbb P^1$ they are parameter equations on the second factor and $\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ is locally free there. This sheaf need not be locally free on $M$. Near its intersection with $P$ the component $B$ is absent, so the Cartier equation of $P$ agrees with that of the infinity fibre; step 1.2 therefore restricts a finite locally free resolution of $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ exactly to the ordinary fibre and to $P$, where the restricted complex resolves the restrictions of the sheaf. Near $B$ the sheaf is zero, and a bounded exact complex of vector bundles resolving the zero sheaf is split exact by induction on its length, starting from the last cokernel; hence the restriction of the resolution to $B$ is an exact complex, as asserted.

fact_uses.text: [L4] Smooth local structure of regular embeddings: the conormal sequence, étale-local coordinate model and regular sequences are as in [[lem-smooth-immersion-normal-sequence-and-deformation-charts]]; blowups and strict transforms are as in [[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]].

proof_steps.claim: Sections of smooth morphisms. Let $s:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a regular immersion followed by a smooth projection $p:P\to T$ with $ps$ flat of the expected relative dimension. Locally write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $P=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}C$; the Koszul resolution of $C$ over $B$ has $A$-flat terms because $B$ is smooth hence flat over $A$, and its quotient $C$ is $A$-flat by hypothesis, so the successive kernels are $A$-flat by the Tor vanishing criterion; tensoring with any $A'$ therefore stays exact, so the regular equations remain regular after every base change, and the normal cone of the base-changed embedding is the full base-changed normal bundle with fundamental cycle the bundle pullback. Inverting bundle pullback gives $s^!p^*=(ps)^*$; when $ps=\operatorname{id}$ this is $s^!p^*=1$.

Composition. Apply the equality criterion of [L3] and blow up the product of the two ideals defining the inverse images of $Z$ and $Y$ to make both Cartier, splitting off the excess bundles with [L1] so that the outer normal bundle is a line bundle $N_{Y/T}$ over the base; if an inverse image is the whole base the identity reduces to the excess formula of [L1]. Write $o:Y\to C_YT$ for the zero section; the essential cone identity is $o^![C_ZT]=[C_ZY]$ as a class in $A_{n-1}(C_ZT\times_{C_YT}Y)$ for integral $T$ of dimension $n$. On an affine open write $Z=(a)$ and $Y=(b)$ with $b=ac$ and $a,b\ne0$; the $t$-charts of the two deformations are $R_a=A[t,u]/(tu-a)$ and $R_b=A[t,v]/(tv-b)$, both embedded in $A[t,t^{-1}]$ because their principal ideals are generated by nonzerodivisors, and the homomorphism $R_b\to R_a$, $v\mapsto cu$, defines a morphism from the $t$-chart of the $Z$-deformation to that of the $Y$-deformation which restricts on $t=0$ to the induced map of normal cones. The strict transform of $Y\times\mathbb P^1$ in the $Z$-blowup has coordinate ring $R_a/((b)R_a:t^\infty)=(A/(b))[t,\bar a/t]$, the contraction of $(b)$ after inverting $t$ (saturation is essential: for $b=a^2$ the quotient has relation $u^2=0$ at infinity, not merely $\bar c u=0$), and its special fibre is $\operatorname{gr}_{(\bar a)}(A/(b))=C_ZY$ with all nonreduced multiplicities. The strict transform $\mathbb P^1_Y$ in the $Y$-blowup is the Cartier divisor $v=0$ with infinity restriction the zero section $o$; pulling its Cartier operator back to the $Z$-chart cuts by $cu$, a nonzero divisor because $R_a$ is a domain, and the ordinary parts agree, so the two Cartier classes differ by classes at infinity, which the infinity Cartier Gysin kills because the normal line is trivial ($j^!j_*\eta=c_1(1)\eta=0$). Hence $o^![C_ZT]=[C_ZY]$; write $p:N_{Z/T}\to Z$, $p_1:N_{Z/Y}\to Z$, and $e:N_{Z/Y}\hookrightarrow N_{Z/T}$. After the excess reduction, $e$ is the inverse image of the zero section of the outer normal line. Proper/Cartier compatibility pushes the cone identity to $e^!a_*[C_ZT]=a_{1*}[C_ZY]$, while the relative-line coordinate calculation gives $e^!p^*=p_1^*$. The classes defining the two operations are characterized by $p^*\gamma=a_*[C_ZT]$ and $p_1^*\gamma_1=a_{1*}[C_ZY]$; hence $p_1^*\gamma=p_1^*\gamma_1$, and the injectivity of $p_1^*$ proves the required equality, and pushing down the modifications gives the composition formula for regular embeddings.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-adhm-fixed-point-instanton-count]]: the fixed points for $N=1,k=1$ are indexed by the one one-box partition, and their tangent character is computed from the ADHM deformation complex.

proof_steps.claim: There is exactly one partition of $k=1$ for $N=1$, namely $Y_1=\{(0,0)\}$, so [F2] gives the unique fixed point. Here $\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=e_1$ and $\mathbf W=e_1^{-1}$, whence $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf V=1$, $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf W^\vee=1$, and $t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V=t_1t_2$. Substitution in the tangent character gives $t_1+t_2$; the two additive weights are $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$, so the Euler class is $\epsilon_1\epsilon_2$.

The degree-one coefficient is the sum over the single fixed point, so it equals $(\epsilon_1\epsilon_2)^{-1}$. This is a formal equivariant fixed-point contribution, not an asserted continuum path-integral value.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[thm-adhm-fixed-point-instanton-count]]: fixed points are indexed by two-tuples of partitions of total size one, and the tangent character is $\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf V(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V^\vee\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V$.

proof_steps.claim: A two-tuple of partitions with total size one places its single box in exactly one of the two colors, so the only possibilities are $(\{(0,0)\},\varnothing)$ and $(\varnothing,\{(0,0)\})$. Their quotient representatives have $V$-characters $e_1$ and $e_2$, respectively.

For the first point, the ADHM convention [F1] gives $\mathbf W=e_1^{-1}+e_2^{-1}$ and $\mathbf W^\vee=e_1+e_2$, while $\mathbf V=e_1$. Substitution in [F2] gives $$t_1+t_2+\frac{e_2}{e_1}+t_1t_2\frac{e_1}{e_2}.$$ The corresponding additive weights are $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_2-a_1,\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2+a_1-a_2$, so their product is $E_1$. Interchanging the two colors gives the second displayed character and $E_2$.

Each fixed-point contribution is the reciprocal of its Euler product, so the degree-one coefficient is $E_1^{-1}+E_2^{-1}$. The TikZ drawing only records the two one-box colorings and is not used in this calculation.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] Stable data yield the stated framed monad, and its sheaf is locally free exactly for costable data. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: At zero real level, $J=0$ still follows from $I\ne0$ and $IJ=0$, while the real equation becomes $|I|^2=0$. This contradicts $I\ne0$, so the stable zero-level locus is empty. In the positive chamber, $J=0$ makes all of $V$ a nonzero invariant subspace in $\ker J$; the data are not costable. By [F3], their framed sheaves are not locally free.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] The ADHM-to-monad construction uses source $V\mathcal O(-1)$, middle $(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O$, target $V\mathcal O(1)$, and the displayed Hilbert polynomial. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Substituting $V=0$ into the monad leaves $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its kernel at the right is $W\mathcal O$ and the image at the left is zero, so the middle cohomology is canonically $W\mathcal O$. Restriction to $L_\infty$ is the identity framing on the prescribed basis of $W$. Since $\chi(\mathcal O(m))=\binom{m+2}{2}$, its Hilbert polynomial is $N\binom{m+2}{2}$, the case $k=0$ of [F2]. No Euler-block or empty-matrix convention changes these calculations.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] For a stable complex datum the framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad has maps $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0B_2+z_2,z_0B_1-z_1,z_0I)$, and its middle cohomology is a framed torsion-free sheaf; local freeness is equivalent to costability. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Substituting that representative in [F3] gives $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ and $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,z_0)$. Their product is $-z_2z_1+z_1z_2=0$. The row $\beta$ is surjective at every projective point because its three entries have no common zero, and $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map because it is nonzero away from $p$. Let $K=\ker\beta$. Projection to the third coordinate restricts to a morphism $\gamma:K\to\mathcal O$. On the affine chart $z_0=1$, put $x=z_1$ and $y=z_2$; a vector in $K$ has the form $(u,v,-yu+xv)$, so $\gamma(K)=(x,y)$ and its kernel is generated by $(-x,-y,0)$, the image of $\alpha$. On any chart away from $p$ where $z_1$ or $z_2$ is a unit, the same equations show that $\gamma$ is onto and its kernel is generated by $\alpha$. Hence $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha\cong I_p$ globally, where $I_p$ is the ideal sheaf of $p$.

At $p$, the local ideal $(x,y)$ is not principal: if it were generated by one element in the regular local ring $\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x,y)}$, its quotient by the maximal ideal would have dimension at most one, whereas $(x,y)/(x,y)^2$ has dimension two. Therefore $I_p$ is not locally free at $p$. Its framing on $L_\infty$ is the canonical trivialization because $p\notin L_\infty$. This exhibits a positive-FI stable point outside the costable, locally-free zero-FI locus; the correspondence with ordinary ASD moduli is restricted to that zero-FI locus and does not absorb this boundary point.

final_edge_fact_uses.text:
[F3] The finite monad resolution gives
$c_2(F)=kH^2$; the charge on $S^4$ is conditional on the stated pullback.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-charge-normalization]]

proof_steps.claim:
The residual $U(1)$ action sends
$I\mapsto gI$ and $J\mapsto Jg^{-1}$; it preserves the raw representative's
orbit, and its stabilizer is trivial because $gI=I$ with $I\ne0$ forces
$g=1$. The framed $W$ coordinates at infinity are fixed, so they introduce
no extra unitary factor. The finite monad resolution and [F3] give
$c_2(F)=H^2$, the unit charge under the positive incidence pullback
condition. The example verifies an exact one-instanton block with no
singularity because $f_z$ never vanishes.

final_edge_fact_uses.text:
[F2] The finite monad resolution has
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N-kH^2$, $c_2(F)=kH^2$, and
$\chi(F)=N-2k$; the topological charge statement is conditional on a
pullback bundle.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-charge-normalization]]

proof_steps.claim:
Setting $k=0$ in [F2] gives
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N$, $c_2(F)=0$, and $\chi(F)=N$. Directly,
$F=W\otimes\mathcal O$ has these same classes; if it is written as

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] The preceding vanishing lemma reconstructs a three-term monad with dimensions $k,2k+N,k$ from the Ward bundle. [[lem-qftx-asd-twistor-vanishing-and-monad-reconstruction]]

proof_steps.claim: The reconstructed monad in [F1] is linear with locally free middle bundle, trivial on every real line, and has the positive Hermitian Ward pairing and unitary framing fixed in the definition. Its dimensions are those required by [A1]. Thus, assuming the exact supplier [A1], extract the raw tuple from its intrinsic normal form. Its monad composition vanishes, so [F5]'s polynomial identity makes both raw moment coefficients zero. Full fiber rank on each real line and [F5]'s Gram/rank equivalence identify the locus exactly with stable-and-costable regularity. The intrinsic unitary normalization and inverse-extraction clause in [A1] identify the remaining framed monad changes precisely with $(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ for $g\in U(k)$. The compact-rotation and framing chain maps are exactly those in [F5] and [A1]; first-order naturality is used only in [A1]’s locally-free/base-change range. No arbitrary analytic-family algebraization is inferred. No source-coordinate conjugation or nonexistent universal equivalence is invoked.

Conversely, the regular raw monad in [F5] is a global holomorphic bundle, trivial on every real line, with canonical positive reality: its pairing is induced by the standard Hermitian form on K and β(v)=α(σv)*. It is well-defined on cohomology since kerβ(v) is orthogonal to imα(σv), and on a real line its canonical representatives are kerD with the positive restricted metric; at infinity it is W. Apply the proved local Ward construction to obtain a global framed unitary ASD connection. On the finite chart it equals P d: for a kernel representative v along a D=ker(de) direction, β is constant, so its derivative lies in kerβ; the component of dv orthogonal to kerD lies in im a⊕im b, and β=f(−λ₂,λ₁) forces that component to lie in im(aλ₁+bλ₂)=imα. It therefore vanishes in monad cohomology, leaving exactly P dv. Thus evaluation identifies the projection and Ward connections; the Ward construction supplies the smooth extension and framing at infinity. The normalization of [F3] with determinant reduction [F4] gives k=c₂(E)[S⁴]=−q_N. Under [A1], extraction and construction are inverse on U(k) orbits and framed Ward connections, proving the full claim under the exact normal-form, GAGA and coupled-vanishing hypotheses stated above.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] The standard projective diagonal has the Koszul resolution $0\to\mathcal O(-3)\boxtimes\Omega^3(3)\to\mathcal O(-2)\boxtimes\Omega^2(2)\to\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes\Omega^1(1)\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\Delta\to0,$ because the diagonal is a regular embedding of codimension three and its three local coordinate differences form a regular sequence. [[lem-koszul-resolution-and-flat-fibre-restriction]]

proof_steps.claim: Apply [F4] to the diagonal Koszul resolution [F3], tensoring the second factor by $\mathcal E(-2)$, pushing to the first factor, and twisting that output factor by $\mathcal O(2)$. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Z,\mathcal E(-2)\otimes\Omega_Z^{-p}(-p))\otimes\mathcal O_Z(p+2)$ for $p=-3,-2,-1,0$. Steps 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 and Serre duality make every term in rows $q=0,1,3$ vanish except possibly $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)$ at $(-2,1)$. No differential can enter this term; its only possible outgoing $d_2$ lands in $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. It therefore survives to $E_\infty$, but the diagonal construction resolves $\mathcal E(-2)$ before the output twist and $\mathcal E$ after that twist; it is concentrated in degree zero and has no degree $-1$ hypercohomology. Since $(-2)+1=-1$, the term is zero. Thus the remaining spectral-sequence row is $q=2$.

The row $q=2$ gives the complex $H^2(\mathcal E(-3))\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)\otimes\mathcal O\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))\otimes\mathcal O(1)$. All higher differentials vanish because all other rows are zero. Its only cohomology is the degree-zero hypercohomology of the diagonal resolution, namely $\mathcal E$; the first and last terms are exact because the other total degrees vanish. The maps are linear in the homogeneous output coordinates, since each Koszul differential is contraction with the universal linear section. Thus this is the stated monad; its cohomology vector spaces are canonical, and changing bases acts by $GL(U)\times GL(K)\times GL(U')$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] The total Chern character is additive on exact complexes of vector bundles, $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal O(1))=e^H$, $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal O(-1))=e^{-H}$, and on $\mathbb CP^3$ all classes of degree greater than six vanish. [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]]

proof_steps.claim: In the Grothendieck group, exactness of the monad gives $[\mathcal E]=(2k+N)[\mathcal O]-k[\mathcal O(-1)]-k[\mathcal O(1)]$. By [F1], its Chern character is $(2k+N)-ke^{-H}-ke^H=N-kH^2$, because the constant terms cancel to $N$, the linear terms cancel, the quadratic contribution is $-kH^2$, and terms of degree at least four vanish on $Z$. Therefore $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$ and $c_2(\mathcal E)=-\operatorname{ch}_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F4] Chern classes are natural under pullback, the second Chern class of a bundle with $c_1=0$ is represented by $-\operatorname{ch}_2$, and Chern–Weil forms represent the corresponding real characteristic classes. [[thm-chern-weil-forms-represent-the-at-characteristic-classes-over-the-reals]], [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]]

proof_steps.claim: In the Grothendieck group, exactness of the monad gives $[\mathcal E]=(2k+N)[\mathcal O]-k[\mathcal O(-1)]-k[\mathcal O(1)]$. By [F1], its Chern character is $(2k+N)-ke^{-H}-ke^H=N-kH^2$, because the constant terms cancel to $N$, the linear terms cancel, the quadratic contribution is $-kH^2$, and terms of degree at least four vanish on $Z$. Therefore $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$ and $c_2(\mathcal E)=-\operatorname{ch}_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] The Koszul complex of a section whose zero scheme is a regular codimension-two subscheme resolves its structure sheaf, and exactness persists under the stated flat fiber restriction. [[lem-koszul-resolution-and-flat-fibre-restriction]]

proof_steps.claim: Let $Q$ be the universal rank-two quotient bundle on the first factor. The section of $\mathcal O(1)$ on the second factor tensored with $Q$ on the first, induced by the second tautological line modulo the first, vanishes exactly on the diagonal. In affine coordinates transverse to the diagonal its two components are a regular parameter pair; hence its Koszul complex is exact and resolves $\mathcal O_\Delta$. Since $\det Q=\mathcal O(1)$ and $Q^*=\Omega^1(1)$, the resolution is $0\to\mathcal O(-1)\boxtimes\mathcal O(-2)\to\Omega^1(1)\boxtimes\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O\boxtimes\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\Delta\to0$. The regularity check is local along the diagonal, and outside it one component is a unit; this verifies exactness at every point. Its alternating $K$-class is the diagonal generator from [F5], but here the actual Koszul complex, rather than only its $K$-class, supplies the resolution.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] The Chern character is additive on exact complexes, $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal L)=e^{c_1(\mathcal L)}$ for a line bundle, and $\operatorname{ch}_2=\tfrac12(c_1^2-2c_2)$. [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]]

proof_steps.claim:
In the algebraic Chow ring, [F1] and $H=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ give
$$
\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)=(2k+N)-ke^{-H}-ke^H=N-kH^2,
$$
because $H^4=0$ on the complex threefold and the odd powers cancel. Thus $c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal F)=0$ and $c_2^{\rm alg}(\mathcal F)=kH^2$. In the underlying topological category the same exact sequences are exact sequences of complex vector bundles, so [F5] and the line-class identity $c_1(\mathcal O(1))=H$ give
$$
c(\mathcal F)=\frac{1}{(1-H)^k(1+H)^k}=(1-H^2)^{-k}=1+kH^2
$$
through degree six, since $H^4=0$. Hence the topological classes are $c_1(\mathcal F)=0$, $c_2(\mathcal F)=kH^2$, and $c_3(\mathcal F)=0$. The universal formulas $\operatorname{ch}_1=c_1$, $\operatorname{ch}_2=\tfrac12(c_1^2-2c_2)$, and $\operatorname{ch}_3=\tfrac16(c_1^3-3c_1c_2+3c_3)$ then give the topological $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)=N-kH^2$. This compares only the identical finite line-bundle resolution and its line class, not arbitrary analytic and algebraic cohomology.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F6] The algebraic first Chern class of $\mathcal O(1)$ is the hyperplane divisor class; its cycle class is the Poincaré dual of the complex hyperplane, which is the Euler class of its complex normal line. Thus its cycle class is $H_{\rm top}$. [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]], [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]]

proof_steps.claim: A fiber $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)$ is a complex linear $\mathbb P^1\subset\mathbb P^3$. Its real codimension in $\mathbb P^3$ is $4$ and its real dimension is $2$, so the sign in [F3] is $(-1)^{4\cdot2}=+1$. Therefore $\pi^*u$ is Poincaré dual to $[L_x]$. The restriction of $\mathcal O(1)$ to this linear $\mathbb P^1$ has first Chern number $1$; [F2] then identifies its Poincaré dual as $H_{\rm top}^2$. Thus $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] The exact rank-two theorem supplies the ordinary framed ASD connection of a regular rank-two datum by its raw forward monad/projection construction, extends it smoothly over infinity, and proves $q_2=-k$. Its exact GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form hypotheses are retained in the rank-one raw emptiness deduction. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition.

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] The exact framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad theorem gives the stable-data/framed torsion-free-sheaf correspondence, with rank $N\ge1$, Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, framing character $\sum e_\alpha^{-1}$, inverse extraction, and tangent correspondence in its stated locally-free/base-change family range. Combined with the finite real/complex quotient theorem, its positive-FI clause has the quotient used here. [[thm-qftx-framed-p2-monad-adhm-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: The quotient in [A1] has exactly the raw equation, stability, dual framing representation, rank and Hilbert polynomial of the Statement. Its normalized construction is equivariant for those framing and rotation characters, and the first-order family clause identifies tangent representations in its stated base-change range. Thus [A1] transfers the fixed-point bijection and tangent characters of step 1.1 to the Gieseker space.

For $k>0$, use the tuple $Y_1=\{(i,0):0\leq i<k\}$ and $Y_\alpha=\varnothing$ for $\alpha>1$; step 1.1 constructs a stable datum. Replacing $B_1$ by $B_1+c\,\mathrm{id}_V$ preserves the complex equation and stability while changing $\operatorname{tr}(B_1)$ by $kc$ for every $c\in\mathbb C$. Trace is invariant under conjugation, so the descended trace function on the geometric quotient has image $\mathbb C$, which is not compact. Thus the quotient is noncompact. proof_steps.claim: Conversely, let $\mathcal E$ be a framed torsion-free sheaf with the stated Hilbert polynomial. The preceding Beilinson lemma constructs its monad, with terms $V_1\mathcal O(-1)$, $M\mathcal O$, and $V_2\mathcal O(1)$ of ranks $k,2k+N,k$. Its restriction to $L_\infty$ remains exact at the ends because $\mathcal E$ is locally free there. Put $K=\ker\beta|_{L_\infty}$. The sequence $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to W\mathcal O\to0$ splits since $\operatorname{Ext}^1(W\mathcal O,V_1\mathcal O(-1))=V_1\otimes W^*\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$.

The remaining line extension $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\oplus W\mathcal O\to M\mathcal O\to V_2\mathcal O(1)\to0$ has class in $\operatorname{Hom}(V_2,V_1)\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$, since $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$. Twist by $\mathcal O(-1)$ and take cohomology. The connecting map $V_2\to V_1\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$ is an isomorphism: the adjacent groups $H^0(\mathcal O(-1))$ and $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))$ vanish, while $H^1(\mathcal O(-2))\cong\mathbb C$. Thus $V_2$ is identified with $V_1$ by this canonical extension class. Choosing a basis of $V_1$ and using the fixed framed basis of $W$ identifies $M=V\oplus V\oplus W$ and the line maps with the two Euler blocks in the Statement. Any other such choice differs by one simultaneous element of $GL(V)$.

The remaining coefficients of the two linear maps are their $z_0$ coefficients, so write $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0C_1+z_2,z_0C_2-z_1,z_0I)$. The coefficients of $z_0z_1$ and $z_0z_2$ in $\beta\alpha=0$ force $C_1=B_2$ and $C_2=B_1$; the $z_0^2$ coefficient is then $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. This recovers the stated ADHM form. The surjectivity of $\beta$ implies stability: if $U=\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(W)\}$ were proper, it is invariant and the induced $B_1,B_2$ on $V/U$ commute because $[B_1,B_2]=-IJ$ has image in $U$. Their dual actions on the nonzero annihilator $U^\perp\subset V^*$ commute, so [F6] gives a common eigen-covector $\lambda\ne0$ with $\lambda I=0$. At the corresponding affine point, $\lambda\beta=0$, contradicting surjectivity.

The Beilinson construction is natural under framed sheaf isomorphisms, so an isomorphism of framed sheaves induces maps on the cohomology vector spaces used in steps 1.2–6.2 and hence a single change of basis $g\in GL(V)$; the normalized Euler blocks force the recovered tuples to differ by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)$. Conversely such a $g$ is an isomorphism of monads acting trivially on $W$, and therefore induces a framed sheaf isomorphism. This proves the pointwise inverse equivalence modulo $GL(V)$. For a finite-type data family, step 2.1 makes $\beta$ surjective on the total space, so $K=\ker\beta$ is locally free. The sequence $0\to V\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to\mathcal E\to0$ is exact and its terms before $\mathcal E$ are flat over the base. After tensoring with any residue field of the base, the first map remains sheaf-injective by step 1.1; hence $\operatorname{Tor}_1(k(s),\mathcal E)=0$. Since $\mathcal E$ is finite over each local ring of $\mathbb P^2\times S$ and its residue fiber is a vector space over the residue field, [F8] gives flatness over $S$. Under the stated relative cohomology and base-change hypotheses, the same constructions use vector bundles and are inverse for families.

Apply the family equivalence to $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. A first-order deformation of the ADHM data is $(\dot B_1,\dot B_2,\dot I,\dot J)$ satisfying $d\mu_{\mathbb C}=0$; infinitesimal changes of basis are $d_0(\xi)=([\xi,B_1],[\xi,B_2],\xi I,-J\xi)$. Differentiating the monad gives the chain perturbation $(\dot\alpha,\dot\beta)$ with $\beta\dot\alpha+\dot\beta\alpha=0$, and a change by $d_0(\xi)$ is the corresponding chain homotopy. Since the family construction and its inverse commute with this dual-number base change, they induce inverse linear maps on first-order framed deformations and on the quotient tangent spaces $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$.

If $k=0$, $V=0$, all four maps and both equations are the unique zero-dimensional maps, stability and costability are vacuous, and the monad is $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its middle cohomology is the framed bundle $W\mathcal O$ with Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}$. Conversely, [F3] constructs this same zero-term monad from every framed sheaf with that polynomial, so the framing identifies each such sheaf with $W\mathcal O$. Thus both moduli spaces are points, and all empty-matrix and Euler-block conventions are satisfied.

proof_steps.claim: The adjoint of $b_z^\dagger$ is the column $b_z=(-B_2^\dagger+\bar z_2,\ B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1,\ I^\dagger)^T$. A covector $v^\dagger$ annihilates the image of $b_z^\dagger$ exactly when $B_i^\dagger v=\bar z_i v$ and $I^\dagger v=0$, equivalently $v^\dagger B_i=z_i v^\dagger$ and $v^\dagger I=0$. Such a nonzero covector annihilates every word vector $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, so stability implies surjectivity for every $z$. Conversely, if the word span $Q$ is proper, it is invariant under both $B_i$ and contains $I(W)$. The complex moment equation makes the induced pair on $V/Q$ commute, since $IJ(V)\subseteq I(W)\subseteq Q$. By [F2] its dual has a common eigenvector; pulling that covector back to $V^*$ gives $v^\dagger I=0$ and $v^\dagger B_i=z_i v^\dagger$ for some $z$, so $b_z^\dagger$ is not surjective.

A nonzero vector in $\ker a_z$ is a common eigenvector of $B_1,B_2$ contained in $\ker J$, so costability implies injectivity for every $z$. Conversely, if a nonzero common invariant subspace $Q\subseteq\ker J$ exists, then $IJ(Q)=0$ and the complex moment equation gives $[B_1,B_2]|_Q=0$. The restrictions commute and have a common eigenvector by [F2]; this vector lies in $\ker a_z$ for its eigenvalues $z_1,z_2$. Thus the two affine rank criteria are equivalent to stability and costability.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F6] For $N\ge1$, each regular complex $GL(V)$ orbit has a zero-real-moment representative, unique modulo $U(V)$; the resulting identification is equivariant in the raw compact character convention. [[thm-qftx-adhm-real-complex-quotient-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F4] Commuting complex matrices on a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space have a common eigenvector: choose an eigenspace of the first, which is invariant under the second, and then an eigenvector of its restriction. The same applies to dual matrices. [[thm-the-complex-numbers-are-algebraically-closed]]

proof_steps.claim: Failure of surjectivity of $b_z^\dagger=(-B_2+z_2,B_1-z_1,I)$ gives a nonzero covector $\ell$ with $\ell B_i=z_i\ell$ and $\ell I=0$, contradicting the stable spanning set. Conversely, if the stable word span $S$ is proper, the induced pair on $V/S$ commutes since $[B_1,B_2]=-IJ$ has image in $S$. Its dual has a common eigenvector by [F4], and the resulting covector annihilates $I$ and both rows at the corresponding $z$, so surjectivity fails there. A kernel vector of $a_z$ is a common eigenvector of $B_i$ in $\ker J$ and contradicts costability. Conversely, on any nonzero common invariant $S\subset\ker J$, the pair commutes by the complex equation and has a common eigenvector by [F4], producing such a kernel. This proves both equivalences.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] The stable complex ADHM equation locus has a free proper gauge action and a Hausdorff second-countable complex quotient of dimension $2kN$, with tangent $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$. Word-frame slices give holomorphic quotient charts and explicit character gauge lifts at fixed points. [[lem-adhm-stable-quotient-and-torus-lift]]

proof_steps.claim: Apply [F3] to the displayed equation and stability condition. Its proof uses the declared holomorphic implicit-function supplier, proves properness by word-frame bounds on both the gauge transformation and its inverse, and constructs holomorphic quotient charts. Thus the quotient here is a Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold, with tangent $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$ and complex dimension $2kN$. For $k=0$ the quotient is a point. This is the stable complex quotient; no real moment-map or sheaf/ASD identification is inferred.

At a $T$-fixed quotient point represented by $x$, [F3] gives the unique gauge lift $g(t)=C(x)\operatorname{diag}(e_{\alpha_\ell}t_1^{a_\ell}t_2^{b_\ell})C(x)^{-1}$ from a standard-framing word basis. This is a smooth representation of the compact torus itself. The fixed-orbit equations give $g(t)I(w_\alpha)=e_\alpha I(w_\alpha)$ and $g(t)B_i=t_iB_i g(t)$, so all weights generated by stability have the form $e_\alpha t_1^it_2^j$ with $i,j\ge0$. Under $t_1t_2hJ=Jg(t)^{-1}$, a nonzero component from a $V$-weight $\chi$ to the $\beta$th framing line requires $\chi=e_\beta t_1^{-1}t_2^{-1}$. Distinct integer characters on the compact torus cannot satisfy this equality with any generated weight, so $J=0$. The moment equation then gives $[B_1,B_2]=0$. No Zariski-density or algebraic lifting assertion is used.

The label set in step 6.1 is finite: for $k>0$ every box of a size-at-most-$k$ downward-closed diagram has both coordinates less than $k$, so the possible tuples lie in a finite collection of subsets; $k=0$ has only the empty tuple. Hence the fixed locus is a finite set in the Hausdorff quotient from [F3], and each point is isolated. By [F3] the quotient has a finite invariant affine atlas with algebraic action of $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^{N+2}$. In each slice its coordinate functions are eigenfunctions. A point fixed by the compact torus has every nonzero-weight coordinate equal to zero, since each nontrivial integer character is nontrivial on that compact torus; conversely these equations make the point fixed by $T_{\mathbb C}$. Thus the two fixed loci have the same point set. The fixed subscheme is smooth by [F4], because $T_{\mathbb C}$ is diagonalizable and hence linearly reductive. Its fixed ideal in these affine coordinates is generated by the nonzero-weight coordinates. Linearizing that ideal, using the tangent-kernel description in [F4], identifies its tangent with the invariant tangent subspace. A smooth fixed scheme with a finite point set has dimension zero at every point, so that subspace is zero. Therefore every complex tangent weight is a nonzero character. Its associated $u_\chi$ is a nonzero integer linear polynomial in the algebraically independent variables and is invertible in $K$. The tangent has complex dimension $2kN$, so the Euler product has exactly $2kN$ factors counted with multiplicity.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] Absolute projective GAGA on P³ supplies an exact tensor equivalence and cohomology comparison. [[thm-qftx-projective-gaga-for-monad-data]]

proof_steps.claim: Algebraize the holomorphic bundle using [A1]. Its algebraic sheaf is locally free: the holomorphic bundle is dualizable, the exact tensor equivalence transports its evaluation and coevaluation and reflects their triangle identities, and those identities give a finite dual basis on each local algebraic chart, hence a finite projective module. In a splitting C⁴=A⊕B into two-planes, a graph chart of G consists of X:A→B and the incidence is (X,[λ])↦[λ,Xλ], with p a product with P(A). In the library quotient convention it is the projective bundle of the dual of the tautological subbundle. Thus [F1] gives properness, finite presentation and flatness, and e*E is a coherent locally free sheaf flat over G.

At a real line L, absolute P³ GAGA applied to the coherent algebraic sheaf i*(E|L), for the closed immersion i:L→P³, identifies its cohomology with that of the trivial analytic restriction. This uses no GAGA on the Grassmannian: closed-immersion direct image is exact, and its analytification is the same local quotient-module tensor construction. Hence the algebraic fiber cohomology is C^N in degree zero and zero above by [F3]. Its degree-one base-change map has zero target, so is surjective. By [F2] that map is an isomorphism; the finite stalk of R¹p*e*E has zero residue fiber, and Nakayama kills it on a neighborhood. The degree-one local-freeness criterion of cohomology/base change now gives surjectivity in degree zero. Its degree-zero case makes H=p*e*E a finite locally free rank-N bundle with all degree-zero base-change maps isomorphisms near L.

Analytify this actual evaluation isomorphism. On every local product V×P¹, a holomorphic function is constant on each P¹ fiber by the maximum principle, and its remaining function on V is holomorphic by evaluation at a fixed point. Thus p_an*O=O. Trivializing H locally gives p_an*p_an*H_an=H_an, where the inner star denotes pullback and the outer star denotes direct image. Consequently the analytic direct image of e_an*E is H_an, its evaluation is the analytified evaluation, and all degree-zero analytic fiber maps are isomorphisms. The same product calculation after any base change identifies the base-change maps. No circular assumption of analytic base-change surjectivity or broad Grauert theorem is used.

The quaternionic involution on G sends a graph X to j_B X j_A^{-1}; its fixed graph matrices form the real four-dimensional quaternionic subspace, whose complexification is the entire graph space. These charts embed HP¹ smoothly and totally really into G. On its incidence family evaluation is a diffeomorphism onto Z: the inverse sends [v] to (span_C(v,jv),[v]), smoothly in projective charts, and j²=-1 excludes dependence of v,jv. Restrict H_an to this real locus to obtain the smooth rank-N bundle with the claimed fibers and evaluation. The positive pairing induces its Hermitian matrix by evaluating local section frames at a smoothly chosen point on each line; this proves smoothness and positivity, independently of parallelness. At infinity the given unitary frame induces the section-bundle frame. All arguments use only the stated local absolute comparison.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-aqft-susy-wilsonian-action]]: the high- and low-energy actions use smooth classical N=1 chiral fields and a derivative-free holomorphic F-term, with real D-term data kept separate; all Wilsonian, renormalization, threshold, external-energy, regulator, and operator-suppression scales are supplied independently.

proof_steps.claim: Vary the terms depending on $X$ using the normalized physical action brackets in [F1]. At fixed chiral coordinates, $P_{\mathrm{raw}}=\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot2}}\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot1}}|_{\bar\theta=0}$ extracts the top barred coefficient, so $I_D(U)=I_F(P_{\mathrm{raw}}U)$ up to the spacetime total derivatives removed by [A3]. Since $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$, the physical transfer is $[U]_D=[P_{\mathrm{phys}}U]_F$ with $P_{\mathrm{phys}}=-P_{\mathrm{raw}}/2=+\bar D^{\dot\alpha}\bar D_{\dot\alpha}/4$. This is equivalently the minus-one-quarter formula with LOWER-FIRST contraction $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\bar D^{\dot\alpha}$. Chirality annihilates the barred derivatives of the even variation $\delta X$, so the D variation is $[\delta X P_{\mathrm{phys}}(X^\dagger)]_F$. The superpotential variation is $[\delta X(MX+J)]_F$. Thus the physical chiral Euler equation is $P_{\mathrm{phys}}(X^\dagger)+MX+J=0$, and its projector has positive derivative degree one.

By definition, each $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$ has positive derivative degree $1/2$, so $\Pi_0(P_{\mathrm{phys}}X^\dagger)=0$. Applying $\Pi_0$ to the equation in step 1.1 gives $MX+J(\Phi)=0$. Because $M>0$, this scalar linear equation has the unique solution $X_*=-J(\Phi)/M$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-aqft-susy-wilsonian-action]]: the Wilsonian action has a derivative-free holomorphic chiral integrand $F_\lambda(\Phi,W)$ and a separate real D-term; its finite operator quotient, ordered basis, cutoff, and field coordinates are supplied data.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-qftx-physical-bps-charge-data]]: on a regular patch the formal label lattice is $\mathbb Z^2$, $z_u(n_e,n_m)=\sqrt2(n_ea+n_ma_D)$, the chosen DSZ form is integral and antisymmetric, and $\Omega_u(\gamma)$ is the second-helicity supertrace on the supplied one-particle BPS sector.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-qftx-superconformal-index]]: $\mathsf Q$ is self-adjoint and odd with $\mathsf Q^2=\Delta$; the supplied joint energy/charge/parity basis gives maximal diagonal charge domains, and joint charge projections reduce $Q,Q^\dagger,\mathsf Q$ including their domains. Joint blocks have strictly positive constant weights and hence finite dimension for an admissible fugacity pair, even when total gap eigenspaces are infinite.

proof_steps.claim: Fix a joint label $(\lambda,a,b)$ with $\lambda>0$. By [F1], its basis vectors lie in the diagonal domain $D(\Delta)=D(\mathsf Q^2)$, and its joint projection reduces $\mathsf Q$. Trace-class summability makes this joint block finite-dimensional: each of its orthonormal basis vectors has the same positive weighted heat diagonal $w=p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}$, so $n$ such vectors would contribute $nw$ for every $n$ if the block were infinite. Apply [F2] to this restricted Hilbert space: $V_{\lambda,a,b}=\mathsf Q/\sqrt\lambda$ maps its even part unitarily onto its odd part. Their finite dimensions therefore agree.

On the fixed block, $\Xi_{p,q}$ is the scalar $p^a q^b$ and the heat factor is $e^{-\beta\lambda}$. Each supplied even or odd basis vector contributes that same weight. Only finitely many joint blocks meet that set; the sum over those complete blocks differs from the full sum by at most the omitted absolute tail. Thus regrouping by joint charge blocks preserves the sum, even if infinitely many such blocks have the same gap $\lambda$. Every positive-gap block vanishes by step 2.1.

The remaining basis vectors are exactly those with $\lambda=0$. Their heat factor is one and their diagonal weights $p^a q^b$ have finite total absolute sum as a subfamily of the trace-class heat diagonal. Therefore the resulting signed zero-sector trace equals the expression in the Statement and has no $\beta$ dependence, including when the protected kernel is infinite-dimensional.

proof_steps.claim: For $g\in GL(V)$ put $x'=g\cdot x$ and $M(g)^2=\sum_i\|B_i'\|^2+\|I'\|^2+\|J'\|^2$. A fixed word frame $C(x)$ exists by [F2]. Each column of $gC(x)=C(x')$ is a product of at most $k-1$ matrices $B_i'$ followed by $I'$ on a unit framing vector. Submultiplicativity and operator norm bounded by Frobenius norm give $\|g\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le A_x(1+M(g))^k$ for $A_x=\sqrt{k}\|C(x)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. If $x$ is costable, the rows consisting of coordinate rows of $JB_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}$ span $V^*$: their common annihilator is the largest common $B_i$-invariant subspace in $\ker J$, hence zero. The same finite dimension-growth argument as for columns gives a row basis $D(x)$ using words of length at most $k-1$. Since $D(x')=D(x)g^{-1}$, the identical norm estimate gives $\|g^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le A_x'(1+M(g))^k$. This also proves costability is open, since it is covered by the nonvanishing determinants of finitely many such row frames.

Diagonalize $H$ by [F4], with real eigenvalues $\lambda_i$. Along the preceding path the squared $B_i'$ entries have factors $e^{2t(\lambda_a-\lambda_b)}$, the squared $I'$ entries have $e^{2t\lambda_a}$ and the squared $J'$ entries have $e^{-2t\lambda_a}$. The log determinant is affine in $t$. Hence $F_\zeta''$ is a sum of $4w^2|z|^2e^{2tw}$ over those entries and their listed weights $w$, and is nonnegative. It can vanish only when $[H,B_i']=0$, $HI'=0$ and $J'H=0$. Stability of $x'$ then forces $H=0$, by applying $H$ to all spanning word vectors. Thus the path is strictly convex for every nonzero $H$. Given two critical matrices $g_1,g_2$, diagonalize the positive matrix $(g_2g_1^{-1})^\dagger(g_2g_1^{-1})$ and take the positive logarithms of its eigenvalues to write $g_2g_1^{-1}=u e^H$ with $u$ unitary and $H$ Hermitian. The endpoints of $e^{tH}g_1$ are both critical, after removing $u$ by invariance. Strict convexity forces $H=0$, so $g_2=ug_1$. This proves uniqueness of the unitary orbit at either level.

At a balanced datum $x$, let $L_x:\operatorname{Herm}(V)\to\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ be $H\mapsto\frac{d}{dt}\mu_{\mathbb R}(e^{tH}\cdot x)|_{t=0}$. Step 4.1 gives $2\operatorname{tr}(H L_xH)=F_\zeta''(e^{tH})|_{t=0}>0$ for nonzero $H$, so $L_x$ is injective and hence invertible in finite equal dimensions. The map $(H,y)\mapsto\mu_{\mathbb R}(e^H\cdot y)-\zeta I$ is smooth. To see smoothness of the exponential in the matrix entries directly, differentiate its absolutely convergent power series: on a bounded matrix set, an order-$r$ derivative of its degree-$m$ term is bounded by a constant times $m^r R^{m-r}/m!$, a summable majorant; this applies through real block matrices as in [F4]. By [F5] the balancing $H=H(y)$ is locally $C^r$ for every finite $r$, and uniqueness glues these branches to the same smooth map. The same invertible derivative along the Hermitian gauge directions in $T_xX^s$ proves that the real-level locus is a smooth submanifold. The unitary group is compact (closed bounded matrices), its action there is free by [F2] and proper (inverse images are closed subsets of $U(V)$ times a compact coordinate projection); therefore its quotient is smooth by [F6]. The map to the complex quotient is smooth using local submersion sections in [F6]. On any word-frame chart [F2], the local balancing map just constructed, followed by the unitary quotient map, is its smooth inverse; step 4.1 proves independence of all choices. Thus the bijections are diffeomorphisms. The compact torus commutes with gauge actions and preserves both the complex equation and $\mu_{\mathbb R}$, so the bijections are equivariant. For $k=0$ all matrices and equations are empty and all quotients are points, proving every boundary case stated. No sheaf or ASD identification was used.

proof_steps.claim: For any Ward bundle use [F3] to form the analytic vector bundle H over a complex-open neighborhood U of every real line in G=Gr(2,4), with holomorphic evaluation p*H≅e*E on the universal family. On a graph chart X:A→B, incidence is (X,[λ])↦[λ,Xλ]. The distribution D=ker(de) consists of matrix variations v with vλ=0 and no λ variation. It is a holomorphic involutive rank-two subbundle, since it is tangent to the fibers of the submersion e. The restriction of p*Ω¹_U to D has kernel B*⊗O(-1) on each projective-line fiber and target D*≅O(1)². The O(-1) vanishings in [F3] give Ω¹_U≅p_*D*. Equivalently, on the graph chart a linear covector on Hom(A,B) restricts to a section on all kernels vλ=0; the map is injective because those kernels span Hom(A,B), and both coefficient spaces have dimension four. This gives the holomorphic sheaf isomorphism without any extra analytic base-change assumption.

The explicit incidence chart fixes vertical complex orientation followed by the positive base orientation to be the complex orientation of Z. The pullback of the positive point Thom class on S⁴ is the positive normal Thom class of its fiber CP¹; [F5] identifies its absolute class as the Poincaré dual of that fiber. A linear CP¹ has dual H²: H restricts with integral one to the line, and the integral projective cohomology ring gives H² as its positive degree-four generator. Hence π*u=H² for the positive generator u of H⁴(S⁴). Smooth evaluation gives E_twistor≅π*H, so c₂(E_twistor)=kH² is equivalent to c₂(H)[S⁴]=k. By [F4] this is q_N=-k; the same calculation verifies the forward map's charge clause. Framing is transported by evaluation at infinity. All constructions use incidence, evaluation and unique relative connections, so commute with the specified projective rotations and framing transformations. They therefore give the claimed T-equivariant bijection and all stated invariants, conditional on the exact absolute GAGA comparison [A1].

proof_steps.claim: Fix $q>0$ and a nonzero $s_0$. For $q=1$, the eventual surjections in step 4.2 make the finite dimensions in [A4] nonincreasing integers, hence eventually constant; thereafter multiplication by $s_0$ is an isomorphism. For $q\ge2$ it is already eventually an isomorphism. Choose $N$ beyond this range, put $V=H^q(\mathcal M(N))$, and identify each $H^q(\mathcal M(n))$, $n\ge N$, with $V$ by successive multiplication by $s_0$. A second independent section $s_1$ induces an endomorphism $T_n$ on $V$ between successive degrees. The commuting multiplication square gives $T_{n+1}=T_n=T$. If $V\ne0$, choose an eigenvalue $\lambda$ by [F7]. Multiplication by the nonzero section $s_1-\lambda s_0$ then induces $T-\lambda I$, singular at every such degree. But step 4.2 applied to this fixed section is eventually an isomorphism for $q\ge2$; for $q=1$ it is eventually surjective between spaces of the same stabilized dimension and hence an isomorphism too. This contradiction proves eventual vanishing. The eigenvalue is chosen before its section's threshold; no bound uniform over an infinite pencil is used.

A simultaneous bound is available. For $1\le q\le r$ take the maximum of the finitely many bounds from step 5.2. If $q>r$, the inductive algebraic dimension bound [F7] makes all relevant cohomology groups of $K_s,Q_s$ in step 4.2 zero at every twist. Multiplication by every nonzero $s$ is then an isomorphism on $H^q(\mathcal M(n))$ at every integer $n$. The same two-section contradiction starting at any degree forces these groups to be zero at every twist. Thus one integer bounds vanishing for all $q>0$.

Fix a point $p$ and choose a hyperplane $H_s$ through it. By the inductive equivalence, $Q_s$ is algebraic. Its finite resolution [F2] begins with a surjection from a finite sum of twisting sheaves. After a sufficiently positive twist each summand is generated by its finite homogeneous monomials, so $Q_s(n)$ has finitely many global generators, analytically as well by inductive comparison. Also choose $n$ so $H^1(\mathcal M(n-1))=0$ by step 6.1 and $H^2(K_s(n))=0$ by induction and [F3]. The first exact sequence in step 4.2 gives $H^1(I_s(n))=0$; the second then lifts those finitely many generators to global sections of $\mathcal M(n)$. The cokernel $C$ of these lifts satisfies $C_p/sC_p=0$, so local Nakayama [F7] gives $C_p=0$. Finite local generation of the coherent cokernel gives an open neighborhood of $p$ on which the lifts generate.
