By [F7] the operators form a complex, so $0\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal A^{0,0}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\mathcal A^{0,r}\to0$ is an exact sheaf resolution. The whole-polydisc statement [F10] also gives positive-degree exactness on each coordinate polydisc. Each $\mathcal A^{0,j}$ is a module over smooth functions, hence is $\Gamma(U_I,-)$-acyclic by [F11]. The resolution cycles lie in the supplied injective-data domain [F13], and [A1] supplies the DC required by [F12]. Applying [F12] identifies $H^q(U_I,\mathcal O)$ with the cohomology of the global Dolbeault complex on $U_I$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] A Hartogs-pseudoconvex domain has zero positive-degree derived cohomology for its holomorphic structure sheaf ([[lem-qftx-gaga-scalar-pseudoconvex-acyclicity]], [[cor-dolbeault-vanishing-pseudoconvex-domain]]).

proof_steps.claim: Each connected component $V_\alpha$ is a bounded domain in the chart of $D_{i_0}$ and inherits the continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion $\rho$. Apply [F1] to obtain a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion on $V_\alpha$, then [F2] to conclude that $V_\alpha$ is Hartogs pseudoconvex. By [F3], $H^q(V_\alpha,\mathcal O)=0$ for $q>0$, hence $H^q(V_\alpha,\mathcal O^{p})=0$ for every finite rank $p$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] Under full AC, the local Dolbeault lemma makes the smooth $(0,\bullet)$-complex exact in positive degrees on polydiscs ([[thm-dolbeault-lemma-polydisc]]).

proof_steps.claim: On each coordinate polydisc in $\Omega$, [F2] says the sequence of sheaves $0\to\mathcal O_\Omega\to\mathcal A^{0,0}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\mathcal A^{0,1}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots$ is exact in positive degree. Its degree-zero kernel is exactly $\mathcal O_\Omega$: a smooth function in that kernel has all $\bar z$-derivatives zero and is holomorphic by [F3]. Thus it is an exact sheaf resolution on $\Omega$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] On a bounded extension domain, $W^{k,2}$ is a Banach algebra when $2k>d$, and the higher-order embedding gives $H^k\hookrightarrow C^1$ when $k>d/2+1$. The same estimates apply componentwise to finitely many localized bundle coefficients. [[cor-sobolev-algebra-above-the-critical-index]], [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]]

proof_steps.claim: Localize by the fixed finite partition and extend each compactly supported coefficient by zero into a bounded Euclidean ball. For $p=2$, $2k>d$; [F2] makes each localized $H^k$ coefficient a Banach algebra and gives its $C^1$ representative when $k>d/2+1$. The finite sum of these estimates proves the same algebra and embedding bounds for sections, matrix-valued functions, and forms in the chosen bundle atlas.

The finite-dimensional matrix exponential is smooth, has derivative the identity at zero on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, and maps $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ into $SU(N)$. In the Banach algebra from step 2.1 its power series and every termwise derivative converge in $H^{k+1}$ on a sufficiently small ball, since the algebra norm is submultiplicative after an equivalent rescaling. The matrix logarithm series converges on a neighborhood of the identity; for a unitary matrix sufficiently close to identity its logarithm is anti-Hermitian, and its trace is zero because the determinant is one and the sum of the small eigenvalue angles lies in $2\pi\mathbb Z$. Hence pointwise $\exp$ and $\log$ give inverse smooth maps between neighborhoods of zero in $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the identity in $\mathcal G_{k+1}$. The inverse-function theorem [F3] also supplies these local Banach charts. Their translated charts cover the group; changes of chart are smooth because the transition functions of $\operatorname{Ad}P$ act by smooth conjugation and the multiplication is a bounded bilinear Sobolev map. The pointwise product and inverse therefore close on $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and are smooth, giving the asserted Hilbert Lie group.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F4] Every bounded sequence in $H^{k+1}$ of sections on the compact manifold has a subsequence converging in $H^k$. [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], assertion 1.

proof_steps.claim: By [F4], a subsequence converges strongly in $H^k$ to a section $u$. The $H^k\hookrightarrow C^0$ embedding preserves the pointwise $SU(N)$ equations and the bundle transition law, so $u$ is a group-bundle section. In the gauge equation, $A_j\to A$, $B_j\to B$, and $u_j\to u$ in $H^k$; because $H^k$ is an algebra, $u_jB_j-A_ju_j\to uB-Au$ in $H^k$. Thus $du_j$ converges in $H^k$ and the local coefficients converge in $H^{k+1}$. The limit satisfies $du=uB-Au$, equivalently $B=A^u$, and $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$.

proof_steps.claim: First solve one equation with all other coordinates regarded as parameters $p$. Write $z_j=\rho w$ on a disk slightly larger than $|w|\le2$, choose a fixed smooth cutoff $\chi$ supported in $|w|<2$ and equal to one for $|w|\le1$, and put $a_\rho(w,p)=\rho A_j(\rho w,p)$. For fixed $0<\alpha<1$, its $C^\alpha_w$ norm is bounded uniformly on a compact parameter polydisc by $C\rho(M_0+\rho M_1)$, where $M_0,M_1$ bound $A_j$ and its first derivatives. Multiplication is bounded in the matrix Hölder norm by the product rule for increments, and [F1] bounds $K(p)u=T(\chi a_\rho u)$ on $C^\alpha(\overline D_2)$. Choose one positive $\rho$ making $\|K(p)\|<1/4$ for every parameter. By [F3], $g=1-K(p)g$ has a unique fixed point; $\|g-1\|\le\|K\|/(1-\|K\|)<1/3$, so $g$ is invertible everywhere. On $|w|<1$, [F1] gives $\partial_{\bar w}g=-a_\rho g$.

The coefficients depend smoothly on parameters as maps into $C^\alpha_w$, since all their parameter derivatives have uniform bounds on compact subsets. The inverse $(1+K(p))^{-1}$ is the uniformly convergent Neumann series; the identity $L(p+h)-L(p)=-L(p+h)(K(p+h)-K(p))L(p)$ for $L=(1+K)^{-1}$ gives its first derivative in operator norm, and induction gives derivatives of every order. Hence $g=L(p)1$ is smoothly parameter-dependent in $C^\alpha_w$. For each such derivative, the fixed-point equation and [F1] gain one $w$ derivative; induction gives all mixed $C^{m,\alpha}_w$ derivatives on the same radius, because only the inverse in the initial $C^\alpha$ space needs smallness. Thus $g$ is jointly smooth. If $A_j$ is holomorphic in an untouched coordinate, $K$ has zero antiholomorphic parameter derivative by [F2], and differentiating the inverse identity gives the same for $g$.

Gauge by this $g$ on the smaller disk. The transformed coefficient is $A_i'=g^{-1}(\partial_{\bar z_i}g+A_i g)$, and $A_j'=0$. The square-zero condition in a smooth frame is $\partial_{\bar z_i}A_j-\partial_{\bar z_j}A_i+[A_i,A_j]=0$, and it is preserved by the gauge transformation by direct conjugation of $(D'')^2$. Therefore every remaining $A_i'$ is holomorphic in $z_j$. Kill the next coordinate by steps 1.1–2.1 with a cutoff only in that coordinate. Their holomorphic-parameter assertion preserves $A_j'=0$. Continue through the finitely many coordinates, shrinking the respective coordinate disks as needed. The product of the resulting smooth invertible gauges has all transformed coefficients zero, proving the required local frame.

If $G$ and $H$ are two such frames, $D''G=D''H=0$ gives $\bar\partial(G^{-1}H)=0$. For smooth scalar functions this implies holomorphy: the one-variable Cauchy formula applies with the other variables fixed, and its iterated integral on a product of small circles gives a locally convergent joint power series. Thus the transition matrices are holomorphic, giving [F4]'s bundle structure; any other structure with the same $D''$ has the same class of holomorphic frames, hence agrees. In these frames an intertwining smooth bundle map has matrix $M$ with $\bar\partial M=0$, so is holomorphic by the same calculation, and the converse follows by the Leibniz rule. Rank zero is immediate and the finite gauge induction covers every positive finite rank.

proof_steps.claim: For a finite-type algebraic base $S$, tensor the relative diagonal Koszul resolution by the flat family and use the assumed base-change isomorphisms [A1]. The direct-image terms are vector bundles of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, and the finite filtered complex commutes with residue-field restriction. On every fiber, step 6.1 gives the monad. The right end map is surjective on every fiber, hence surjective by Nakayama [F8], and its kernel $K$ is locally free. Locally on $S$, write the remaining exact sequence as $0\to P^{-1}\to K\to\mathcal E\to0$, with $P^{-1}$ and $K$ flat over the base. Tensoring by any residue field $k(s)$ stays injective at the left because the fiber complex is a monad on the whole projective plane. Thus $\operatorname{Tor}_1^{\mathcal O_{S,s}}(k(s),\mathcal E)=0$, equivalently the maximal-ideal multiplication map is injective. Since $\mathcal E$ is finite over the local ring of $\mathbb P^2\times S$, [F6] proves flatness over $S$. The same base-change maps identify the relative middle cohomology with the given family. This is precisely the family range stated and does not assert base change outside it.

proof_steps.claim: Chirality anticommutes with $D_4$ and is parallel, so $D_5^2=D_4^2-\partial_t^2$. It has scalar positive principal symbol and smooth coefficients. Formal symmetry follows from unitary connection compatibility and periodic integration by parts. The same shifted-resolvent argument applies to $D_4$ and $D_5$ on a general compact background: each square has scalar positive principal symbol, and [F2] gives the inverse of its positive shift from $L^2$ to $H^2$; multiplying by $D_j\mp i$ gives surjectivity of $D_j\pm i$ and the $H^1$ selfadjoint domain exactly as in [F1]. An $L^2$ weak chiral cokernel vector also has square zero distributionally; testing against smooth sections and using their $H^2$ density puts it in the adjoint domain of the selfadjoint square, hence in $H^2$, and [F2] then makes it smooth. This justifies identifying the cokernel with the negative-chirality kernel. Weak kernels are smooth by the same argument. For a zero mode $\psi$, integration by parts gives $0=\|D_5\psi\|^2=\|D_4\psi\|^2+\|\partial_t\psi\|^2$. Thus $\psi$ is independent of $t$ and lies in $\ker D_4$; conversely every such spinor gives a periodic product zero mode. In general its complex dimension is $n_++n_-$, identifying the smooth negative-chirality kernel with the cokernel by the formal $L^2$ adjoint. For the concrete round twist this dimension is $1$ by [F1]. This avoids any unproved general spectral-flow identity.

proof_steps.claim: Fix $r\in\{1,2,3\}$. In the first sequence of [F1], the map $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)\to H^0(\mathbb P^{r-1},\mathcal O)$ is restriction of constants and hence is the identity $\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$. Exactness therefore gives $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(-1))=0$. The adjacent higher groups of $\mathcal O$ and $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^{r-1}}$ vanish by [A1]; the long exact sequence then gives $H^q(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ for every $q>0$.

proof_steps.claim:
Pull back $0\to U_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to K'\to F'\to0$ along $K\to F\xrightarrow f F'$. Its extension obstruction and ambiguity are respectively
$H^1(K^*\otimes U_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1))$ and $H^0(K^*\otimes U_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1))$. Dualizing the first sequence of step 1.1 and tensoring by $U_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1)$ gives
$$
0\to (U')^*\otimes U_1\otimes\mathcal O(-2)\to S^*\otimes U_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to K^*\otimes U_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to0.
$$
The long exact sequence and [F2] make both groups zero, so the lift $\phi:K\to K'$ exists and is unique.

Extend $\phi$ across $K\hookrightarrow S\otimes\mathcal O$ using $0\to K'\to S_1\otimes\mathcal O\to U_1'\otimes\mathcal O(1)\to0$. The obstruction and ambiguity are $H^1((U')^*\otimes S_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1))$ and $H^0((U')^*\otimes S_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1))$, both zero by [F2]. Hence there is a unique middle map $g:S\otimes\mathcal O\to S_1\otimes\mathcal O$ extending $\phi$.

The restriction $g\alpha$ lands in $\operatorname{im}\alpha'$ because its class in $F'$ is $f$ applied to the zero class of $\alpha$. Since $\alpha'$ is injective, this defines a unique map $p:U\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to U_1\otimes\mathcal O(-1)$. Since $\beta'g$ vanishes on $K$, it factors uniquely through $(S\otimes\mathcal O)/K\cong U'\otimes\mathcal O(1)$, defining the third chain map. The chain equations hold by construction. Every matrix entry of these maps is a global holomorphic section of $\mathcal O$, hence is constant by [F2]. Any other lift agrees on $K$ by step 1.2 and on $S$ by step 1.3; injectivity of $\alpha'$ and surjectivity of $\beta$ then force equality of both end maps.

By step 1.4, $h_F$ has a unique chain lift $h=(p,H,r):M\to D(M)$. The displayed diagram records its two chain equations; it is notation only, and the equations and uniqueness are established in the text.
$$
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large]
U\otimes\mathcal O(-1) \arrow[r,"\alpha"] \arrow[d,"p"'] &
S\otimes\mathcal O \arrow[r,"\beta"] \arrow[d,"H"] &
U'\otimes\mathcal O(1) \arrow[d,"r"]\\
(U')^*\otimes\mathcal O(-1) \arrow[r,"-\beta^\#"'] &
S^*\otimes\mathcal O \arrow[r,"\alpha^\#"'] &
U^*\otimes\mathcal O(1)
\end{tikzcd}
$$
Thus the squares assert $H\alpha=-\beta^\#p$ and $r\beta=\alpha^\#H$. Its dual $D(h)$ lifts the same self-pairing, so uniqueness gives $h=D(h)$; in particular $H=H^\dagger$ and the end maps are adjoints under the pairing's identifications. The lift is an isomorphism: lift $h_F^{-1}$ by step 1.4 and use uniqueness to identify both composites with the identity lift. The middle map $H$ is therefore nondegenerate. In bases identifying the end spaces by this lift, the chain equation is $H\alpha(z)=-\beta(jz)^\dagger$. Replacing $z$ by $jz$ and using linearity in homogeneous coordinates yields both displayed identities in the Statement.

Since $K\subseteq S\otimes\mathcal O$ and $H^0(\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$, every global section of $K$ is a constant vector $s\in S$. Its image in $F$ is a global section exactly when $\beta(z)s=0$ for every $z$, equivalently $\beta_i s=0$ for every coefficient. Hence $H^0(F)=L$.

proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition.

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step.

The compact family $f(\overline U_2)$ is uniformly stable under a sufficiently small $C^1$ perturbation: each member has the finite-loop positive margin in [F2], and a finite subcover gives one positive tolerance. Include this $C^1$ norm among the finitely many seminorms in which all forthcoming approximations are to be small.

Such a cutoff follows from finitely many ambient bumps separating the two compact sets. Define on $K$ the continuous family $h(s)=f(s)+\theta(s)(g(s)-f(s))$. The straight interpolation from $f$ to $h$ is fixed near $L$ and is $\delta$-small in every selected seminorm. By the uniform $C^1$ margin in step 1.1, choosing $\delta$ small ensures it is irreducible on $\overline U_2$. Its closed reducible-parameter set $R=\{s\in K:h(s)\notin\mathcal A_\infty^*\}$ is compact and contained in $K\setminus U_2$, hence in the ambient open region where $\theta=1$ and $h=g$ on $K$. If $R$ is empty the first interpolation already proves the result. Otherwise choose an ambient open $W$ with compact closure in $V\cap\{\theta=1\}$, containing $R$ and avoiding a neighborhood of $L$, and a smooth cutoff $0\le\chi\le1$ with compact support $T\subset W$, positive on $R$. Choosing a basis of $V_1$ and using the fixed framed basis of $W$ identifies $M=V\oplus V\oplus W$ and the line maps with the two Euler blocks in the Statement. The remaining coefficients of the two linear maps are their $z_0$ coefficients, so write $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0C_1+z_2,z_0C_2-z_1,z_0I)$. Under the stated relative cohomology and base-change hypotheses, the same constructions use vector bundles and are inverse for families.

Then $G(C_t(x))$ is a homotopy from $G$ to the constant map at $A$ that fixes $x_0$ and remains in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$. Restricting it to $S^j$ gives a based nullhomotopy of $u$; by [F3], its class in $\pi_j(\mathcal A_\infty^*,A)$ is zero. Since $j$ and $u$ were arbitrary, every stated homotopy group vanishes.

final_edge_fact_uses.text:
[A1] Under full AC, the batch-67 scalar cohomology theorem states
$H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$ and
$H^q(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0$ for $q>0$ for $0\le r\le3$.
[[thm-qftx-gaga-analytic-projective-dolbeault-scalar-cohomology]]

proof_steps.claim: First the holomorphic monad maps have homogeneous linear entries. Indeed, in the $m=1$ sequence of [F10], $H^1(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0$ by [A1], so restriction $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(1))\to H^0(\mathbb P^{r-1},\mathcal O(1))$ is surjective and its kernel is the defining hyperplane coordinate times $H^0(\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$. Starting with $r=0$, where $\mathcal O(1)$ on a point has one-dimensional section space, induction shows that every section is a linear combination of the homogeneous coordinates: subtract the global coordinate lifts of its restriction, then the remaining section is a constant multiple of the defining coordinate. This applies to entries of both $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O(-1),\mathcal O)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O,\mathcal O(1))$. Thus no algebraic/analytic comparison is needed to introduce their four coefficient maps. By [A1] and [F9], the hyperplane sequences and analytic scalar theorem give exactly the negative-twist vanishings required by [F1]. Apply [F1] to the pairing isomorphism; it gives the unique constant Hermitian lift $H$ with the signed identities there. Thus no algebraic cohomology group is being substituted for the analytic lifting groups.

For the algebraic $\mathbb P^3_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2]$ family category, [F11] directly supplies the needed $\mathcal O(-1)$ and $\mathcal O(-2)$ groups over $A$ and $H^0(\mathcal O_A)=A$. Separately, on the analytic first-order thickening each twist has the split underlying analytic sheaf $\mathcal O_A(d)=\mathcal O(d)\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O(d)$; finite direct sums commute with sheaf cohomology, so [F9] gives the same vanishings there. Thus a holomorphic family pairing can be lifted analytically, whereas algebraic family sheaves use [F11]; neither computation substitutes algebraic cohomology for an analytic group or invokes GAGA. Both yield constant $A$-valued chain maps. In both categories the two kernel/image sequences identify global sections with the same constant coefficient kernel of $\beta_A$, so the specified global-section base-change condition is respected by this identification. Repeating the obstruction and ambiguity calculation of [F1] over these coefficient modules lifts the family pairing uniquely to an $A$-linear constant chain isomorphism with Hermitian middle matrix $H_A$; its inverse exists because its reduction is invertible. Global section base change identifies $H^0(F_A)$ with the constant coefficient kernel $L_A$ in $S_A$. Its reduction is injective, so a full-rank minor is a unit and $L_A$ is a direct summand.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A5] For $0\le r\le3$, the analytic Dolbeault resolution computes holomorphic vector-bundle cohomology, and $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$, $H^q(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0$ for $q>0$. Arbitrary coherent positive-twist vanishing and generation are derived below, not assumed in this scalar input. [[thm-qftx-gaga-analytic-projective-dolbeault-scalar-cohomology]]

proof_steps.claim: Suppose the absolute theorem has been proved in dimensions below $r$, where $1\le r\le3$. For $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}$ the natural comparison is an isomorphism by [A5] and [F3]. The exact hyperplane sequences $0\to\mathcal O(m-1)\xrightarrow{x_0}\mathcal O(m)\to i_*\mathcal O_H(m)\to0$ exist on both sides by step 1.1, and their cohomology maps commute with analytification. For $m\ge1$, assume comparison at $m-1$. The lower-dimensional comparison and [F3] give $H^q(H,\mathcal O_H(m))=0$ for $q>0$; the sequence therefore gives analytic higher vanishing at $m$ and an exact sequence on global sections. Every homogeneous degree-$m$ polynomial on $H$ extends by the same polynomial in $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ on $\mathbb P^r$; the kernel of restriction is $x_0$ times the degree-$m-1$ polynomials. The natural map of these exact section sequences is an isomorphism at its outer terms, hence also at its middle term by [F4]. This proves the natural comparison for all $m\ge0$ without using GAGA in dimension $r$.

For the negative twists, the sequence $0\to\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O\to i_*\mathcal O_H\to0$ has restriction $\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ equal to the identity in degree zero and no positive cohomology in the two right terms by [A5] and lower-dimensional comparison. Thus analytic $\mathcal O(-1)$ is acyclic, as is its algebraic counterpart by [F3]. For every $m<-1$, multiplication by a power of $x_0$ injects the line bundle $\mathcal O(m)$ into $\mathcal O(-1)$: in each analytic chart its local equation is a nonzero holomorphic function in the integral holomorphic germ ring, so multiplication is injective. Hence $H^0(\mathcal O(m))=0$. Descend using $0\to\mathcal O(m)\to\mathcal O(m+1)\to i_*\mathcal O_H(m+1)\to0$. Comparison is already known at $m+1$ and on the hyperplane at every twist. For $q\ge1$, the four neighbors in $H^{q-1}(\mathcal O(m+1))\to H^{q-1}(\mathcal O_H(m+1))\to H^q(\mathcal O(m))\to H^q(\mathcal O(m+1))\to H^q(\mathcal O_H(m+1))$ are therefore naturally compared isomorphically, so [F4] gives the middle comparison. This also handles $r=1$, where the point hyperplane's negative twists still have a one-dimensional section space; they were not incorrectly set to zero. Thus all integer twists have canonical cohomology comparison, without analytic Serre duality or an affine finite-pole assertion.

For an algebraic finite-type base map $S'\to S$, apply the same class-pullback construction to the pulled-back family. Tensor associativity identifies its analytification with the analytic pullback family. The square of the two comparison morphisms and the algebraic and analytic base-change maps commutes, since all maps pull back the same local cohomology classes and [F6] respects compositions. Whenever both families satisfy the Statement's locally-free and fiber-base-change hypotheses, step 12.1 makes their comparison morphisms invertible, so it identifies their base-change maps. This proves the complete stated family range, including the closed-fiber maps, without asserting arbitrary analytic-family algebraization. Full AC is inherited through [F1] and the resolution construction [F5]. The exact analytic suppliers [A1], [A3]–[A5] remain prerequisite proof obligations until their actual carriers are checked; the internal Serre argument above does not certify them.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F4] Proper pushforward is functorial, closed inclusions are proper, and cap product with an equivariant cohomology class sends $[X]_T$ to Borel–Moore degree $2d-q$. [[def-qftx-localized-equivariant-borel-moore-data]]

proof_steps.claim: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper $T$-equivariant map between smooth separated finite-type varieties with finite invariant affine covers and proper fixed loci $F_X,F_Y$. Its restriction $f^T:F_X\to F_Y$ is proper, and the square formed by $i_X,i_Y,f^T,f$ commutes because $f$ sends fixed points to fixed points. Functoriality of proper Borel–Moore pushforward gives $f_*i_{X*}=i_{Y*}f^T_*$. After localization both $i_{X*}$ and $i_{Y*}$ are isomorphisms by [F2], so applying their inverses and then the proper traces proves $p_{Y*}^{\mathrm{loc}}f_*=p_{X*}^{\mathrm{loc}}$. If $X\to\mathrm{pt}$ itself is proper, then $p_{F*}=p_{X*}i_*$; composing with $i_*^{-1}$ proves $p_*^{\mathrm{loc}}=p_{X*}$.

Let $ eta=(i_*)^{-1}(\alpha\cap[X]_T)$. On each component, the complex orientation and refined Gysin map give $i_a^!(\alpha\cap[X]_T)=i_a^*\alpha\cap[F_a]_T$. Since $\alpha\cap[X]_T=i_* eta$, the self-intersection formula [F3] gives $e_T(
u_a)\cap eta_a=i_a^*\alpha\cap[F_a]_T$. Properness of $F_a$ makes $e_T(
u_a)$ invertible after localization by [F3], hence $ eta_a=(i_a^*\alpha/e_T(
u_a))\cap[F_a]_T$. Applying $p_{a*}$ and summing the finitely many components yields the displayed formula. The degree is $2d-q$: division by the degree-$2c_a$ Euler class lowers the localized cohomological degree of the insertion from $q$ to $q-2c_a$, and capping with the degree-$2d_a$ fundamental class gives $2d_a-(q-2c_a)=2d-q$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] For the stated Sobolev index, the smooth irreducible projection $\mathcal A_\infty^*\to\mathcal A_\infty^*/\overline{\mathcal G}_\infty$ is a locally trivial topological principal $\overline{\mathcal G}_\infty$-bundle with its actual $C^\infty$ quotient topology; the Sobolev irreducible locus $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open. [[thm-qftx-sobolev-smooth-irreducible-gauge-bundle]]

proof_steps.claim: Choose the fixed integer $k>r/2+1$. The smooth clause of [F3], applied with the configuration data [F2], makes $q_*$ a locally trivial principal $\overline{\mathcal G}^\infty(P)$-bundle. By [F4], its total space is nonempty, path connected, and has $\pi_j=0$ for every $j\ge1$, so it is weakly contractible in the sense used in [F6]. For a constant central gauge section $u=\zeta I_N$, the local action formula gives $A^u=A$ because $u^{-1}Au=A$ and $du=0$; hence reduced and full gauge groups have the same orbits on $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)$.

The locus $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)$ is gauge invariant: in the chosen frame, the based holonomy subgroup of $A^u$ is $u(p_m)^{-1}\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)u(p_m)$, so it has the same invariant subspaces up to conjugation. It is open: by [F2], the inclusion $\mathcal A^\infty(P)\hookrightarrow\mathcal A_k(P)$ is continuous, as each fixed $H^k$ norm is bounded by finitely many smooth derivative seminorms on the finite compact atlas. The smooth irreducible locus is the inverse image of the Sobolev irreducible locus, which is open by [F3]. The full orbit projection $q$ is open because, for any open $U\subseteq\mathcal A^\infty(P)$, its saturation $q^{-1}(q(U))=\bigcup_{u\in\mathcal G^\infty(P)}U\cdot u$ is open. For fixed smooth $u$, the map $A\mapsto u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$ is continuous in every finite-atlas derivative seminorm by the Leibniz rule; its inverse is the same formula for $u^{-1}$, so each gauge translate is a homeomorphism. Therefore $q(\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P))$ is open and $q|_{\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)}$ is an open quotient map onto this subset. The reduced and full actions have the same orbits there, so their quotient topologies identify the reduced orbit space homeomorphically with $q(\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P))$; this proves the claim about $\iota$ in the Statement. If $q$ had a continuous section, its restriction to this open subset would take each irreducible orbit to a point in that same orbit, hence into $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)$. Via the stated homeomorphism, this would give a continuous section of $q_*$, contradicting step 3.1. Thus $q$ has no continuous section.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F6] For a smooth-coefficient elliptic operator on a compact manifold, distributional solutions gain two Sobolev derivatives when the right-hand side gains the corresponding Sobolev order, with the stated elliptic estimate. [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]]

proof_steps.claim: For the smooth-space clause, fix now a smooth irreducible center $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and use the Banach slice and trivialization established in step 4.1. Put $U_A=\Phi_A(S_{A,\varepsilon}\times\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1})$ and $V_A=\pi_k(S_{A,\varepsilon})$. Since $U_A$ is open in $\mathcal A_k^*$, $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open in the stated $C^\infty$ topology; set $S_A^\infty=S_{A,\varepsilon}\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and $V_A^\infty=\pi_\infty(S_A^\infty)$. For a smooth $B\in U_A$, its unique reduced gauge class from step 4.1 has a representative $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$. It satisfies $d_A^*(B^{u^{-1}}-A)=0$. Locally in a bundle frame, write $C_j=uB_j u^{-1}-(\partial_j u)u^{-1}-A_j$. Substitution in $d_A^*C=0$, use of $\partial_i(u^{-1})=-u^{-1}(\partial_i u)u^{-1}$, and multiplication on the right by $u$ isolate the equation $g^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j u=R(A,B,g;u,u^{-1},du)$ on each chart. Every term in $R$ is a finite product of smooth coefficients (including first derivatives of $A,B$) and factors among $u,u^{-1},du$; hence the principal operator is the scalar smooth Laplacian on each matrix entry. If $u\in H^{r+1}$ for $r\ge k$, then this right-hand side lies in $H^r$ by [F7] and the smooth coefficient bounds. Elliptic regularity [F6] gives $u\in H^{r+2}$. Iteration proves $u$ smooth; changing its representative by an element of the finite center preserves smoothness. Thus every smooth point of the Banach saturation has a smooth trivialization representative, and $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*=\pi_\infty^{-1}(V_A^\infty)$.

Suppose smooth $B_j\to B$ in $C^\infty$ within $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$. The Banach trivialization from step 4.1 gives convergence of their slice representatives in $H^k$ and of their reduced gauge classes in $H^{k+1}$. In a quotient chart around the limiting class from step 1.1, choose lifts $u_j,u$ that converge in $H^{k+1}$; this is possible because the finite center acts by disjoint translates. The equation in step 5.2 and elliptic estimates [F6] bootstrap convergence: if $u_j\to u$ in $H^{r+1}$, then the assumed $C^\infty$ convergence gives $B_j\to B$ in $H^{r+1}$, and [F7] makes the right-hand sides converge in $H^r$. Apply the elliptic estimate to $u_j-u$, using also their already known $H^{k+1}$ convergence for the $L^2$ term, to get $u_j\to u$ in $H^{r+2}$. Induction gives convergence in every Sobolev order, which on compact $M$ is the $C^\infty$ section topology. The slice representatives converge in $C^\infty$ by their action formula. Conversely the forward action is continuous in the $C^\infty$ topology by multiplication and differentiation of smooth sections. The saturation $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open, and $V_A^\infty$ is open in the quotient because the quotient map is open: the saturation of any open set is a union of its open gauge translates. The restricted map $S_A^\infty\times\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty\to\pi_\infty^{-1}(V_A^\infty)$ is therefore a homeomorphism for the actual quotient topology, and it is equivariant. This proves the smooth-space topological principal bundle claim.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[lem-qftx-taubes-disk-barriers-and-monotone-iteration]]: for every exhausting disk $D_R$, it supplies $u_R$ with $u_-\le u_R\le0$, the exact divisor equation and smooth center subtraction, plus $R$-uniform local $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,\alpha}$ bounds after subtracting the fixed logarithmic singular function $s$.

proof_steps.claim: Choose radii $R_k\to\infty$ with every center in $D_{R_k}$. Let $s=2\sum_jm_j\log|z-z_j|$ and $w_k=u_{R_k}-s$. For each compact disk $K$ and each $0<\alpha<1$, [F2] gives a uniform $C^{2,\alpha}$ bound on $w_k$ on a slightly larger disk. Thus $(w_k,Dw_k,D^2w_k)$ is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous there. Apply the Euclidean sequence statement [F6] to the finite derivative tuple on each nonempty compact disk. A countable diagonal selection under [A1] then gives locally uniform convergence of $w_k$ and all its derivatives through order two. The fundamental theorem of calculus on coordinate segments identifies the limiting derivative tuple as the first and second derivatives of one $C^2$ function w. Thus the subsequence converges in $C^2$ on every compact disk. Set $h=s+w$.

On every compact set, $e^{u_{R_k}}=e^s e^{w_k}$ converges uniformly to $e^h$. Passing to the limit in the weak divisor equation for $u_{R_k}$ gives $\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=4\pi D$ distributionally. Since $s-2m_j\log|z-z_j|$ is smooth near each center and $w$ is $C^2$ there, the prescribed logarithmic subtraction extends continuously. The equation for $w$ is $\Delta w=\kappa(e^s e^w-1)$ with smooth coefficient $e^s=|P|^2$; repeated interior Schauder regularity [F4] bootstraps $w$ to $C^\infty$, so each center subtraction is smooth. The bounds $u_-\le u_{R_k}\le0$ pass to the limit, and $u_-(z)\to0$ at infinity; hence $h\le0$ and $h\to0$.

proof_steps.claim: The rational character formula is [F2]. The constant central automorphism acts by $-1$ on both chiral spinor kernels and cokernels, and fixes the background connection. Its scalar on the inverse determinant line is $(-1)^{-n_+}(-1)^{n_-}=(-1)^{n_+-n_-}$. For the actual round twist [F1] gives dimensions one and zero, hence scalar $-1$. Parallel transport along a constant path is the identity for any connection. Closing by the inverse endpoint identification gives $z_*^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}=-1$; tensor powers give $(-1)^N$. This is an actual finite-dimensional exterior-power action, not an assumption equating a periodic eta invariant with holonomy.

For any finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with anti-linear involution $J$, every $v$ has the unique decomposition $v=(v+Jv)/2+i(v-Jv)/(2i)$ with both displayed real components fixed by $J$. A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. fact_uses.text: [L10] If $\sigma:F\to F'$ is a field isomorphism, $0\ne f\in F[x]$ and $E/F$, $E'/F'$ are splitting fields of $f$ and $\sigma_*f$, then $\sigma$ extends to an isomorphism $E\to E'$ ([[thm-isomorphisms-extend-to-splitting-fields]]).

proof_steps.claim: The extension $E/F$ is purely inseparable, and $E=F$ in characteristic zero. Since $M/F$ is finite it is algebraic by [L8], and by [L1] and [L9] $M$ is a splitting field over $F$ of the product $p_1\cdots p_n$ of the minimal polynomials of a finite generating list of $M/F$. Let $a\in E$ with minimal polynomial $q$ over $F$, and let $b\in M$ be any root of $q$. The assignment $a\mapsto b$ defines an isomorphism $F(a)\to F(b)$ of $F$-extensions: the $F$-algebra map $F[T]\to M$ with $T\mapsto b$ kills $q$ and so factors through $F[T]/(q)\cong F(a)$ by [L13], and it is injective because $F(a)$ is a field. Moreover $M$ is a splitting field of $p_1\cdots p_n$ over both $F(a)$ and $F(b)$, since all roots of the $p_j$ lie in $M$ and generate it over $F$, hence also over each of these intermediate fields. By [L10] applied over the base field $F(a)$ the isomorphism $a\mapsto b$ extends to an isomorphism $M\to M$, which is an $F$-automorphism because it fixes $F$; so $b=\sigma(a)=a$ for this $\sigma\in G$, since $a$ lies in the fixed field $E$. Hence $q$ has exactly one distinct root in $M$, and by normality of $M/F$ it has all its roots in $M$ by [L6]. If $F$ has characteristic $p>0$, write $q(T)=g(T^{p^{e}})$ as in [L11] with $g$ irreducible and separable; the distinct roots of $q$ in $M$ correspond bijectively to the roots of $g$ in $M$, because $z\mapsto z^{p^{e}}$ is injective by [L12], so $g$ has exactly one root and $\deg g=1$; writing $g(T)=T-\beta$ with $\beta\in F$ gives $q(T)=T^{p^{e}}-\beta$ and hence $a^{p^{e}}=\beta\in F$. Thus every element of $E$ has a $p$-power in $F$, so $E/F$ is purely inseparable by [L12]. If instead $F$ has characteristic zero, then the irreducible $q$ is separable by [L11], so $q$ has $\deg q$ distinct roots in $M$ by [L7]; having exactly one root forces $\deg q=1$ and $a\in F$. Hence $E=F$ in characteristic zero. This proves all three clauses of the statement.

proof_steps.claim: Substituting that representative in [F3] gives $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ and $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,z_0)$. Their product is $-z_2z_1+z_1z_2=0$. The row $\beta$ is surjective at every projective point because its three entries have no common zero, and $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map because it is nonzero away from $p$. Let $K=\ker\beta$. Projection to the third coordinate restricts to a morphism $\gamma:K\to\mathcal O$. On the affine chart $z_0=1$, put $x=z_1$ and $y=z_2$; a vector in $K$ has the form $(u,v,-yu+xv)$, so $\gamma(K)=(x,y)$ and its kernel is generated by $(-x,-y,0)$, the image of $\alpha$. On any chart away from $p$ where $z_1$ or $z_2$ is a unit, the same equations show that $\gamma$ is onto and its kernel is generated by $\alpha$. Hence $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha\cong I_p$ globally, where $I_p$ is the ideal sheaf of $p$.

At $p$, the local ideal $(x,y)$ is not principal: if it were generated by one element in the regular local ring $\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x,y)}$, its quotient by the maximal ideal would have dimension at most one, whereas $(x,y)/(x,y)^2$ has dimension two. Therefore $I_p$ is not locally free at $p$. Its framing on $L_\infty$ is the canonical trivialization because $p\notin L_\infty$. This exhibits a positive-FI stable point outside the costable, locally-free zero-FI locus; the correspondence with ordinary ASD moduli is restricted to that zero-FI locus and does not absorb this boundary point.

Substitution in the raw homogeneous formulas gives the displayed

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[lem-qftx-stable-adhm-partition-fixed-points-and-tangent-character]]: the stable positive-FI ADHM quotient is smooth, separated and finite-type, with a finite invariant affine cover, finite reduced partition fixed locus, and the stated dual-framing tangent character. It assumes full AC and asserts neither a sheaf/ASD dictionary nor an integration identity.

proof_steps.claim: For $k=1$ and $N=2$, the only partition pairs are $((\Box),\varnothing)$ and $(\varnothing,(\Box))$. Substituting their characters into [F2] gives the tangent characters $t_1+t_2+e_2/e_1+t_1t_2e_1/e_2$ and $t_1+t_2+e_1/e_2+t_1t_2e_2/e_1$, respectively. Their ADHM-convention weights have Euler products $$E_1^{\mathrm A}=\epsilon_1\epsilon_2(b_2-b_1)(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2+b_1-b_2),\qquad E_2^{\mathrm A}=\epsilon_1\epsilon_2(b_1-b_2)(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2+b_2-b_1),$$ where $b_\alpha=a_\alpha^{\mathrm A}=c_1^T(e_\alpha)$. Substituting $b_\alpha=-a_\alpha^{\mathrm P}$ gives $E_1^{\mathrm A}=\epsilon_1\epsilon_2(a_2^{\mathrm P}-a_1^{\mathrm P}+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)(a_1^{\mathrm P}-a_2^{\mathrm P})$ and $E_2^{\mathrm A}=\epsilon_1\epsilon_2(a_1^{\mathrm P}-a_2^{\mathrm P}+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)(a_2^{\mathrm P}-a_1^{\mathrm P})$, exactly the two source denominators in $C_1$.

For the first one-box tuple, the contributing weights in the displayed Nekrasov factor are $E_{11}=\epsilon_2$ and $E_{12}=a_2^{\mathrm P}-a_1^{\mathrm P}+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2$. Thus its hypermultiplet numerator is $(\epsilon_1-\widetilde m)(\epsilon_2-\widetilde m)(a_2^{\mathrm P}-a_1^{\mathrm P}+\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2-\widetilde m)(a_1^{\mathrm P}-a_2^{\mathrm P}-\widetilde m)$, and its vector denominator is $E_1^{\mathrm A}$ from step 1.1. For the second color the two Coulomb weights interchange and the denominator is $E_2^{\mathrm A}$. Adding these two fixed-point contributions gives exactly $C_1$ in the Example. This is the finite fixed-point evaluation of the mathematical tangent-twist insertion.

Let $X_k$ be the stable $U(2)$ ADHM quotient in [F2], of complex dimension $4k$. Extend its torus by a flavor factor $\mathbb C^\times_f$ acting trivially on $X_k$, and let $L_{-\widetilde m}$ be its character line with additive first Chern class $-\widetilde m$. The global insertion is $\alpha_{\widetilde m}=e_{T\times\mathbb C^\times_f}(TX_k\otimes L_{-\widetilde m})$, capped with the complex-oriented fundamental class $[X_k]$. The finite invariant affine atlas remains invariant under this trivial base action; the fixed locus remains finite reduced, hence proper. Every hypothesis of [F4] therefore holds. A point with tangent weights $w_j$ contributes $\prod_j(w_j-\widetilde m)/\prod_jw_j$ to $p_*^{\mathrm{loc}}(\alpha_{\widetilde m}\cap[X_k])$. For $k=1$ these are the four weights at each of the two points in steps 1.1–2.1, giving exactly $C_1$. For $k=0$, $X_0$ is a point, both Euler products are empty and the coefficient is $1$. Thus the mathematical noncompact localized-pushforward coefficient is proved. Identifying this insertion with the physical hypermultiplet sector is the sourced pole prescription [A3], not a consequence of equivariant cohomology.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-qftx-superconformal-index]]: $\Delta=E-2J_2-\tfrac32R$, $J_+=J_1+J_2+R/2$, $J_-=J_2-J_1+R/2$, and the admissible weighted supertrace is the signed $p^{J_+}q^{J_-}$ trace on $\ker\Delta$ when its weighted diagonal sum converges.

proof_steps.claim: For the scalar letter, $\Delta=E-2J_2-\tfrac32R=1-0-1=0$ and $J_+=J_-=1/3$, so its signed fugacity weight is $(pq)^{1/3}$.

For $\bar\psi_{\dot +}$, $\Delta=\tfrac32-1-\tfrac12=0$ and $J_+=J_-=\tfrac12+\tfrac16=2/3$; its fermion parity contributes the negative weight $-(pq)^{2/3}$. Each $D_p$ adds one to $J_+$ and zero to $J_-$, while each $D_q$ adds zero to $J_+$ and one to $J_-$, and both preserve $\Delta=0$.

By [A1] and [F1], the trace is the supplied-basis trace of a trace-class weighted heat operator, with absolutely summable diagonal. Put $a=(pq)^{1/3}<1$ and $b=(pq)^{2/3}<1$. The total absolute bosonic and fermionic mode weights are $a/((1-p)(1-q))$ and $b/((1-p)(1-q))$, both finite. Because $-\log(1-x)\le x/(1-a)$ for $0\le x\le a$ and $\log(1+y)\le y$ for $y\ge0$, the absolute Fock partition product converges; hence the signed product and the protected-sector trace converge absolutely. The increasing finite mode sets exhaust all finite-support occupation states, so their absolute occupation sums converge to this finite product and justify the signed infinite trace/product identity. This proves protected-sector convergence for the stated fugacity range; convergence of any additional positive-gap sector remains the independent hypothesis in [A2]. Under that hypothesis, [F2] identifies the protected trace with the full superconformal heat supertrace, independent of $\beta$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-qftx-physical-bps-index]]: for a pure-point graded physical index datum with trace-class heat operators, the Witten index is the absolutely convergent even-minus-odd diagonal sum in a supplied compatible basis.

proof_steps.claim: Thus the heat operator is diagonal with eigenvalues $1,e^{-\beta E_*},e^{-\beta E_*}$ on $(e_0,e_+,e_-)$; it is finite rank and trace class, and this basis is a complete compatible basis for the pure-point datum under the trace conventions using [A1].

By [F1], $W_E(\beta)=\langle e_0,e_0\rangle+e^{-\beta E_*}\langle e_+,e_+\rangle-e^{-\beta E_*}\langle e_-,e_-\rangle=1+e^{-\beta E_*}-e^{-\beta E_*}=1$. The single even zero mode supplies the net index; the positive-energy even/odd pair cancels for every $\beta>0$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F5] Compatible affine schemes glue along open isomorphisms. A finite-presentation polynomial quotient with an invertible full equation-Jacobian minor is smooth of the corresponding relative dimension. A geometric quotient has orbit fibers, quotient topology and regular functions equal to invariant regular functions upstairs. [[thm-gluing-affine-schemes]], [[thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism]], [[def-categorical-and-geometric-quotients-of-classical-varieties]]

proof_steps.claim: Each $S_C$ is the affine scheme cut out in the original matrix space by $\mu=0$ and $C=I$. These equations have jointly surjective derivative: $d\mu=d_1$ is onto by step 2.1, and on its kernel the orbit directions map under $dC$ onto every matrix. Thus the $2k^2$ equation-Jacobian rows are independent and [F5] makes each slice smooth of dimension $2kN$. The transition $s\mapsto D(s)^{-1}\cdot s$ is regular on the principal open $\det D(s)\ne0$; its inverse and the cocycle identities follow from uniqueness of the word normalization. Glue the finitely many affine slices by [F5]. To check separatedness, in $S_C\times S_D$ write the two data as $x,y$, and set $G=C(y)$, $H=D(x)$. They represent the same orbit exactly when $GH=HG=I$, $B_i(y)=GB_i(x)H$, $I(y)=GI(x)$ and $J(y)=J(x)H$. Necessity follows from $C(x)=D(y)=I$ and word-frame equivariance; sufficiency follows because these equations make $G$ invertible with inverse $H$ and give $y=Gx$. These polynomial equations cut out the diagonal in every product of affine charts, hence the glued scheme is separated. In each word-frame product $GL(V)\times S_C$, an invariant regular function is exactly its restriction to $\{I\}\times S_C$ pulled back by projection. Projection is Zariski open: for a principal open in the product, multiply its defining regular function by a power of $\det g$ and expand the resulting polynomial in the matrix entries of $g$; its image is the union of the nonvanishing loci of the resulting coefficient functions on $S_C$. Such functions vanish on all invertible matrices only when that polynomial is zero. Thus the product charts identify invariant regular functions with regular functions on the slice and identify the quotient Zariski topology. These identifications glue on overlaps. This proves the geometric-quotient condition in [F5]. Finally $U_C$ is torus invariant because $\det C(t x)$ is the nonzero character $\det D_C(t)$ times $\det C(x)$. On its slice the torus action is $s\mapsto D_C(t)^{-1}\cdot(t s)$, where $D_C(t)=\operatorname{diag}(e_{\alpha_\ell}t_1^{a_\ell}t_2^{b_\ell})$. Every matrix coordinate transforms by a fixed Laurent character, so this is an algebraic action of $(\mathbb C^*)^{N+2}$ and the finite slice atlas is invariant. The case $k=0$ is the point scheme.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-aqft-local-operator-and-dimension]]: for a finite jet representation, the polynomial algebra is $\operatorname{Sym}(J_{\bar 0}^{*})\otimes\Lambda(J_{\bar 1}^{*})$, and the selected operator space has an explicit finite maximum polynomial field degree.

proof_steps.claim: If $n=0$, the polynomial algebra consists only of constants, so its degree-at-most-$q$ subspace has dimension at most one. If $n>0$, every monomial is indexed by an exponent vector $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ with $0\leq a_j\leq q$ for each $j$, since $\sum_j a_j\leq q$; hence the full degree-at-most-$q$ algebra is spanned by at most $(q+1)^n$ monomials. The exterior generators only reduce this finite set because their exponents are restricted to $0$ or $1$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F5] The exact raw real monad, moment coefficients, regularity/rank equivalence, positive kernel projection, local ASD curvature and framing torus chain factors are proved directly, without the source substitution. [[lem-qftx-raw-adhm-real-twistor-block]]

proof_steps.claim: The entrywise-conjugation counterexample remains valid for the literal source equations; it is not a defect in the raw block supplied by [F5]. The source's displayed M also ends its first block row with P* despite declaring P of size k×N, so that entry has N rows rather than k in general. The reconstructed monad in [F1] is linear with locally free middle bundle, trivial on every real line, and has the positive Hermitian Ward pairing and unitary framing fixed in the definition. Its dimensions are those required by [A1]. Thus, assuming the exact supplier [A1], extract the raw tuple from its intrinsic normal form. Its monad composition vanishes, so [F5]'s polynomial identity makes both raw moment coefficients zero. Full fiber rank on each real line and [F5]'s Gram/rank equivalence identify the locus exactly with stable-and-costable regularity. The intrinsic unitary normalization and inverse-extraction clause in [A1] identify the remaining framed monad changes precisely with $(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ for $g\in U(k)$. The compact-rotation and framing chain maps are exactly those in [F5] and [A1]; first-order naturality is used only in [A1]’s locally-free/base-change range. No arbitrary analytic-family algebraization is inferred. No source-coordinate conjugation or nonexistent universal equivalence is invoked.

Conversely, the regular raw monad in [F5] is a global holomorphic bundle, trivial on every real line, with canonical positive reality: its pairing is induced by the standard Hermitian form on K and β(v)=α(σv)*. It is well-defined on cohomology since kerβ(v) is orthogonal to imα(σv), and on a real line its canonical representatives are kerD with the positive restricted metric; at infinity it is W. Apply the proved local Ward construction to obtain a global framed unitary ASD connection. On the finite chart it equals P d: for a kernel representative v along a D=ker(de) direction, β is constant, so its derivative lies in kerβ; the component of dv orthogonal to kerD lies in im a⊕im b, and β=f(−λ₂,λ₁) forces that component to lie in im(aλ₁+bλ₂)=imα. It therefore vanishes in monad cohomology, leaving exactly P dv. Thus evaluation identifies the projection and Ward connections; the Ward construction supplies the smooth extension and framing at infinity. The normalization of [F3] with determinant reduction [F4] gives k=c₂(E)[S⁴]=−q_N. Under [A1], extraction and construction are inverse on U(k) orbits and framed Ward connections, proving the full claim under the exact normal-form, GAGA and coupled-vanishing hypotheses stated above.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] The Ward transform associates a holomorphic bundle on $Z$ to a framed unitary ASD connection on $S^4$. [[thm-qftx-framed-penrose-ward-correspondence-on-s4]]

proof_steps.claim: Let $\xi\in H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))$. By the assumed injective map $\mathcal P_{\mathcal E}$, its image is a smooth section solving the coupled equation in the Statement. Since $R/6>0$, [F2] makes that image zero, and injectivity gives $\xi=0$. Thus $H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=0$.

Apply the same argument to $\xi^\vee\in H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))$ and the assumed injective map $\mathcal P_{\mathcal E^\vee}$; [F2] gives a zero image and injectivity gives $\xi^\vee=0$. Hence $H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0$, proving both asserted vanishings conditional on the specified transforms.

For the Ward bundle of [F1], the underlying smooth bundle is the twistor pullback and its holomorphic operator is the ordinary vertical derivative and the $A$-horizontal alpha-plane operator by the forward Ward construction. The sphere, incidence and orientation are exactly those of [A1]. Thus [A1] applies directly and gives both stated vanishings, with no additional injective-map assumption and no irreducibility hypothesis. The dual connection is still unitary and ASD, since its curvature is $-F_A^t$ and Hodge star commutes with transpose. The dual holomorphic operator is the induced one, so the dual clause matches as well. This identifies the exact supplier-to-consumer application; it uses the vanishing Statement directly without inferring existence of the conditional transform maps.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A2] Absolute projective GAGA and the universal-line direct-image lemma supply the needed local evaluation and degree-zero base-change maps; they are no longer extra assumed surjectivity inputs. [[thm-qftx-projective-gaga-for-monad-data]], [[lem-qftx-twistor-line-section-direct-image]]

proof_steps.claim: Let $L\cong\mathbb P^1$ be any real twistor line. Its normal bundle in $\mathbb P^3$ is $\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$, and the conormal sequence splits because its extension group is $H^1(\mathcal O(1))^{\oplus2}=0$. Hence $\Omega_Z^1|_L\cong\mathcal O(-2)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}$ and $T_Z|_L\cong\mathcal O(2)\oplus\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$. Since $\Omega_Z^2\cong T_Z(-4)$, each of $\mathcal E(-1)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-3)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-2)|_L$, $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))|_L$, and $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)|_L$ is a sum of negative line bundles. The Serre-dual bundles restrict respectively to $\mathcal E^*(-3)$, $\mathcal E^*(-1)$, $\mathcal E^*(-2)$, $\mathcal E^*\otimes T_Z(-3)$, and $\mathcal E^*\otimes\Omega_Z^1$, also sums of negative line bundles. Every point of $Z$ lies on a real line, so negativity on every such line makes every global section zero. Thus [F6] gives $H^0(Z,F)=0$ and [F5] gives $H^3(Z,F)=0$ for all the listed coefficient bundles $F$.

Choose a plane $P\cong\mathbb P^2$ containing a real twistor line. By [A2] and the direct-image result, an open family of lines near that line has evaluation isomorphisms and hence trivial restrictions of $\mathcal E$. Those lines form a nonempty complex-open subset of the line family of $P$. Choose affine coordinates $(x,y)$ with the original line given by $y=0$. This open family contains the projective lines $y=b$ for all sufficiently small complex $b$, so their union contains a nonempty open subset of $P$. A section of $\mathcal E(-2)|_P$ vanishes on each such line because $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus N})=0$. It therefore vanishes on that open subset. In a connected coordinate chart and holomorphic bundle frame, [F8] makes its zero-germ locus closed as well as open. The plane is connected (any two points lie on a connected projective line), so the section vanishes everywhere; no density assertion for an arbitrary complex-open line family is needed. The divisor sequence $0\to\mathcal E(-3)\to\mathcal E(-2)\to\mathcal E(-2)|_P\to0$ and step 1.1 now give $H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-3))=0$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] For the standard projective cover and $k=0,-1,-r-1$, the actual analytic twisting sheaves have acyclic intersections; their analytic sheaf cohomology is the normally convergent Laurent–Čech complex. For every integer twist, restrictions preserve Laurent coefficients and the stated mode contractions converge on the output charts. [[lem-qftx-gaga-projective-cover-laurent-cohomology]]

proof_steps.claim: A global section of $\mathcal O(-k)$, $k=1,2$, would have an entire coefficient $f_0(t)$ with $f_0(t)=t^{-k}f_\infty(1/t)$. By the normally convergent expansions in [F2], the left side has only powers $t^n$ with $n\ge0$, whereas the right side has only powers $t^n$ with $n\le-k$. Uniqueness of Laurent coefficients forces every coefficient to vanish. Thus both degree-zero groups vanish.

A one-cochain on the two-chart overlap has a normally convergent Laurent expansion $g(t)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}a_nt^n$. Coboundaries subtract the entire $t$-series with $n\ge0$ and the series $t^{-k}f_\infty(1/t)$ with $n\le-k$. These two tails converge on their respective entire charts by [F2]; the cover is acyclic for both twists because $r=1$ and $k=1,2$. For $k=1$ they exhaust every integer exponent, so the analytic first cohomology is zero. For $k=2$ the sole remaining exponent is $n=-1$; its coefficient cannot be a coboundary, and it identifies the analytic first cohomology with $\mathbb C$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] For every finite-rank holomorphic bundle $G$ on $\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$, $0\le r\le3$, analytic sheaf cohomology is canonically the global smooth Dolbeault quotient. [[thm-qftx-gaga-analytic-projective-dolbeault-scalar-cohomology]]

proof_steps.claim: By [A1], a sheaf class has a global smooth closed representative $\alpha$. Its vertical restriction has harmonic part $s(x)\sigma_x$, where $s(x)=\int_{L_x}\iota_x(\alpha_V)$ componentwise in $E_x$. This is smooth by integration over compact fibres. Solve $\gamma_x=B(\alpha_V-s\sigma_x)$; then $\bar\partial_V\gamma_x=\alpha_V-s\sigma_x$. Step 2.1 makes $\gamma$ smooth. A change of unit quaternionic frame acts by an $SU(2)$ fibre isometry and a change of unitary $E$ frame acts by a matrix constant on each fibre; both preserve the equation. Uniqueness from $H^{0,0}(\mathcal O(-2))=0$ makes these local solutions agree. Hence $\gamma$ is global and $\alpha_H:=\alpha-s\sigma-\bar\partial_F\gamma$ annihilates vertical tangent, proving the asserted decomposition. The harmonic/exact orthogonality and the same zero kernel prove its uniqueness.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F4] Both Dolbeault groups of $\mathcal O(-1)$ vanish. [[lem-qftx-coupled-penrose-fibre-dolbeault]]

proof_steps.claim: For the global metric splitting, the mixed component of $\bar\partial(s\sigma)$ is a vertical degree-one form with coefficient $\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}\otimes E_x$. On a fibre it has a unique vertical primitive by [F4]. The fixed-fibre $B=\bar\partial^*G$ construction and smooth-parameter difference-quotient argument in [F2], with the estimates [F5], make that primitive smooth over the base. The same fibrewise uniqueness makes it agree across frame and chart changes. Denote the horizontal correction by $\phi(s)$; then $\psi(s)=s\sigma+\phi(s)$ has zero mixed differential. If $s$ is the image of a closed representative $\alpha$, [F2]'s decomposition and closedness say that its horizontal remainder solves this same mixed equation. The difference is fibrewise holomorphic in $\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}\otimes E_x$, hence zero by [F4]. Thus $\psi(s)=\alpha-\bar\partial_F\gamma$ is closed for a class image. The differential can still have a horizontal degree-two component for arbitrary $s$; the curvature component of the metric splitting is retained.

These local forms are regular on the complete projective fibre. For $w=1/t$, the horizontal vectors are $\widetilde H_i=wH_i$, $\widetilde\theta^i=w^{-1}\theta^i$, and $\widetilde e=w^2e$. Thus the new horizontal coefficients are $\widetilde h_i=t h_i$. They become $c(D_{\bar1}u+\bar wD_2u)/(1+|w|^2)$ and $c(D_{\bar2}u-\bar wD_1u)/(1+|w|^2)$, both smooth. The vertical coefficient changes to $-c u\,d\bar w/(1+|w|^2)^2$ in frame $\widetilde e$, also smooth. The sign is the canonical-coordinate transition, not a change of harmonic normalization. Therefore $\psi_{\mathrm{loc}}$ exists over every entire fibre above this base chart. Its difference from the intrinsic form of step 1.1 has zero vertical part and zero mixed differential. By [F4] that difference is zero. This proves that the coordinate calculation computes the actual global correction, despite using a different horizontal splitting for its displayed coefficients.

The local expression equals the intrinsically constructed differential by step 3.1. The same construction and calculation apply in any stereographic chart with the unit round metric. Thus it patches smoothly across the base overlap and infinity; a chartwise solution satisfies the invariant operator equation globally. For the class image $s$, the residual vanishes by step 1.1, and the nonzero frame in step 5.1 gives $(\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+2)s=0$. Gauge changes preserve the fibre normalization and transport the unique mixed correction, while $D_\mu$ and the final operator conjugate by the same unitary frame change. On the dual, $F_{A^\vee}=-F_A^{\mathsf T}$ remains ASD; the identical construction applies. More generally a connection-preserving smooth bundle map commutes with the componentwise vertical projection and inverse, and transports the unique mixed correction; thus the edge and residual construction are natural for such maps, including direct sums. Nothing used irreducibility, absence of parallel sections or nonzero curvature.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] The character line $L_\chi$, its Chern class $u_\chi$, the Borel cap action on equivariant Borel–Moore homology, and the multiplicative set $S_T$ are defined by the localized Borel–Moore data. [[def-qftx-localized-equivariant-borel-moore-data]]

proof_steps.claim: The set $D(f)$ is $T$-invariant because $f(t\cdot x)=\chi(t)f(x)$. On its Borel construction, define $s([e,x])=[e,f(x)]$ in the associated character line. This is well-defined: replacing $(e,x)$ by $(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$ replaces $f(x)$ by $f(t^{-1}\cdot x)=\chi(t)^{-1}f(x)$, exactly the right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$. Since $f$ never vanishes on $D(f)$, $s$ is a nowhere-zero section and trivializes that line bundle. The same formula trivializes its restriction to every $T$-invariant open $V\subseteq D(f)$.

On each finite Borel approximation, the first Chern class of the trivialized line is zero. By [F2] this is the Euler class of the line, and by [F3] its cap action on the approximating Borel–Moore groups is zero. The stable comparison in [F1] therefore gives $u_\chi\cap\beta=0$ for every $\beta\in H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(D(f);\mathbb Q)$, and the identical argument holds on $V$.

proof_steps.claim: A fiber kernel of $\alpha$ over $[1:u_1:u_2]$ is a nonzero vector $v$ with $B_1v=u_1v$, $B_2v=u_2v$, and $Jv=0$. The remaining coefficients of the two linear maps are their $z_0$ coefficients, so write $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0C_1+z_2,z_0C_2-z_1,z_0I)$. If $q$ had a continuous section, its restriction to this open subset would take each irreducible orbit to a point in that same orbit, hence into $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)$. For the smooth-space clause, fix now a smooth irreducible center $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and use the Banach slice and trivialization established in step 4.1.
