proof_steps.claim:
In the algebraic Chow ring, [F1] and $H=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ give
$$
\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)=(2k+N)-ke^{-H}-ke^H=N-kH^2,
$$
because $H^4=0$ on the complex threefold and the odd powers cancel. Thus $c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal F)=0$ and $c_2^{\rm alg}(\mathcal F)=kH^2$. In the underlying topological category the same exact sequences are exact sequences of complex vector bundles, so [F5] and the line-class identity $c_1(\mathcal O(1))=H$ give
$$
c(\mathcal F)=\frac{1}{(1-H)^k(1+H)^k}=(1-H^2)^{-k}=1+kH^2
$$
through degree six, since $H^4=0$. Hence the topological classes are $c_1(\mathcal F)=0$, $c_2(\mathcal F)=kH^2$, and $c_3(\mathcal F)=0$. The universal formulas $\operatorname{ch}_1=c_1$, $\operatorname{ch}_2=\tfrac12(c_1^2-2c_2)$, and $\operatorname{ch}_3=\tfrac16(c_1^3-3c_1c_2+3c_3)$ then give the topological $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)=N-kH^2$. This compares only the identical finite line-bundle resolution and its line class, not arbitrary analytic and algebraic cohomology.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F6] The algebraic first Chern class of $\mathcal O(1)$ is the hyperplane divisor class; its cycle class is the Poincaré dual of the complex hyperplane, which is the Euler class of its complex normal line. Thus its cycle class is $H_{\rm top}$. [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]], [[lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold]]

proof_steps.claim: A fiber $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)$ is a complex linear $\mathbb P^1\subset\mathbb P^3$. Its real codimension in $\mathbb P^3$ is $4$ and its real dimension is $2$, so the sign in [F3] is $(-1)^{4\cdot2}=+1$. Therefore $\pi^*u$ is Poincaré dual to $[L_x]$. The restriction of $\mathcal O(1)$ to this linear $\mathbb P^1$ has first Chern number $1$; [F2] then identifies its Poincaré dual as $H_{\rm top}^2$. Thus $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] The exact rank-two theorem supplies the ordinary framed ASD connection of a regular rank-two datum by its raw forward monad/projection construction, extends it smoothly over infinity, and proves $q_2=-k$. Its exact GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form hypotheses are retained in the rank-one raw emptiness deduction. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]]

proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition.

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A2] For $N\ge2$, the zero-FI correspondence supplier identifies the stable-and-costable real quotient with the framed ordinary ASD sector having $q_N=-k$, preserving the specified orientation, unitary framing, compact torus action and exact first-order family qualifications. For $N=1$, the rank-one boundary lemma proves that both ordinary spaces are empty at $k>0$ and are the framed flat point at $k=0$, with compatible compact actions and an explicit first-order groupoid equivalence. Its stabilization proof retains the rank-two supplier's actual GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form prerequisites; it introduces no extra rank-one dictionary premise. The two suppliers therefore cover the ordinary dictionary for every $N\ge1$ under exactly those inherited hypotheses. Neither identifies the positive-FI resolution or its rank-one formal coefficients with ordinary ASD moduli. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]], [[lem-qftx-rank-one-regular-adhm-and-ordinary-asd-boundary]]

proof_steps.claim: For $N\ge2$, the source and target of [A2]'s rank-two-and-higher supplier agree with the zero-FI regular quotient and the framed ASD sector in the conditional dictionary, with $q_N=-k$ and identical framing and orientation. For $N=1$, stabilize by adding one unused framed line as in the boundary lemma: its moment equations, word stability and costability are unchanged. Its proved boundary identifies the two empty spaces at $k>0$ and the unique framed flat points at $k=0$, and its direct first-order gauge argument supplies the corresponding family identification rather than inferring it from an orbit-set bijection. Thus the ordinary dictionary has no uncovered rank-one case; its exact rank-two analytic and normal-form hypotheses remain inherited. This does not place any positive-FI partition fixed point in the open regular ordinary locus. In particular, the positive-FI one-box rank-one contribution is still the formal coefficient of step 1.1 and is not an ordinary positive-charge abelian instanton.

For $k>0$, use the tuple $Y_1=\{(i,0):0\leq i<k\}$ and $Y_\alpha=\varnothing$ for $\alpha>1$; step 1.1 constructs a stable datum. Replacing $B_1$ by $B_1+c\,\mathrm{id}_V$ preserves the complex equation and stability while changing $\operatorname{tr}(B_1)$ by $kc$ for every $c\in\mathbb C$. Trace is invariant under conjugation, so the descended trace function on the geometric quotient has image $\mathbb C$, which is not compact. Thus the quotient is noncompact. The completed Borel carrier matches the compact real-Borel interface in [L1]. The ADHM/monad comparisons in [A1]–[A2] retain their exact analytic and family hypotheses, while step 2.3 has supplied the precise intrinsic localized Borel–Moore pushforward covered by [F6].

fact_uses.text: [F3] [[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] supplies the cornerwise isomorphisms $\Phi^r_{ij}$ through the adjunction chain $\operatorname{Hom}_E(f_{i!}k_i,f_{j!}k_j[t])=\operatorname{Hom}_{X_i}(k_i,f_i^!f_{j!}k_j[t]) =\operatorname{Hom}_{Z_{ij}}(k_{Z},q^!k_j[t])$ with $t=r+d_j-d_i$, their naturality in constructible coefficient morphisms, and their compatibility with stabilization.

proof_steps.claim: Typed correspondences. Put $t=r+d_j-d_i$ and $w=s+d_k-d_j$. Under the chain of [F3] the maps $\alpha$ and $\beta$ correspond to kernel forms $\kappa:k_A\to q^!k_j[t]$ and $\lambda:k_B\to v^!k_k[w]$, equivalently to cohomological correspondences $U:q_!k_A\to k_j[t]$ and $V:v_!k_B\to k_k[w]$; here $k_j=k_{X_j}$ and $k_k=k_{X_k}$. The middle square $(a,b;q,u)$ is Cartesian with $qa=ub$, and the three-factor identities $pa=\ell h$, $vb=mh$ hold by construction of the triple fiber product.

Geometric interpretation of the mate. Put $S=A\times B$, $F=(q,u):S\to X_j\times X_j$, and $\theta:T\hookrightarrow S$. By [F1] the pulled-back positive purity counit is $g_F:\theta_*k_T[-2d_j]\to k_S$. The external dualizing class corresponding to $\kappa\boxtimes\lambda$ has degree $n+n'$, where $n=d_i+d_j-r$ and $n'=d_j+d_k-s$ by [F3]; composing it with $g_F$ and taking the adjoint under $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$ gives a class of degree $n+n'-2d_j$ on $T$. The graph-factorization and composition-of-counits comparison proved in [F1] identifies this supported cap map with the mate in step 2.1, followed by $b^!\lambda[t]$. Thus its representative is exactly the adjoint of $W$. The purity counit, its pullback, and the mate are fixed global morphisms; the positive normal-ball generator fixes their orientation, while their equality on arbitrary supports follows from that supported adjunction comparison.

The composition square commutes. The inverse of the chain of [F3] sends $U$ to $f_{i!}k_i\xrightarrow{f_{i!}\eta_p}f_{i!}p_*k_A=f_{j!}q_!k_A\xrightarrow{f_{j!}U}f_{j!}k_j[t]$ and $V$ to the analogous map built from $u,v$, where $\eta_p:k_i\to p_*p^*k_i=p_*k_A$ is the adjunction unit and $f_{j!}=f_{j*}$. In the composite of these two maps, naturality of $\eta_u:\operatorname{id}\to u_*u^*$ moves $f_{j!}U$ past the second unit, and proper base change $u^*q_!\cong b_!a^*$ identifies the resulting two units with the unit $\eta_{pa}:k_i\to(pa)_*k_T$; the Beck–Chevalley unit identity is the transpose of the triangle equations under $f_{i!}\dashv f_i^!$ and $(vb)_!\dashv(vb)^!$, so both routes give the same morphism $f_{i!}k_i\xrightarrow{f_{i!}\eta_{pa}}f_{k!}(vb)_!k_T\xrightarrow{f_{k!}W}f_{k!}k_k[t+w]$. Applying the inverse map to $U_C$ gives the same expression, because $pa=\ell h$ and the composed-unit formula $\eta_{\ell h}=\ell_*\eta_h\ell^*\circ\eta_\ell$ follows from the same triangle equations. Hence the product square commutes for arbitrary cohomological correspondences, before orientation or grading is applied; this is the compatibility of products asserted in the Statement.

Units and the algebra statement. Let $\delta:X_i\to Z_{ii}$ be the diagonal, with $p\delta=q\delta=\operatorname{id}_{X_i}$. The cohomological correspondence for its fundamental class is $U_\delta:q_!k_{Z_{ii}}\to q_!\delta_*k_{X_i}=k_{X_i}$, induced by restriction $k_{Z_{ii}}\to\delta_*k_{X_i}$. Its inverse image under the chain [F3] is $f_{i!}k_{X_i}\to f_{i!}p_*k_{Z_{ii}}\to f_{i!}k_{X_i}$; restriction of the first unit to $\delta$ is the identity, so this composite is the identity. The adjoint kernel of $U_\delta$ is the proper trace of the positive fundamental class of $X_i$, since $\delta^!q^!k_{X_i}=k_{X_i}$. Hence $\Phi_{ii}^0(\operatorname{id}_{L_i})=\delta_*[X_i]=[\Delta_{X_i}]$, of corner degree zero. Step 5.1 transfers associativity and these units from shifted composition; the unit on the finite sum is $\sum_i[\Delta_{X_i}]$. The cornerwise bijections of [F3] therefore give the claimed unital graded algebra isomorphism, with nonmatching corners zero by [F2]. AC is inherited through [A1].

The polar decomposition $T\cong K\times(\mathbb R_{>0})^r$ makes $K\hookrightarrow T$ a homotopy equivalence. Choose one contractible free $T$-space $E$; it is also free for $K$, and $E/K\to E/T$ has contractible fiber $T/K$. The Borel fibrations $(E\times X)/K\to E/K$ and $(E\times X)/T\to E/T$ have common fiber $X$, with identity map on that fiber. Their homotopy exact sequences therefore make $(E\times X)/K\to(E\times X)/T$ a weak equivalence. Model independence of the universal free contractible space identifies this with the product right Milnor model and the algebraic-torus approximation in [F1].

The operations in the Definition are the proper pushforward, open restriction, and support maps of [F2]; the cap action is the action of Borel cohomology through $E_K\times_KX\to B_K$. These constructions respect the stable comparison of [F1].

proof_steps.claim: A two-tuple of partitions with total size one places its single box in exactly one of the two colors, so the only possibilities are $(\{(0,0)\},\varnothing)$ and $(\varnothing,\{(0,0)\})$. Their quotient representatives have $V$-characters $e_1$ and $e_2$, respectively.

Interchanging the two colors gives the second displayed character and $E_2$.

Each fixed-point contribution is the reciprocal of its Euler product, so the degree-one coefficient is $E_1^{-1}+E_2^{-1}$. The TikZ drawing only records the two one-box colorings and is not used in this calculation.

$q(I)$. These charts cover the circle. If two charts overlap, local lifts
differ by an integer; this integer is locally constant, so each transition
map is locally a translation and hence smooth. The charts therefore define a
smooth one-manifold without boundary compatible with the quotient topology.

Addition and inversion on one factor are smooth in these charts. Near any
pair of points, choose local real lifts $x,y$ and an output chart around their
sum; after shrinking the input intervals, the coordinate expression for
addition is $x+y$ plus one fixed integer. Near any point, choose local lifts
for it and its inverse; the coordinate expression for inversion is $-x$ plus
one fixed integer. Both expressions are smooth. With the group law already
given by [F2], this is a Lie group by [F6]. Its underlying circle is compact,
Hausdorff and connected by [F2] and [F3], and it is abelian by the quotient
addition law.

The circle has a finite CW structure with one vertex $[0]$ and one open
$1$-cell, the image of $(0,1)$; its characteristic interval has both
endpoints attached to that vertex. For $T$, index product cells by subsets
$J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$: coordinates in $J$ lie in the open $1$-cell and
all other coordinates equal $[0]$. Each cell is an open cube of dimension
$|J|$, its closure meets only cells indexed by subsets of $J$, and its
characteristic cube is the product of the factor characteristic intervals;
identify each closed cube with a closed disk of the same dimension. The map
$q^r:[0,1]^r\to T$ is a continuous surjection because every coordinate class
has a representative in $[0,1]$ by [F2]. If $K$ is closed in the cube,
then $K$ is compact, $q^r(K)$ is compact, and $q^r(K)$ is closed because $T$
is Hausdorff by [F2] and [F3]. Thus $q^r$ is a quotient map. It is the
characteristic map for the top cell. Every lower-cell characteristic cube is
obtained by precomposing $q^r$ with the continuous coordinate insertion that
fixes omitted coordinates at $0$, so the quotient topology of $q^r$ already
makes every characteristic map continuous; conversely $q^r$ is itself one of
those maps. Hence this quotient topology is exactly the weak topology
determined by the finitely many characteristic cubes. This gives a finite CW
structure with the identity as a $0$-cell. The singleton
identity is a subcomplex, so [F7] gives the homotopy extension property for
its inclusion.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F18] The fixed product torus is a compact connected abelian Lie group, and each period-one basis vector exponentiates to its coordinate circle subgroup as specified in the local torus definition. [[def-standard-product-torus-as-a-compact-lie-group]]

proof_steps.claim: Pullback naturality [F13] shows that $d$ preserves the $T$-fixed forms. Put $\phi_s=a_{\exp(-s e_i)}$. The local torus definition [F18] identifies $\exp(-s e_i)$ with the coordinate one-parameter subgroup, so the group law gives $\phi_{s+h}=\phi_s\circ\phi_h$. Differentiating at $h=0$ gives $\frac{d}{ds}\phi_s(p)=(d\phi_s)_pX_{e_i}(p)=X_{e_i}(\phi_s(p))$ by step 1.4. Thus $\phi_s$ is the flow of $X_{e_i}$. final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-abbv-equivariant-integration-conventions]]: equivariant integration is real Borel fiber integration, a character of weight $m$ has Euler class $m u$, and the product orientation fixes the component-integration signs.

proof_steps.claim: The first-factor action fixes exactly $p_0=[1:0]$ and $p_\infty=[0:1]$, while it fixes every point of the second factor. Thus $M^T=F_0\sqcup F_\infty$, with each component a copy of $\mathbb{CP}^1$. The normal bundle is the tangent line of the first factor at its fixed point; in the coordinates $z_1/z_0$ and $z_0/z_1$ its weights are $+1$ on $F_0$ and $-1$ on $F_\infty$.

The normal complex line is the first factor and the fixed-component tangent space is the second. Moving the real two-dimensional first-factor orientation past the real two-dimensional second-factor orientation has sign $(-1)^{2\cdot2}=+1$, so the induced component orientations agree with the product orientations.

The dual tautological fiber at $p_0$ has weight $0$ and at $p_\infty$ has weight $-1$, so the first-factor class restricts to $0$ and $-u$. Thus the contribution from $F_0$ is $0/u=0$; on $F_\infty$, the restricted class is $(-u)\eta$ and the normal Euler class is $-u$, leaving $\eta$, whose integral is $1$. The fixed-component sum is therefore $1$.

Product fiber integration factors over the two compact oriented factors. On the first $\mathbb{CP}^1$, the section of $\mathcal O(1)$ induced by $\ell(z_0,z_1)=z_0$ has one positive transverse zero at $p_\infty$, so its Euler integral is $1$ by the normalized Thom-class zero count; the second-factor integral of $\eta$ is $1$ by definition. Hence $\int_M\alpha=1\cdot1=1$, agreeing with step 3.1.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-abbv-equivariant-integration-conventions]]: a character of weight $m$ has equivariant Euler class $m u$ in real Borel cohomology; equivariant integration uses the complex orientation.

proof_steps.claim: A point $[z_0:z_1]$ is fixed by every $\lambda$ precisely when it lies on one coordinate axis, so the fixed set is $\{p_0,p_\infty\}$. In the coordinate $w=z_1/z_0$ near $p_0$, the action is $w\mapsto\lambda w$, giving tangent weight $+1$; in $v=z_0/z_1$ near $p_\infty$, it is $v\mapsto\lambda^{-1}v$, giving weight $-1$. The complex orientations agree with $M$, so the Euler denominators are $u$ and $-u$.

The tautological fiber at $p_0$ is the trivial coordinate line, and at $p_\infty$ it is the weight-$+1$ coordinate line. Dualizing gives the fixed-fiber weights $0$ and $-1$ for $\mathcal O(1)$, hence $x|_{p_0}=0$ and $x|_{p_\infty}=-u$.

The linear functional $\ell(z_0,z_1)=z_0$ defines a section of $\mathcal O(1)$ that vanishes only at $p_\infty$. In the local coordinate $v=z_0/z_1$ and the dual tautological frame there, its coefficient is $v$, so its unique zero is transverse with positive local degree $+1$. Pulling the normalized Thom class back by a transverse section counts its isolated zeros with these local degrees: excision reduces the pairing to the degree of the section on the boundary of a small disk around each zero. Hence the ordinary Euler number is $1$. Restricting the Borel pushforward to the basepoint of connected $BT$ gives this ordinary Euler number, and $H^0(BT;\mathbb R)=\mathbb R$; therefore $\int_{\mathbb{CP}^1}x=1$, independently confirming the localized sum.

proof_steps.claim: For each nonzero mode choose its least $j\notin N(m)$. If $j\in I$, then $h_m\delta c$ vanishes and the only nonzero term in $\delta h_mc$ deletes $j$; its two signs agree and give $+c_I$. Terms deleting a vertex of $N(m)$ vanish because the resulting index does not contain $N(m)$. Therefore $\delta h_m+h_m\delta=\mathrm{id}$ in every degree for all six possible $N(m)$.

The modewise formula defines a homotopy on actual holomorphic cochains: by [F3], each output component is a sum of subseries grouped by at most the three choices of $j\notin I$, each retained mode has no negative exponent at the added coordinate, and the subseries converge locally uniformly on $U_I$. Consequently their sums are holomorphic on $U_I$, including across the added coordinate hyperplane, and the coefficient identity in step 2.1 is an identity of analytic cochains.

Every nonzero mode is contractible by steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1, while the zero mode has the cohomology computed in step 2.2. The unique normally convergent coefficient expansions and their cochain homotopies make this coefficientwise computation valid for holomorphic sections, and [F3] identifies the resulting fixed-cover Čech cohomology with analytic sheaf cohomology. Hence the displayed sheaf-cohomology values follow.

proof_steps.claim: A global section restricts to every singleton chart $U_i$. Its coefficient mode $m$ must therefore occur on every $U_i$, so [F4] requires $N(m)\subseteq\{i\}$ for all $i$. Since $r\ge1$, there are at least two distinct singleton charts, whose intersection as index sets is empty; hence $N(m)=\varnothing$ and every $m_i\ge0$. For total degree $-1$, the equation $\sum_i m_i=-1$ is then impossible. Thus the degree-zero Čech cocycles for $\mathcal O(-1)$ are zero, and the fixed-cover comparison in [F4] gives $H^0(X,\mathcal O(-1))=0$.

The top Čech cochains have the single index set $J=\{0,\ldots,r\}$. A degree-$k$ mode appears there with no restriction beyond $N(m)\subseteq J$. It is a top coboundary exactly when its negative set is contained in at least one codimension-one face $J\setminus\{j\}$, equivalently when $N(m)\ne J$: one implication follows because the input cochain on that face has no coefficient unless $N(m)\subseteq J\setminus\{j\}$; conversely, if $N(m)\ne J$, choose $j\in J\setminus N(m)$ and the contraction of [F4] supplies a preimage in that face. Therefore top cohomology has exactly the modes with $N(m)=J$.

For $k=-r-1$, if every $m_i<0$, write $m_i=-1-n_i$ with integers $n_i\ge0$. The total-degree equation becomes $-(r+1)-\sum_i n_i=-(r+1)$, so $\sum_i n_i=0$ and every $n_i=0$. Thus the only surviving mode is $m=(-1,\ldots,-1)$, and its coefficient space is $\mathbb C$. The normal convergence and analytic cochain contraction in [F4] show that this coefficient quotient is the actual analytic Čech quotient. The comparison in [F4] now gives $H^r(X,\mathcal O(-r-1))\cong\mathbb C$.

For a parameter derivative, the matrix exponential satisfies $\partial e^{-p}=-\int_0^1e^{-(1-s)p}(\partial p)e^{-sp}\,ds$, obtained by differentiating the matrix ODE defining the exponential. Iterating this identity and differentiating in $\xi$ expresses every derivative in $y,\xi$ as finitely many simplex integrals of products of polynomial derivatives of $p$ and exponential factors whose time lengths sum to one. Since $p\ge c'|\xi|^2I$ uniformly on the chart closure, the product norm is at most a polynomial in $|\xi|$ times $e^{-c'|\xi|^2}$. Thus $e^{-p(y,\cdot)}$ is a uniformly bounded smooth Schwartz family. By [F1] its inverse transform $k_y(w)$ has all uniformly bounded Schwartz seminorms, and $\int k_y(w)\,dw=e^{-p(y,0)}=I$. This uses Fourier inversion on Schwartz functions, not an exchange of an undamped double Fourier integral.

Let $\kappa_i$ be finitely many charts with smooth unitary frames, and let $\phi_i$ be a partition subordinate to compact subsets of those charts. In each summand the principal coefficients are frozen at the source $z$. Step 1.1, local equivalence of chart distance and $d$, and cutoff support give $\|Z_t(y,z)\|\le C_LH_{t,L}(y,z)$, where $H_{t,L}=t^{-n/2}(1+d(y,z)/\sqrt t)^{-L}$. For $R_t=(\partial_t+P_y)Z_t$, the frozen principal part cancels $\partial_t$. The remaining principal term contains $A(y)-A(z)=O(d(y,z))$ and two derivatives of the frozen kernel; lower terms contain at most one derivative. The bound $d(y,z)t^{-1}H_{t,L+1}\le t^{-1/2}H_{t,L}$ therefore gives $\|R_t(y,z)\|\le C_Lt^{-1/2}H_{t,L}(y,z)$. Fix $x$ and put $y=\exp_x(\sqrt t\,a)$, $z=\exp_x(\sqrt t\,b)$. For each such derivative, the fixed-point equation and [F1] gain one $w$ derivative; induction gives all mixed $C^{m,\alpha}_w$ derivatives on the same radius, because only the inverse in the initial $C^\alpha$ space needs smallness. Thus $g$ is jointly smooth. If $A_j$ is holomorphic in an untouched coordinate, $K$ has zero antiholomorphic parameter derivative by [F2], and differentiating the inverse identity gives the same for $g$.

Gauge by this $g$ on the smaller disk. The transformed coefficient is $A_i'=g^{-1}(\partial_{\bar z_i}g+A_i g)$, and $A_j'=0$. The product of the resulting smooth invertible gauges has all transformed coefficients zero, proving the required local frame.

If $G$ and $H$ are two such frames, $D''G=D''H=0$ gives $\bar\partial(G^{-1}H)=0$. For smooth scalar functions this implies holomorphy: the one-variable Cauchy formula applies with the other variables fixed, and its iterated integral on a product of small circles gives a locally convergent joint power series. proof_steps.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient.

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition.

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step.

Under independent gauge transformations $h,h'$ of the incoming and outgoing slices, change temporal-link variables by $\eta_x\mapsto h_x\eta_x(h'_x)^{-1}$. Each such coordinate map also preserves Haar factors by [F1], and thus preserves $d\mu_V$ by [F6]. Substitution in $Q_{x,i}=\eta_xU'_{x,i}\eta_{x+\hat i}^{-1}U_{x,i}^{-1}$ cancels the neighboring $h'$ matrices and gives $Q_{x,i}\mapsto h_xQ_{x,i}h_x^{-1}$; each spatial plaquette is likewise conjugated at its base vertex. Trace invariance therefore preserves $S_t,S_s$, and the temporal integration gives $K(h'\cdot u',h\cdot u)=K(u',u)$ for every pair $(h',h)$. In particular, setting $h=1$ gives $K(h'\cdot u',u)=K(u',u)$. The integral representation in [F5], applied almost everywhere, then gives $(T\psi)(h'\cdot u')=(T\psi)(u')$ almost everywhere for each fixed $h'$, so $T\psi\in\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$. The constant function has norm one because $d\mu_s$ is a probability and is fixed by every gauge transformation, so it is a nonzero physical vector.

Each $\mathcal U(h)$ is unitary by measure preservation from step 4.1; the Hilbert structure follows from [F5] under full AC [A1]. Its fixed space is the kernel of the bounded operator $\mathcal U(h)-I$, hence is closed; the intersection over all $h$ is $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$, so $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$ is closed.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F7] [[thm-global-schauder-regularity-for-the-weak-dirichlet-laplacian]]: on a bounded $C^{2,\alpha}$ disk, a weak zero-Dirichlet solution of $-\Delta v=f$ with $f\in C^{0,\alpha}$ has a unique representative in $C^{2,\alpha}$.

proof_steps.claim: Set $G_R(v)=\kappa+L_Rv-\kappa A_Re^v$ and choose $L_R\ge\kappa\max_{\overline D_R}(A_Re^{\psi_R})$. For $v\le\psi_R$, $G_R'(v)=L_R-\kappa A_Re^v\ge0$, so the iteration map $T_R=(-\Delta+L_R)^{-1}G_R$ is order preserving. The subsolution inequality from step 2.1 gives $v_0\le T_Rv_0$ and the supersolution inequality from step 1.2 gives $T_R\psi_R\le\psi_R$, by positivity of the resolver in step 1.3. Thus $v_0\le v_1\le\cdots\le\psi_R$; every iterate after $v_0$ has zero Dirichlet trace. Each has a smooth representative: starting from smooth $v_0$ and $A_R$, rewrite its shifted resolvent equation as a Laplace equation, use boundedness and [F5] for $W^{2,p}$, then [F6]–[F7] and local bootstrapping; this also identifies continuous representatives up to the boundary. These representatives realize the order pointwise.

Since $v_0\le v_R\le\psi_R$ and $A_R$ is bounded on $\overline D_R$, the right-hand side in step 4.1 lies in $L^p(D_R)$ for every finite $p$. For a prescribed $0<\alpha<1$, choose $p>2/(1-\alpha)$. The disk is bounded and smooth, so [F5] gives $v_R\in W^{2,p}$; [F6] gives a $C^{1,\beta}$ representative with $\beta>\alpha$ and zero boundary values. The nonlinear right-hand side is then $C^{0,\alpha}$, and [F7] upgrades the weak solution to $C^{2,\alpha}(\overline D_R)$. Repeated local Schauder bootstrapping, using [F9], makes $v_R$ smooth in $D_R$. Setting $u_R=u_{s,R}+v_R$ proves its distributional equation and logarithmic center behavior.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [A1] Absolute projective GAGA on P³ supplies an exact tensor equivalence and cohomology comparison. [[thm-qftx-projective-gaga-for-monad-data]]

proof_steps.claim: Algebraize the holomorphic bundle using [A1]. Its algebraic sheaf is locally free: the holomorphic bundle is dualizable, the exact tensor equivalence transports its evaluation and coevaluation and reflects their triangle identities, and those identities give a finite dual basis on each local algebraic chart, hence a finite projective module. In a splitting C⁴=A⊕B into two-planes, a graph chart of G consists of X:A→B and the incidence is (X,[λ])↦[λ,Xλ], with p a product with P(A). In the library quotient convention it is the projective bundle of the dual of the tautological subbundle. Thus [F1] gives properness, finite presentation and flatness, and e*E is a coherent locally free sheaf flat over G.

At a real line L, absolute P³ GAGA applied to the coherent algebraic sheaf i*(E|L), for the closed immersion i:L→P³, identifies its cohomology with that of the trivial analytic restriction. This uses no GAGA on the Grassmannian: closed-immersion direct image is exact, and its analytification is the same local quotient-module tensor construction. Hence the algebraic fiber cohomology is C^N in degree zero and zero above by [F3]. Its degree-one base-change map has zero target, so is surjective. By [F2] that map is an isomorphism; the finite stalk of R¹p*e*E has zero residue fiber, and Nakayama kills it on a neighborhood. The degree-one local-freeness criterion of cohomology/base change now gives surjectivity in degree zero. Its degree-zero case makes H=p*e*E a finite locally free rank-N bundle with all degree-zero base-change maps isomorphisms near L.

Analytify this actual evaluation isomorphism. On every local product V×P¹, a holomorphic function is constant on each P¹ fiber by the maximum principle, and its remaining function on V is holomorphic by evaluation at a fixed point. Thus p_an*O=O. Trivializing H locally gives p_an*p_an*H_an=H_an, where the inner star denotes pullback and the outer star denotes direct image. Consequently the analytic direct image of e_an*E is H_an, its evaluation is the analytified evaluation, and all degree-zero analytic fiber maps are isomorphisms. The same product calculation after any base change identifies the base-change maps. No circular assumption of analytic base-change surjectivity or broad Grauert theorem is used.

The quaternionic involution on G sends a graph X to j_B X j_A^{-1}; its fixed graph matrices form the real four-dimensional quaternionic subspace, whose complexification is the entire graph space. These charts embed HP¹ smoothly and totally really into G. On its incidence family evaluation is a diffeomorphism onto Z: the inverse sends [v] to (span_C(v,jv),[v]), smoothly in projective charts, and j²=-1 excludes dependence of v,jv. Restrict H_an to this real locus to obtain the smooth rank-N bundle with the claimed fibers and evaluation. The positive pairing induces its Hermitian matrix by evaluating local section frames at a smoothly chosen point on each line; this proves smoothness and positivity, independently of parallelness. At infinity the given unitary frame induces the section-bundle frame. All arguments use only the stated local absolute comparison.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[def-qftx-localized-equivariant-borel-moore-data]]: the normalized fundamental class of a smooth complex dimension-$d$ variety has Borel–Moore degree $2d$, and equivariant cohomology classes act by cap product.

proof_steps.claim: Apply [F1] to this insertion. [[def-standard-product-torus-as-a-compact-lie-group]]

proof_steps.claim: By [F6] and the group isomorphism [F7], the Milnor theorem's well-pointed CW-type hypothesis holds for the circle model used in each factor. final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-aqft-heavy-chiral-u1-threshold-data]]: $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\delta_\alpha\theta=-\alpha$, $G=dB$ is invariant, and $M_H=|y|v>0$; the model adopts the mass-independent anomalous Jacobian as its threshold interpretation.

proof_steps.claim: From [F1], $G'=d(B+d\alpha)=G+d^2\alpha=G$, while $\delta_\alpha\theta=-\alpha$. Thus $G\wedge G$ is invariant under the specified small background transformations.

In Bilal's Hermitian convention [A1], $\mathscr A=-B$ and $\epsilon=-\alpha$. The linear evaluation $E^4_{0,\alpha}$ of [F3], with component rule $sB_\mu=\partial_\mu\eta$, gives the same infinitesimal four-form variation as [F1]; in Bilal's anti-Hermitian variables this is $-i\mathscr A=iB$ and $-i\epsilon=i\alpha$, matching the product-group charge-one connection. final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[def-aqft-threshold-matching-map]]: the realified matching family is jointly continuously differentiable in scale and coefficient coordinates on an open domain where both beta fields are defined; RG compatibility means $\partial_t\widehat M_t(x)+D_x\widehat M_t(x)\beta_+(t,x)=\beta_-(t,\widehat M_t(x))$. Its selected high- and low-energy amplitudes are matched with the same infrared regulator through the declared truncation.

proof_steps.claim: Let $x_+(t)=\Phi_+(t,t_i)x_i$ and set $y(t)=\widehat M_t(x_+(t))$. The chain rule and [A2] give $y'(t)=\partial_t\widehat M_t(x_+(t))+D_x\widehat M_t(x_+(t))\,\beta_+(t,x_+(t))=\beta_-(t,y(t))$ for every $t\in K$. Thus $y$ is a low-energy RG trajectory on the whole common interval.

Fix any $s\in K$. The low-energy trajectory obtained by matching at $s$ starts at $\widehat M_s(x_+(s))=y(s)$ and solves the low-energy RG equation. Since $y$ solves that same initial-value problem, [F3] implies that the two solutions agree on their common interval $K$. Therefore $x_-^{(s)}(t_f)=y(t_f)$, which does not depend on $s$.

At the fixed final scale, the selected amplitude or Green-function value is evaluated from the same low-energy coefficient vector $y(t_f)$ with the same external states, kinematics, regulator, and truncation [A3]. It is therefore identical for every matching scale $s$. Apply the matching equality in [F2] at scale $t_f$ to the high-energy coefficient $x_+(t_f)$ and its matched image $y(t_f)=\widehat M_{t_f}(x_+(t_f))$; the low-energy value equals the selected high-energy value through the retained orders.

For finitely many thresholds, apply steps 1.1–3.1 to the first matching map, then to each subsequent map in the ordered composition. Each compatible map transports its incoming trajectory to a solution of the next theory's RG equation, and uniqueness identifies that solution independently of the selected matching scale. Finite induction gives the same final coefficient vector and selected prediction for every compatible choice of intermediate scales.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[post-aqft-smeft-model]]: $H$ is a smooth complex doublet of hypercharge $Y=1/2$ (integer charge $y=3$), and its conjugate is $\widetilde H=i\sigma^2H^*$; the adopted field content, unit conventions and direct-product gauge action are fixed there.

proof_steps.claim: For $H=(a,b)^T\ne0$, let $\rho=(H^\dagger H)^{1/2}>0$. Direct multiplication gives $\Sigma=(i\sigma^2H^*,H)=\begin{psmallmatrix}b^*&a\\-a^*&b\end{psmallmatrix}$, so $\Sigma^\dagger\Sigma=(|a|^2+|b|^2)I=\rho^2I$ and $\det\Sigma=|a|^2+|b|^2=\rho^2$. Therefore $U=\Sigma/\rho$ is unitary with determinant one, hence lies in $SU(2)$, and $h=\sqrt2\rho-v>-v$ lies in $J$. The map $\Phi$ is smooth by scalar and matrix multiplication. Also $H^\dagger H$ is smooth and positive on $\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\}$, $s\mapsto\sqrt{s}$ is smooth on $(0,\infty)$, and division by $\rho>0$ is smooth, so the displayed inverse is smooth. Conversely, direct multiplication for an $SU(2)$ matrix gives $i\sigma^2U^*=Ui\sigma^2$ and $i\sigma^2e_2=e_1$, so $\Sigma(\Phi(h,U))=(v+h)U/\sqrt2$ and $\rho(\Phi(h,U))=(v+h)/\sqrt2$. These identities show that the two formulas compose to the identity in both directions. Thus $\Phi$ is a smooth diffeomorphism onto precisely the nonzero-doublet patch.

For $g_L\in SU(2)$, the defining two-dimensional representation obeys $i\sigma^2g_L^*=g_Li\sigma^2$; this follows by writing $g_L=\begin{psmallmatrix}a&b\\-b^*&a^*\end{psmallmatrix}$ and multiplying. Since $H\mapsto g_Lz^3H$, this identity gives $\widetilde H\mapsto g_Lz^{-3}\widetilde H$. Consequently $\Sigma\mapsto g_L\Sigma\operatorname{diag}(z^{-3},z^3)=g_L\Sigma g_R(z)^{-1}$. Unitarity preserves $\rho$, so $h$ is unchanged and $U=\Sigma/\rho$ has exactly the HEFT transformation law in [F2]. Hence $\Phi$ is equivariant.

The doublet derivative is $D_\mu H=\partial_\mu H+igW_\mu H+\tfrac{i}{2}g'B_\mu H$, because $Y(H)=1/2$. Applying the product rule to $H=(v+h)Ue_2/\sqrt2$ and using $T_3e_2=-e_2/2$ in the $D_\mu U$ formula of [F2] yields
$$D_\mu H=\frac1{\sqrt2}\left((\partial_\mu h)Ue_2+(v+h)D_\mu Ue_2\right).$$
The conjugate formula follows by complex conjugation. Repeated covariant derivatives expand into finite sums by the product rule, and field strengths remain the same curvature polynomials under this substitution. Thus every selected local polynomial representative has a finite HEFT expansion.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F4] [[def-aqft-threshold-matching-map]]: a finite-order matching map compares only selected high- and low-energy renormalized amplitudes or Green functions with the same infrared regulator, external data, and declared loop, operator, and mass truncations; this definition calculates no matching coefficient.

proof_steps.claim: The interpretation of the finite operator quotient as an on-shell amplitude basis inherits full AC through [A1], but the representative formula in step 3.1 is choice-free. By [F4], it supplies only the holomorphic coefficient component of a finite threshold map; it does not establish the selected amplitude equality, the low-energy matching of D-term or derivative coefficients, or any estimate for discarded orders.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F3] [[def-aqft-exact-background-rg-flow]]: the current local definition fixes the finite-regulator model and scale data, the background groupoid and exact symmetry action, the Wilsonian shell comparison, all retained infrared sectors, and the single-valued local functional $C$ relating the two background responses.

proof_steps.claim: Differentiate $W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}=C$ along an infinitesimal background gauge transformation in the identified local BRST complex. The local anomaly representatives then differ by $s\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}+d_Hq_3$ for the boundary-term convention $q_3$ fixed in [F1]. final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-aqft-susy-wilsonian-action]]: the Wilsonian action has a derivative-free holomorphic chiral integrand $F_\lambda(\Phi,W)$ and a separate real D-term; its finite operator quotient, ordered basis, cutoff, and field coordinates are supplied data.

proof_steps.claim: The selected finite invariant-quotient/on-shell-equivalence interpretation carries the full-AC premise [A1]. Separately, by [F2] and [A3], the complete derivative-free holomorphic chiral integrand satisfies $F_\lambda(\Phi,W)=F_{\Lambda_0}(\Phi,W)$ coefficientwise for every formal perturbative order. Setting $W=0$ and restricting to the fixed light-field variables preserves this identity, so $W_\lambda(\Phi)=W_{\Lambda_0}(\Phi)$.

The map $P_{\mathrm{hol}}$ is the same linear coordinate projection at both scales by [A2]. Applying it to the equality in step 1.1 gives $P_{\mathrm{hol}}W_\lambda=P_{\mathrm{hol}}W_{\Lambda_0}$. Since the retained operators are a fixed ordered basis, equality of their coordinate vectors gives equality of each retained coefficient.

The gauge-coupling correction and the freedom of the real D-term are exactly the exceptions in [F2]. The conclusion concerns the fixed Wilsonian holomorphic coordinates, so it does not imply equality of one-particle-irreducible vertices or of coefficients after a scale-dependent field rescaling; the formal perturbative hypothesis in [A3] also excludes nonperturbative and continuum conclusions.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F4] For a bounded $C^1$ domain and a $C^1$ vector field on its closure, the integral of the divergence equals the outward boundary flux; this theorem assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]

proof_steps.claim: On each closed ball $B_R$, $J$ is $C^1$, so [F4] and step 1.1 give $\int_{B_R}\sum_i\kappa(D_i\Phi,B_i)\,d^3x=\int_{S_R^2}\kappa(\Phi,B_i)\hat x_i\,dS$. Positive definiteness in [F2] gives $2|\kappa(D_i\Phi,B_i)|\le\kappa(D_i\Phi,D_i\Phi)+\kappa(B_i,B_i)$, so finite energy makes the cross term integrable. Taking $R\to\infty$ and using the declared surface limit yields $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_i\kappa(B_i,D_i\Phi)\,d^3x=m$.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F2] [[def-qftx-n1-vector-superfield]]: $V$ is a smooth even real matrix-valued superfield and $\mathcal W_\alpha$ is a chiral field-strength superfield.

proof_steps.claim: The superpotential is chiral: the chain rule gives $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}W_G(\Phi)=\sum_a(\partial W_G/\partial\Phi^a)\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi^a=0$. The vector field strength is chiral by [F2]. Therefore both $W_G(\Phi)$ and $\kappa_\mathbb C(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)$ are chiral even superfields.

For $X=\sum_a\bar\Phi^a e^{2gV_{R_a}}\Phi^a$, the finite Grassmann expansion has smooth coefficients, and the ordinary finite-dimensional matrix exponential is smooth in the body coefficients; hence step 1.1 applies. The odd-coordinate derivatives have no top Grassmann coefficient by [F4], so their D-term integrals vanish. The spacetime divergence integrates to zero under the compact-support or relative-action boundary condition in [A1]. The physical D bracket is the fixed multiple $-1/4$ of that raw integral, so every matter D-term is invariant.

final_edge_fact_uses.text: [F1] [[def-qftx-wilsonian-n1-action-data]]: the bare density contains the canonical matter kinetic term $\sum_i\Phi_i^\dagger e^{-V_i}\Phi_i$, an additional real gauge-invariant $G$, and the chiral term $\tau\operatorname{Tr}(W^\alpha W_\alpha)/(8\pi i)+F(\Phi,W)$; the selected cutoff prescription explicitly assumes a local background-spurion extension, a local derivative expansion and one-particle-irreducible vertex coefficients, without proving generic partial integration has these properties.

proof_steps.claim: By [F1], [F4], and [A2], the local Wilsonian density at every perturbative order has the same superspace and gauge-invariant decomposition into the fixed canonical matter kinetic term, an additional real D-term, a chiral F-term, and the separately displayed holomorphic gauge-kinetic term. The BRST differential used to state gauge invariance is well-defined and nilpotent by [F2] and [F3]; this is a premise about the local gauge algebra, not a proof of quantum anomaly cancellation.

Use the local background extension in [F1] and [A3], before specializing the external superfields to constant scalars. A derivative-free local chiral coefficient cannot depend on an unconstrained real background $P$: applying $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$ to such a coefficient gives its derivative with respect to $P$ times the independent odd background jet $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}P$, so chirality forces that derivative to vanish. Terms involving background superderivatives instead have a chiral projection and lie in the D-sector of the stated derivative expansion. The usual factorization $P=Z^\dagger Z e^{V_P}$ does not circumvent this argument. On a patch with positive scalar body, choose any invertible chiral external $Z$ and define the real $V_P=\log P-\log Z-\log Z^\dagger$ by its ordinary body logarithm and finite nilpotent expansion. This merely parametrizes the same external $P$; $Z$ and $V_P$ are not independent physical couplings. In particular $Z\mapsto e^{i\alpha}Z$ leaves $P$ and every regulated coefficient written in the original backgrounds unchanged, with all integrated fields held fixed. A holomorphic chiral coefficient independent of the unconstrained real $V_P$ cannot acquire nonconstant dependence on the dummy $Z$: for a holomorphic function $f$, invariance under every phase implies $Z\partial_Zf=0$. A field-independent quadratic gauge chiral term may change by the topological-angle total derivative; keep this separately in the displayed $\tau_\lambda$ gauge parameter. This is a statement about the local action modulo its stated boundary terms, not an assertion about a Jacobian from rescaling charged fields. Thus the original real D coefficients do not enter the derivative-free $F_\lambda$. Analyticity in [A3] extends the identity on the positive-body patch to the formal coefficient domain.

Consider a connected graph contributing to this chiral density, with $E_V$ external left-handed gaugino lines and $I_V$ internal vector lines. Let $A_m$ count pure-gauge vertices from the quadratic $W^\alpha W_\alpha$ term with $m\geq3$ vector lines; let $B_{mr}$ count vertices from an F-term containing $r$ field strengths and $m\geq r$ vector lines; and let $C_m$ count vertices from the fixed canonical matter kinetic term with two chiral lines and $m\geq1$ vector lines. Counting vector-line ends gives $2I_V+E_V=\sum_{m\geq3}mA_m+\sum_r\sum_{m\geq r}mB_{mr}+\sum_{m\geq1}mC_m$. The R-charge condition gives $\sum_r\sum_{m\geq r}(2-r)B_{mr}=2-E_V$. Each vector propagator contributes one factor $\tau^{-1}$ and each pure-gauge vertex one factor $\tau$, so $N_\tau=\sum_{m\geq3}A_m-I_V$; eliminating $E_V$ and $I_V$ yields $N_\tau=1-\tfrac12[\sum_{m\geq3}(m-2)A_m+\sum_r\sum_{m\geq r}(2-r+m)B_{mr}+\sum_{m\geq1}mC_m]$.

Every coefficient inside the square brackets is a positive integer. A graph contributing to the $\tau$-independent part $H_\lambda$ must have $N_\tau=0$, so the bracket equals two. The positive-integer solutions are two cubic or one quartic pure-gauge vertices, one $B_{mr}$ vertex with $m=r$, two $C_1$ vertices, one $C_2$ vertex, or the mixed case with one cubic gauge vertex and one $C_1$ vertex. For the $B_{mr}$ case, [step 4.1]'s R-charge equation gives $E_V=r=m$; the vector-end equation then gives $I_V=0$. It is the original single tree insertion. In the $A_3=2$ pure-gauge case the R-charge equation gives $E_V=2$ and the vector-end equation is $2I_V+2=6$, so $I_V=2$ and $L=2-2+1=1$. In the $A_4=1$ case it is $2I_V+2=4$, so $I_V=1$ and $L=1-1+1=1$. Both are one-particle-irreducible contributions to the gauge-kinetic term. For either matter-only case, the R-charge equation gives $E_V=2$ and the vector-end equation gives $2I_V+2=2$, so $I_V=0$. Each $C_m$ vertex contains one chiral and one antichiral matter line. A contribution to a holomorphic F-term cannot have an external antichiral line; with no other vertex type present, the two $C_1$ vertices therefore contract their two antichiral ends with their two chiral ends, giving $I_\Phi=2$, while the one $C_2$ vertex contracts its own chiral/antichiral pair, giving $I_\Phi=1$. Thus in each case the total internal-line count equals the vertex count and $L=1$; no matter line is external, so these graphs correct only the field-independent gauge-kinetic term. In the mixed case the end equation is $2I_V+2=3+1=4$, so $I_V=1$; the single $C_1$ vertex contracts its chiral/antichiral pair, giving $I_\Phi=1$. Hence $I=2$, $N_{\rm vert}=2$, and $L=1$. Its sole vector line is a bridge separating the gauge vertex from the matter vertex, so it is one-particle-reducible and excluded by the vertex convention in [F1]. Therefore the only tree contribution is the original $F$, every other allowed contribution is a one-loop gauge-kinetic correction that shifts the separately displayed $\tau_\lambda$, and no higher-loop correction is possible. A graph contributing to an additional $c_\lambda\tau W^2$ term would require $N_\tau=1$, hence a zero bracket and no vertices, which cannot form a graph with external fields; therefore $c_\lambda=0$.

For an unbroken U(1) factor, the prepotential shifts by $V_1\mapsto V_1-\Lambda_1-\bar\Lambda_1$. A constant coefficient $\xi$ multiplying $\int d^4x\,[V_1]_D$ is gauge invariant because the Berezin integral of the chiral and anti-chiral shifts vanishes under the boundary condition in [F1]. For a field-independent coefficient promoted to a real spurion $S$, the physical variation contains $-[P_{\mathrm{phys}}(S)\Lambda_1]_F$ and its Hermitian conjugate, where $P_{\mathrm{phys}}=-\tfrac12\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot2}}\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot1}}|_{\bar\theta=0}=+\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\alpha}\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$ at fixed chiral coordinates is the normalized D-to-F projector in [F1]; invariance for arbitrary chiral $\Lambda_1$ forces the spurion components relevant to this operator to be constant. In canonical exterior gauge write $q=\rho e^{in\theta}$ and $\alpha=A-n\,d\theta$. Directly, $D_Aq=e^{in\theta}(d\rho-i\rho\alpha)$, so the real and imaginary terms are orthogonal and $|D_Aq|^2=|d\rho|^2+\rho^2|\alpha|^2$. Apply step 3.1 first to $p_0$ and $p_*$, defining its finite energy to be $C_0$, and then to $p_*$ and $p_1$, defining its finite energy to be $C_1$. proof_steps.claim: Choose the fixed integer $k>r/2+1$. The smooth clause of [F3], applied with the configuration data [F2], makes $q_*$ a locally trivial principal $\overline{\mathcal G}^\infty(P)$-bundle. By [F4], its total space is nonempty, path connected, and has $\pi_j=0$ for every $j\ge1$, so it is weakly contractible in the sense used in [F6]. For a constant central gauge section $u=\zeta I_N$, the local action formula gives $A^u=A$ because $u^{-1}Au=A$ and $du=0$; hence reduced and full gauge groups have the same orbits on $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)$.

The locus $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)$ is gauge invariant: in the chosen frame, the based holonomy subgroup of $A^u$ is $u(p_m)^{-1}\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)u(p_m)$, so it has the same invariant subspaces up to conjugation. It is open: by [F2], the inclusion $\mathcal A^\infty(P)\hookrightarrow\mathcal A_k(P)$ is continuous, as each fixed $H^k$ norm is bounded by finitely many smooth derivative seminorms on the finite compact atlas. The smooth irreducible locus is the inverse image of the Sobolev irreducible locus, which is open by [F3]. The full orbit projection $q$ is open because, for any open $U\subseteq\mathcal A^\infty(P)$, its saturation $q^{-1}(q(U))=\bigcup_{u\in\mathcal G^\infty(P)}U\cdot u$ is open. For fixed smooth $u$, the map $A\mapsto u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$ is continuous in every finite-atlas derivative seminorm by the Leibniz rule; its inverse is the same formula for $u^{-1}$, so each gauge translate is a homeomorphism. Therefore $q(\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P))$ is open and $q|_{\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)}$ is an open quotient map onto this subset. The reduced and full actions have the same orbits there, so their quotient topologies identify the reduced orbit space homeomorphically with $q(\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P))$; this proves the claim about $\iota$ in the Statement. If $q$ had a continuous section, its restriction to this open subset would take each irreducible orbit to a point in that same orbit, hence into $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)$. Via the stated homeomorphism, this would give a continuous section of $q_*$, contradicting step 3.1. Thus $q$ has no continuous section.

proof_steps.claim: For the smooth-space clause, fix now a smooth irreducible center $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and use the Banach slice and trivialization established in step 4.1. Put $U_A=\Phi_A(S_{A,\varepsilon}\times\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1})$ and $V_A=\pi_k(S_{A,\varepsilon})$. Since $U_A$ is open in $\mathcal A_k^*$, $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open in the stated $C^\infty$ topology; set $S_A^\infty=S_{A,\varepsilon}\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$ and $V_A^\infty=\pi_\infty(S_A^\infty)$. For a smooth $B\in U_A$, its unique reduced gauge class from step 4.1 has a representative $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$. It satisfies $d_A^*(B^{u^{-1}}-A)=0$. Locally in a bundle frame, write $C_j=uB_j u^{-1}-(\partial_j u)u^{-1}-A_j$. Substitution in $d_A^*C=0$, use of $\partial_i(u^{-1})=-u^{-1}(\partial_i u)u^{-1}$, and multiplication on the right by $u$ isolate the equation $g^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j u=R(A,B,g;u,u^{-1},du)$ on each chart. Every term in $R$ is a finite product of smooth coefficients (including first derivatives of $A,B$) and factors among $u,u^{-1},du$; hence the principal operator is the scalar smooth Laplacian on each matrix entry. If $u\in H^{r+1}$ for $r\ge k$, then this right-hand side lies in $H^r$ by [F7] and the smooth coefficient bounds. Elliptic regularity [F6] gives $u\in H^{r+2}$. Iteration proves $u$ smooth; changing its representative by an element of the finite center preserves smoothness. Thus every smooth point of the Banach saturation has a smooth trivialization representative, and $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*=\pi_\infty^{-1}(V_A^\infty)$.

Suppose smooth $B_j\to B$ in $C^\infty$ within $U_A\cap\mathcal A_\infty^*$. The Banach trivialization from step 4.1 gives convergence of their slice representatives in $H^k$ and of their reduced gauge classes in $H^{k+1}$. In a quotient chart around the limiting class from step 1.1, choose lifts $u_j,u$ that converge in $H^{k+1}$; this is possible because the finite center acts by disjoint translates. The equation in step 5.2 and elliptic estimates [F6] bootstrap convergence: if $u_j\to u$ in $H^{r+1}$, then the assumed $C^\infty$ convergence gives $B_j\to B$ in $H^{r+1}$, and [F7] makes the right-hand sides converge in $H^r$. Induction gives convergence in every Sobolev order, which on compact $M$ is the $C^\infty$ section topology. The slice representatives converge in $C^\infty$ by their action formula. Conversely the forward action is continuous in the $C^\infty$ topology by multiplication and differentiation of smooth sections. The restricted map $S_A^\infty\times\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty\to\pi_\infty^{-1}(V_A^\infty)$ is therefore a homeomorphism for the actual quotient topology, and it is equivariant.
